title: Democrat Accuses Nvidia CEO Of Violating US Export Control Law
description: Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer and others say Congress must quickly pass legislation to crack down on US chip exports to China.
author: Reuters
content:
Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer on Tuesday accused Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang of violating federal law limiting exports of advanced technology to China.
Schumer said in a post on X that Huang "shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race."
A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race. This is an unfathomable failure of enforcement by the Trump administration. We urgently need to pass the bipartisan export control bills to start to cut off the flow of AI chips and manufacturing equipment to China once and for all, something I've worked on with @SenWarren and bipartisan partners for months.
— Chuck Schumer (@SenSchumer) November 24, 2026
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A rising number of lawmakers have criticized Nvidia for reinstating Huang as CEO and for President Donald Trump's role in pressuring the company to take the action.
Schumer and others say Congress must quickly pass legislation to crack down on US chip exports to China.
Republican Senator Kevin Cramer said Tuesday on CNBC that more guardrails were needed on US chips exports to China. "We might even have to put a babysitter on Jensen Huang," Cramer said, adding it would be "just make sure that he doesn't do something that is going to risk the United States."
Huang will testify on December 3 before the ‌US Senate Banking Committee in a public hearing, the panel's chair Tim Scott said Monday, as lawmakers probe allegations about Huang's ties to a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.
President Donald Trump on CNBC said he had pressed the Nvidia board to reinstate Huang and that he did not think the board would have done so without his action.
Huang separately is still expected to appear for a closed-door briefing on Dec. 1 with three House panels.
Republican Representative Pat Harrigan said Monday that for two years said privately "there is no way Jensen Huang can argue for the exportation of advanced American chips to China without being compromised. Turns out, well, we all know."
Harrigan added that Huang's "reinstatement today at this juncture is a mistake.... We sent a signal that one man's financial impact on our economy outweighs the importance of good governance, good citizenship, and adherence to the law. That is a dangerous precedent to set"

title: Former OpenAI Board Member Warns No 'Kill Switch' Will Help If AI Goes Rogue
description: Former OpenAI board member Helen Toner warns no single kill switch can stop rogue AI.
author: Abhinav Singh
content:
A former OpenAI board member has issued a sobering warning that there was no universal 'kill switch' or emergency shutdown mechanism if an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) model decided to go rogue. Speaking to Fox News, Helen Toner, executive director of Georgetown University's Centre for Security and Emerging Technology, addressed the challenges posed by growing cybersecurity threats.
"There's not gonna be a single kill switch that can fix all our problems, unfortunately," Toner warned. "There's definitely different layers of places where you can put in emergency overrides, emergency shutdowns that are going to be able to pull back from some types of challenges."
Toner explained that there were AI systems that were running on computing power over which people in the US might not have any control, making them harder to regulate.
"The way that AI works, it's possible to have AI systems that are running on computing power that you don't control, that, you know, humans are in charge of, that aren't subject to US jurisdiction, or that are running fully autonomously. So I think we need to be realistic about, uh, to what extent kill switches can fix our problems, which is, you know, maybe to some extent, but not completely," she said.
As for trusting China in the AI race, Toner said both the countries needed to work together to ensure that the technology does not harm the ordinary people.
"I think trusting China is not going to be the way we solve anything. But I also think we have to really avoid the situation where we say, look, U.S. companies are building this technology that they tell us is incredibly dangerous, we think is incredibly dangerous, but we have no choice, we have to go ahead with this incredibly risky activity because if we don't then China will do this incredibly risky thing," she said.
AI Causing Chernobyl-Like Event
Earlier this month, Geoffrey Hinton, regarded by many as the 'godfather of AI' warned of a Chernobyl-like event in the future where AI might trigger a temporary blackout of financial or power systems.
"Either later this year or next year we'll see Chernobyl, and that may be enough to make people really pay attention," said Hinton. "Can you imagine what would happen? We could recover from it [but] that would make them sit up and take notice."
The 78-year-old also called out the likes of Sam Altman and Elon Musk among other AI leaders who had been participating in the race to develop the next superior AI model that could corner the market share.
"I think [Mark] Zuckerberg and [Elon] Musk and Sam Altman, they understand the risks, and they don't give a sh*t. They'd rather have the money. That's my belief," said Hinton.
Hinton has previously warned that the technology could get out of hand if AI chatbots manage to develop their own language. He added that AI has already demonstrated that it can think terrible thoughts

title: Jensen Huang's Return To Nvidia Brings Open-Weight AI Debate To Fore In US
description: Nvidia's leadership crisis has thrust a tech industry squabble over openweight AI models into the spotlight, where CEO Jensen Huang has become one of
author: Reuters
content:
Nvidia's leadership crisis has thrust a tech industry squabble over open-weight AI models into the spotlight, where CEO Jensen Huang has become one of Washington's loudest voices for US development of a technology now dominated by Chinese companies.
Nvidia's board announced on Monday that it would reinstate Huang as CEO, following his resignation over reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman who news reports said was suspected of spying for the Chinese government.
Before the scandal erupted, Huang had pushed the US Congress and the Trump administration to support American companies developing open-weight AI models, which would align with his company's commercial interests, although a debate has raged over the models' implications for US national security.
President Donald Trump's administration supports open-weight AI systems because they give startups dependable and cheaper options outside proprietary AI tools from providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
"The Trump Administration's clear and long-standing policy has been strong support for" open-weight AI models, a White House official said in a statement to Reuters on Tuesday.
Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened in the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang in part because they viewed him as the protector of US-made open-weight AI models, people familiar with the matter said on Monday. The White House did not comment on the connection between the support for Huang and open-weight models.
Open-weight AI models, unlike closed models, make core components publicly available for users to download, modify and adapt for specific tasks. Such models broaden demand for Nvidia's chips and computing infrastructure beyond a handful of leading AI model developers, providing a business opportunity for Huang's company.
Executives from closed-model developers such as Anthropic and OpenAI have expressed skepticism of open-weight models, according to their public statements, creating a schism in the AI sector. Anthropic and OpenAI earn revenue by selling access to proprietary systems whose underlying technology they control.
"Any kind of political headwinds against Huang and Nvidia could be a harbinger for a crackdown on open weights, which is not good for little tech and companies that are trying to have a fighting chance of disrupting some of the incumbents," said Luther Lowe of Y Combinator, a Silicon Valley incubator and startup fund.
In a letter earlier this year, Huang urged the US government to avoid "premature restrictions" on open-weight tools. A coalition of companies co-signed the letter, including venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, Microsoft and Palantir. Anthropic declined to sign on.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said he disagreed with parts of Huang's statement, arguing that increasingly capable open-weight models could create security risks, including helping users to exploit publicly available information to develop biological weapons. In a statement, he said that "sufficiently capable" AI tools could use publicly available materials to spread infectious diseases.
US competitiveness with China is also a key aspect of the policy debate in Washington. Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Alibaba's offerings have won American business users because they are often cheaper than proprietary systems from OpenAI and Anthropic while performing comparably on many tasks.
The Trump administration has taken a few steps to support the US open-weight ecosystem, including public statements from White House tech adviser Michael Kratsios. The Trump administration over the summer told leading AI model developers that it would not put open-weight AI models through voluntary government safety tests, Reuters reported, a win for proponents such as Nvidia who do not want such models to face additional regulatory hurdles.
The administration is separately considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese-made AI models, including open-weight tools, Reuters reported last week.
Two Republican chairs of House committees involved in AI policy urged the Trump administration last week to go further, by barring US government agencies and contractors from using Chinese open-weight AI models. They want the government to give US companies developing open-weight models more access to computing resources, arguing that expanding the open-weight ecosystem in the US is a national security imperative in the AI race against China.
"The time to act is now, while we still have the opportunity and leverage to do so," House Homeland Security Committee chair Andrew Garbarino and China Committee chair John Moolenaar said in a joint statement.

title: India-UK Trade Deal: Why Is Bulk Scotch Whisky Facing A 162% Import Duty?
description: While bottled Scotch whisky gets the benefit of the lower duty, certain bulk imports are facing a much higher tax burden.
author: Prateek Shukla
content:
India's trade deal with the United Kingdom was expected to make Scotch whisky cheaper to import. The agreement, which came into force on July 15, 2026, cut the import duty on eligible Scotch whisky from 150 per cent to 75 per cent. The rate is also scheduled to fall further to 40 per cent over the next 10 years.
But just months after the deal took effect, the whisky industry has run into an unexpected hurdle.
Several shipments of bulk Scotch whisky have faced action by Indian customs authorities. The issue is not simply about the tax rate. It is about how the whisky is classified when it enters India.
Also Read | Layoffs Are Rising In Tech, But These Skills Are Helping People Unlock Better Pay
While bottled Scotch whisky gets the benefit of the lower duty, certain bulk imports are facing a much higher tax burden. In some cases, the effective duty has been estimated at 162.5 per cent.
The dispute has also attracted the attention of the UK government, raising questions about whether one of the key concessions in the India-UK trade agreement is working as intended.
On November 24, the Commerce Ministry asked the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) to release confiscated bulk Scotch shipments after following due process until a technical solution to the classification dispute is found.
What Did India Promise Under The UK Trade Deal?
India's import duty on Scotch whisky was earlier 150 per cent. Under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), the tariff on eligible Scotch whisky imports under the relevant tariff classification was reduced to 75 per cent when the agreement came into force.
The rate is scheduled to decline gradually to 40 per cent over the next decade.
The move was expected to improve access for British whisky makers to India's growing premium spirits market. It was also expected to give Indian importers more room to bring international brands into the country at a lower cost.
However, the tariff concessions depend on the customs classification of the imported product. And that is where the trouble begins.
Why Are Bottled And Bulk Scotch Whisky Treated Differently?
Not all Scotch whisky entering India arrives in the same form.
Some imports come in bottles, ready to be sold to consumers. Others arrive in large containers as bulk spirit. This whisky is subsequently diluted, blended or bottled in India before reaching retail shelves.
Customs authorities use different Harmonised System of Nomenclature (HSN) codes to classify imported products. Each code carries a specific rate of import duty.
Bottled Scotch whisky is covered under the relevant tariff lines of HS 220830, which receive the 75 per cent preferential rate under the trade agreement.
Bulk whisky, meanwhile, has historically been imported under different classifications, including HS 220890. Under the India-UK trade deal, this category has a different tariff concession, with the rate reduced to 110 per cent.
The current dispute has become more complicated because customs authorities have also sought to classify certain high-strength bulk whisky imports under HS 21069051. This category covers compound alcoholic preparations used in the manufacture of beverages.
Unlike the whisky-specific tariff lines, this newer classification does not receive the negotiated concession under the trade agreement. It attracts a basic customs duty of 150 per cent. A 5 per cent consumption levy can take the effective burden to 162.5 per cent.
Importers and customs authorities disagree over which classification should apply to these shipments.
Why Is The Industry Worried About The HSN Code Dispute?
For liquor companies, the difference between a 75 per cent and a 162.5 per cent import duty can significantly change the economics of doing business.
Bulk Scotch is not a marginal part of India's whisky trade. It is an important input for companies that blend, dilute and bottle whisky locally.
Mokksh Sani, Co-Founder of Cartel Bros and Founder of Living Liquidz, told NDTV that bulk imports account for up to 80 per cent of Scotch whisky imports into India.
"Under the UK-India Free Trade Agreement (FTA), the import duty on Scotch whisky has been reduced from 150 per cent to 75 per cent. However, this reduction is applicable only to Scotch whisky bottled in Scotland. Bulk Scotch whisky imports continue to attract a duty of approximately 162 per cent, creating a significant distinction in the duty structure between bottled and bulk imports," he said.
Sani said the difference in taxation could have wider implications for companies importing Scotch in bulk. It could affect sourcing economics, cost structures and the competitiveness of their product portfolios.
He also highlighted the importance of consistency in the implementation of the trade agreement. "India remains an important market for international spirits brands, with growing consumer interest in premium and globally recognised offerings. As the UK-India FTA creates opportunities for stronger bilateral trade, it is essential that its implementation provides greater consistency and clarity across different categories of Scotch whisky imports," Sani said.
A predictable regulatory framework, he added, would help businesses make informed commercial decisions while supporting the growth of India's premium spirits market.
Why Has The Government Stepped In?
The issue has been discussed between the Commerce Ministry and industry representatives.
On November 2, the Commerce Ministry assured the alcoholic beverages industry that the ambiguity surrounding HSN classification for bulk Scotch imports would be resolved amicably.
Following a meeting with industry associations, the ministry indicated that it would work with the Finance Ministry to find a solution within the framework of the law.
The government also reiterated that India's commitments under the UK trade agreement would be honoured, while ensuring that domestic industry interests were protected.
However, the dispute remained unresolved. On November 24, the Commerce Ministry asked the DRI to release confiscated bulk Scotch shipments after following due process while officials work on a technical solution.
Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said India had not withdrawn its commitments under the trade agreement. The government is examining how to reconcile the negotiated tariff concessions with existing court rulings and customs classifications.
The dispute has also reached the UK government, which has raised concerns over the treatment of bulk Scotch imports. The issue is particularly sensitive because the tariff concessions on Scotch whisky were an important part of the negotiations.
Will Scotch Whisky Become More Expensive For Indian Consumers?
The immediate concern is the cost of importing bulk Scotch whisky. However, the dispute could also have a bearing on Indian consumers if the higher tax burden is passed on through the supply chain.
Companies importing bulk whisky for local blending and bottling could face higher input costs. This may put pressure on the pricing of certain whisky brands and their ability to compete in the premium segment.
However, an immediate price increase across the Scotch whisky market cannot be assumed. The impact will depend on how the government resolves the classification dispute, whether importers can secure the negotiated tariff benefits and how companies absorb any additional costs.

title: Shein Agrees To $100 Million Settlement With US Consumer Watchdog
description: Shein was also accused of describing some products as made with US cotton when the cotton came from China.
author: Agence France Presse
content:
Chinese e-commerce giant Shein has agreed to pay $100 million to settle legal action brought by US authorities over service failures and misleading information, among other allegations.
The settlement, which has yet to be submitted to a federal judge in Los Angeles, provides for the money to be paid to affected consumers, according to a statement released Tuesday.
The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) filed its lawsuit and proposed the settlement on the same day.
Contacted by AFP, Shein stressed that the settlement "does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC's characterization of our business and compliance practices."
The consumer protection agency accused the platform of repeated delivery delays, undelivered orders and poor customer service, among other failings.
Shein did not provide a customer service phone number in the United States, although it now lists one.
When customers tried to contact the department, it rarely answered calls. It had just five staff members, even though Shein delivers nearly a million packages a day in the country.
The FTC also accused Shein of blocking negative reviews on its website.
According to the agency, the Chinese site also marketed items as being made by companies whose pledges not to use forced or child labor had been verified, even though no such checks had been carried out.
Shein was also accused of describing some products as made with US cotton when the cotton came from China.
Under the settlement, Shein has committed to providing more reliable delivery estimates, no longer blocking negative reviews and refraining from making false claims about products sold on its platform.
"Shein has continued to make significant investments in strengthening its consumer practices and compliance efforts," the company told AFP.

title: No Words, Just Smiles: Chinese Couple Run Restaurant Where Customers Order Without Speaking
description: Run by a couple with hearing impairments, the eatery also provides free meals to people in need and employs staff with similar disabilities.
author: Nikhil Pandey
content:
A Chinese couple are winning hearts with their unusual restaurant, where customers do not need to speak to place an order. Instead, they use hand gestures, point at the menu and share warm smiles. According to the South China Morning Post, the restaurant, called Chaoshan Deaf Sister, is located in Taiyuan, in China's Shanxi province. It specialises in steamed rice rolls and is run by Yin Ying and her husband, Feng Yabin, both of whom have hearing impairments.
The South China Morning Post reports that the couple have created a welcoming space where spoken communication is not necessary. Customers can use a Chinese sign language chart or simply point to the food they want. The restaurant also employs other people with hearing impairments, allowing them to work in a supportive environment.
The couple's kindness goes beyond serving food. They offer free meals to people who cannot afford to pay, including students with hearing impairments and sanitation workers. They aim to pass on the kindness they have received from others.
According to the South China Morning Post, the restaurant attracted widespread attention online after a social media influencer visited and said he had no money to pay for a meal. The couple not only gave him free food but also offered him the money they had at the counter.
The influencer was so touched by their generosity that he later shared their story online and created a portrait of the couple.
The restaurant has since become a symbol of kindness and inclusion, showing that a warm smile and a helping hand can sometimes say more than words.

title: India Among Nations On Team Trump's Hit List For New US Tariffs: Report
description: The USTR announcement will likely mean higher tariffs for the targeted countries and will likely cover most products exported from those nations.
author: Sanstuti Nath
content:
India is among dozens of nations that could soon face a new wave of tariffs from the United States, which President Donald Trump's administration argues are harming American companies by supporting their domestic industrial production, according to a Wall Street Journal report.
The proposed new duties are expected to target nations including China, India, Japan, South Korea, the European Union, and several other major economies. They follow a months-long tariff investigation by Team Trump, whose findings the US Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer is expected to unveil as soon as this week.
The US is set to announce the new levies as soon as Tuesday, according to a Bloomberg report.
So far, the White House and the USTR have commented on the reports.
The Framework of New Duties
The probe into the industrial subsidies of India, China, the European Union, and 13 other nations was opened on March 11, under Section 301 of the 1974 trade law, which allows the president to impose tariffs after finding unfair trade practices.
Greer has said those subsidies and other governmental support have created excess industrial capacity in the targeted economies, allowing their firms to flood global markets with cheaper goods, undermining US producers, the WSJ reported.
The USTR announcement will likely mean higher tariffs for the targeted countries and will likely cover most products exported from those nations. However, per the WSJ report, they will likely exclude some industrial goods like steel, aluminium, and automobiles that are tariffed under a separate national security authority.
The final tariff rates remain unclear, but Trump administration officials have repeatedly said they intend to impose tariffs similar to those the President set in 2025, before the Supreme Court invalidated his first batch of levies in February 2026.
In July, the USTR completed an investigation into forced labour in foreign supply chains, which it said justified tariffs of between 10 and 12.5 per cent on dozens of trading partners, including all 16 of the economies covered by the excess manufacturing probe. The new tariffs will likely be added to levies unveiled in July.
India-US Trade Deal
For months, India and the United States have been negotiating an interim bilateral trade agreement, the framework of which they finalised in February. It went back to the discussion board after the Supreme Court struck down the International Emergency Economic Powers Act tariffs imposed last year.
Under the deal, New Delhi is seeking lower tariffs for its goods in the US market than its competitor nations such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Cambodia.

title: Stock market today: Sensex jumps over 2000 points; Nifty50 tops 25,900! Investors richer by Rs 3.84 lakh crore - what's fueling the rally
description: NEW DELHI: Indian benchmark indices rallied sharply on Wednesday, with the BSE Sensex surging over 2,000 points and the Nifty 50 climbing above 25,900 in
author: Kanchan Yadav
content:
NEW DELHI: Indian benchmark indices rallied sharply on Wednesday, with the 
BSE Sensex
 surging over 2,000 points and the 
Nifty 50
 climbing above 25,900 in early trade. The sharp gains added Rs 3.84 lakh crore to investors' wealth, taking the total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies to Rs 513 lakh crore.
Strong foreign fund inflows, easing crude oil prices, buying in heavyweight banking stocks and resilient corporate earnings supported the rally, even as global markets remained volatile amid concerns over AI-linked stocks.
The BSE Sensex surged 2,028.05 points, or 2.46%, to 84,464.54, while the Nifty 50 climbed 570.65 points, or 2.25%, to 25,919.90 in late-morning trade on Wednesday.
Earlier, the Sensex had jumped 1,382.16 points to 83,818.15, while the Nifty advanced 407.60 points to 25,758.45 in the opening session.
The rally followed Monday's sharp selloff, when the Sensex plunged 1,483.72 points, or 1.77%, to close at 82,435.99, while the Nifty fell 450.95 points, or 1.75%, to 25,349.65. Stock markets were closed on Tuesday on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.
Top 5 reasons behind the stock market rally1. Strong foreign fund inflows
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued to buy Indian equities, providing strong support to domestic markets. 
Foreign investors purchased shares worth Rs 5,672.99 crore on Monday, according to exchange data.
Foreign inflows into India have strengthened this month, reflecting a reversal in investor sentiment towards domestic equities.
V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said, "The total reversal of the FII stance towards India is reflected in the FII investment into India, so far, this month at a record $13.2 billion."
2. Lower crude oil prices
Crude oil prices eased on Wednesday, helping improve India's macroeconomic outlook and reducing concerns over inflation and the country's import bill.
Brent crude futures fell 0.5% to $90.97 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) declined 0.6% to $81.58 a barrel. Both benchmarks had gained more than 2% on Tuesday.
Prices have been under pressure amid rising supply and expectations of a market surplus, despite concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East.
3. Rupee rises 23 paise against US dollar
Rupee strengthened 23 paise to 92.62 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday, supported by foreign fund inflows, strong domestic equities and lower crude oil prices.
The rupee opened at 92.65 in the interbank foreign exchange market and subsequently gained to 92.62 against the greenback.
A stronger US dollar, however, capped gains in the domestic currency. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, rose 0.15% to 103.90.
Earlier on Monday, rupee had declined 23 paise to close at 92.85 against the dollar, retreating from its seven-month high.
4. Heavyweight banking stocks lead gains
Banking stocks were among the biggest contributors to the market rally, with strong buying in heavyweight private lenders lifting benchmark indices.
HDFC Bank surged 3.54%, ICICI Bank rose 3.19%, Bajaj Finance advanced 2.65%, Axis Bank added 2.13% and Bajaj Finserv climbed 2.09%.
The Nifty Private Bank index gained 2.27%, while the Nifty PSU Bank index rose 0.68%.
Financial stocks gained 2.2% in broader sectoral trade, with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Reliance Industries also among the major contributors to the rally.
5. Strong corporate earnings support sentiment
Domestic earnings have provided support to Indian equities despite volatility in global markets.
Vijayakumar said, "It is important to understand that India’s improving fundamentals, as reflected in the impressive 27% earnings growth of Nifty 50 in Q2 has the potential to support the increasing FII inflows and impart resilience to the market."
Investors have also been shifting funds towards Indian equities as global markets face uncertainty over valuations and spending in the artificial intelligence sector.
"Earnings have provided a domestic anchor, while rotation away from Asian AI trades have also helped redirect capital towards India," Venkatesh Balasubramaniam and Shanay Mehta of JM Financial told Reuters.
A sharp correction in crude prices has also reduced pressure on the macroeconomic outlook, the analyst added.
6. Recovery after Monday's selloff; global AI trade volatility
Indian markets rebounded after Monday's sharp correction, with investors looking to recover losses amid heightened volatility in global equities.
Vijayakumar said global markets have been witnessing sharp swings driven by AI-linked stocks, with movements in the Nasdaq influencing technology-heavy markets across Asia, including South Korea, Taiwan and Japan.
"There is heightened volatility in global equity markets caused mainly by the swings in AI trade. When the Nasdaq goes down other AI markets like South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, too, go down; when Nasdaq bounces back, these AI trade-dominated markets, too, bounce back. The derivatives trade is aggravating the down moves and up moves in the market, as happened in India last Monday," he said.
"Investors should ignore these wild moves and noise associated with this hyper speculative trade and focus on the fundamentals. From the fundamentals perspective, the Indian market looks resilient," he added.
The rally extended beyond frontline stocks, with broader markets opening in positive territory. The Nifty 100 rose 1.38%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 0.89% and 0.48%, respectively.
Among sectoral indices, the Nifty IT jumped 2.39%, the Nifty Private Bank advanced 2.27%, the Nifty FMCG gained 0.96% and the Nifty Pharma rose 0.98%. The Nifty Auto edged up 0.19%.
However, Tata Steel, Mahindra & Mahindra, Titan and Power Grid were among the stocks trading lower.
The rally in Indian equities came despite weakness across several major Asian markets, where technology stocks faced renewed selling amid global AI-related volatility and concerns over fresh US tariffs.
South Korea's Kospi fell 5.30%, Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 2.74% and Shanghai's SSE Composite index dropped 1%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng traded marginally higher.
The US markets also ended mixed on Tuesday. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% and the S&P 500 declined 0.50%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.85%.
