title: Down the Rabbit Hole: Decoding the GTA VI craze for normies and non-gamers
description: In British politics in the early noughties, it was said that the most terrifying words in the political lexicon were: “Michael Crick is in reception.” The
author: Nirmalya Dutta
content:
In British politics in the early noughties, it was said that the most terrifying words in the political lexicon were: “Michael Crick is in reception.” The words reflected the sheer terror generated in British political circles by the “terrier-like reputation” of Crick, whose journalism, combining unstinting principles with inexhaustible research, made even the most seasoned politicians, used to the most putrid tabloids, quake in their boots.
But the times change, and those who don’t change with the times are often the subject of some ridicule, as Crick learned when he tweeted his outrage about GTA VI on the BBC, calling it a “ridiculous puff (piece)” and “appalling free advertising”.
Crick’s diatribe led Piers Morgan, a man who moves with the alacrity of a bloodhound pouncing upon any outrage, to rebut him with “Calm down, Grandpa”.
Now we live in a hyperconnected world, where we face being labelled outcasts, where one can be mocked for not weighing in on the ending of 
Game of Thrones
, being excited about 
Avengers: Doomsday
, or explaining why the first few soporific episodes of 
Breaking Bad
 are worth the wait.
But even by those exalted standards, GTA VI seems to have become a hitherto unseen cultural phenomenon that has consumed everything in its wake.
The blurb of JRR Tolkien’s 
Lord of the Rings
 used to read: “The English-speaking world is divided into those who have read Lord of the Rings, and those who are going to read Lord of the Rings.” The same applies to GTA VI: even if not everyone plays the game, everyone will be part of the conversation.
Now, if, like Crick, you are scratching your head about how a video game with a grammatically wonky (but legally sound) title became a global phenomenon, here’s a primer.
GTA VI for Noobs
There was a time when gamers were often chided by their mothers for wasting time on video games. Today, it’s usually their wives doing the chiding, but it’s kind of ironic given that Nvidia’s chips, from a company that cut its teeth by making GPUs for gaming nerds, are the foundation upon which the modern AI frontier model race is built.
To understand the GTA phenomenon, we have to take a small walk through the history of video games, which, in popular imagination, started with two white rectangles hitting a white dot across a black screen. That might sound like an exaggeration, but that’s one of the earliest commercially successful video games, called 
Pong
, released by Atari in 1972. The graphics became better with time, with a dot becoming a spaceship in 
Space Invaders
 (1978) and a yellow circle in 
Pac-Man
 (1980). Then came the gaming console era, where aeons were wasted getting an Italian plumber or a parkour-loving prince to rescue a pixelated princess.
Soon, gaming moved from addictive pixels in a 2D world to a more open space.
At this time, a company in Scotland named DMA Design, founded by David Jones, 
developed a game called Race ‘n’ Chase
 that involved police officers pursuing criminals. That turned out to be inordinately, mind-numbingly boring, so the company flipped the script and made the criminal the protagonist, and 
Grand Theft Auto
 was first released in 1997.
And thus we got the most famous Scottish export since whisky and Sean Connery, with each open world based on a real city. The game arrived at a time when politicians discovered that, rather than take responsibility, video games, along with rock music, comic books and television, could be blamed for the moral degradation of society. They were certainly helped by 
notorious British publicist Max Clifford
, who understood that the easiest way to sell something was to get elected officials to deride it. GTA was discussed in the House of Lords – which, given its antecedents, would be a perfect location for a GTA spinoff – and got the kind of publicity money cannot buy.
Onscreen, the revolution happened when GTA went from a bird’s-eye, two-dimensional Flatland look to a full three-dimensional open world with GTA III, where one could do everything one wants to do in the real world but cannot because one’s constitution is too delicate for jail: run over pedestrians, sell drugs and do other things that are frowned upon in civil society.
The latest instalment, GTA VI, takes us back to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami in the state of Leonida, Rockstar’s take on Florida where all the folks are doing things that allows us to create the Florida man headlines.
This time the protagonists are couple Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Jason is a former soldier and Lucia GTA’s first female protagonist which is enough to heckle incels across the world. And much like its predecessors, the actual storyline is only part of the attraction, since players are free to ignore it and spend their time doing whatever they please, provided the game's creators have programmed it.
While explaining the much-debated 
New York Times
 100 Greatest TV Shows of the 21st Century, the Times’ chief television critic James Poniewozik explained that 
The Sopranos
 didn’t make the cut because it premiered in 1999, but its legacy was writ large in the antihero dramas that made the cut, including its top three offerings: 
Breaking Bad
, 
The Wire
 and 
Mad Men
. The same goes for the GTA series, where we’ve overwhelmingly batted for the chance to roleplay as deeply problematic protagonists without having to pay for our sins, as Plato explored all those centuries ago in 
The Republic
 through the story of the Ring of Gyges, which would appear to be an inspiration for Gollum and the LOTR ring.
One could even go further and say that the current state of the world, where the most powerful nation is led by a self-aggrandising leader who doesn’t even pretend to couch his avarice in terms of politesse, as was the norm in politics before, is beginning to resemble a live-action version of GTA.
GTA VI in Numbers
Now every qualitative assessment can come down to a quantitative measure, particularly when a video game gets the sort of attention normally reserved for a World Cup final, a general election result or the death of a monarch.
The numbers make for remarkable reading.
GTA V sold 235 million copies, while GTA VI recorded 32.5 million pre-release sales. Meanwhile, GTA-related content has amassed 900 billion YouTube views, including 40 billion for GTA VI before its launch.
When 
GTA V was released in September 2013
, it earned over $800 million in retail sales within 24 hours and crossed the billion-dollar mark in three days, making it the fastest entertainment product in history to reach that milestone.
For context, 
Avengers: Endgame
, which involved the combined efforts of nearly every superhero Marvel had managed to assemble over a decade, took five days to reach $1 billion at the box office.
GTA VI, released on November 19, 2026, made those figures look like petty change.
According to 
Rockstar Games
, GTA VI generated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, including pre-orders, with 32.5 million copies sold before release. GTA VI, meanwhile, had already sold a staggering 32.5 million copies before it was even released. GTA V sold 235 million copies since 2013, taking the total number of copies, including GTA VI pre-sales, to approximately 512 million.
YouTube states that content related to the GTA franchise has accumulated 900 billion views on the platform, while GTA VI-related videos attracted 40 billion views before the game hit the shelves.
GTA V sold 235 million copies, while GTA VI recorded 32.5 million pre-release sales. Meanwhile, GTA-related content has amassed 900 billion YouTube views, including 40 billion for GTA VI before its launch.
The release itself attracted 7.91 million concurrent viewers across livestreaming platforms, with gamers collectively watching more than 125 million hours of GTA VI streams in the first 24 hours.
But perhaps the most astonishing number is 
13
.
13 years separated GTA V and GTA VI. When the former was released, Barack Obama was US president, Narendra Modi was the chief minister of Gujarat, Manchester United were serial Premier League winners, and the idea of a former reality star upending the world order was laughable.
But perhaps the metric that shows GTA’s stickiness is the fact that between 2013 and 2025, GTA V remained among YouTube’s ten most-viewed games every single year. In a world where it’s almost impossible to remember what happened between two seasons – and can anyone really tell the Targaryen siblings apart in 
House of the Dragon
? – GTA maintained its cultural relevance.
The Cultural Impact of GTA VI
Even before GTA VI dropped, the cultural impact of the game became evident. The moment the first trailer came out, featuring 
Tom Petty’s 1989 song Love Is a Long Road
, the song saw a 36,979% surge in Spotify streams, eventually crossing 40 million streams. The 
first trailer on YouTube
 racked up 93 million views in 24 hours and a total of over 310 million views.
Thirteen years separated GTA V and GTA VI. The world witnessed a pandemic, Messi winning the World Cup, Donald Trump winning two presidential elections and the rise of generative AI. Yet GTA V remained among YouTube’s ten most-viewed games every year from 2013 to 2025.
In India, which has an estimated 
550 million gamers
, mostly on mobile games, GTA VI was released on the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, making it inaccessible to anyone who didn’t own a compatible console or have access to one. Yet, on the day of its release, 
gaming cafés across the country were jam-packed
, with many taking leave from work to play.
Like all things on the internet, it also immediately became a cultural flashpoint, with many complaining that GTA VI was too sanitised because it forces the protagonist to fix sinks, go on dates and even work out, things that people log in to their video games to avoid doing in the real world.
Influential streamer 
Asmongold complained
 about having to repair a sink, rub Lucia's feet and listen to her friends' stories, while others complained that the game had become too 'woke'. A game that was once deemed to be responsible for moral degradation in the real world was now being accused of replicating it too exactly.
The game's most enduring contribution to internet culture, however, might be the meme 
“We got this before GTA VI”
, which became a shorthand for events that nobody thought would happen before the game was released.
In the thirteen years between GTA V and GTA VI, we witnessed a global pandemic, the death of Queen Elizabeth II, Messi winning the World Cup, Donald Trump winning the White House twice, and the rise of generative AI, which means that humanity managed to create machines capable of writing poetry, generating videos and replacing white-collar workers before Rockstar managed to release another GTA. The meme became so popular that when GTA VI finally arrived, internet users started mourning its demise, while some pointed out that we had even got the end of the “We got this before GTA VI” meme before GTA VI.
Brands, governments and even military alliances decided to jump on the bandwagon. Singapore wondered why folks couldn’t remember the MRT map. Miami police reminded gamers that, unlike the game, their city had rules. KFC had a mock funeral for “Ann Alibi”. The 
White House released a GTA-inspired video
 while 
PM Narendra Modi used GTA V vs GTA VI
 to highlight the Centre’s developmental work.
Twenty-nine years after politicians worried about the moral degradation caused by a fictional world, that world’s cultural baggage had become too much for the real world to ignore. One wonders what Max Clifford, who understood the value of manufacturing outrage, would have made of a world where prime ministers, presidents and military alliances were doing Rockstar’s publicity for free.
As Bob Dylan warned in 
The Times They Are A-Changin’
: “Your sons and your daughters are beyond your command.” Six decades later, the parents and politicians seem to have finally got the message.
Now it’s their turn to sing the children’s tune.

title: 'Play 20 balls, the score will be different': How Yuvraj Singh's 30-minute call unleashed Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 204
description: NEW DELHI: A half-hour conversation with his idol and mentor Yuvraj Singh proved to be the turning point for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who went on to produce
author: Hijam Raju Singh
content:
NEW DELHI: A half-hour conversation with his idol and mentor 
Yuvraj Singh
 proved to be the turning point for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who went on to produce one of the most extraordinary batting performances in the history of the game, smashing a world-record 204 off just 53 balls against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament on Tuesday.
The 15-year-old left-hander revealed that he had been struggling with his form and was mentally distracted by a string of low scores before the match. Seeking clarity, he turned to four people, including his father, childhood coach Manish Hoja, former India Under-19 teammate Pratham Jachak and Yuvraj.
But it was the conversation with Yuvraj that helped him identify technical flaws, regain confidence and approach his innings with a clearer mindset.
In a video shared by the 
BCCI
, Sooryavanshi opened up about the conversation and how the former India all-rounder's advice shaped his approach against the UAE.
"I spoke to him [Yuvraj Singh] for almost half an hour. He explained a lot to me about batting. I was very worried, so I spoke to him openly. Sir, I am having these problems. When I am going to bat on the wicket. He explained everything to me for half an hour. He told me that if I play 20 balls, the score will be different. 
He told me a lot of technical things. That helped me a lot today," Sooryavanshi said.
'My mind was a little diverted': Yuvraj's advice helped him rediscover his game
Sooryavanshi admitted that his recent struggles had left him questioning his approach, with the youngster unable to score runs in his previous two matches and a few domestic outings.
He said Yuvraj's advice carried particular weight because of the admiration he has for the former India all-rounder.
"It's not easy, but as I told you, the last two matches and a few domestic matches, I couldn't score runs. I was a little diverted, and kept asking myself what is happening. But I spoke to Yuvraj sir, he is my idol. If you talk to an idol, you listen to everything he says. I listened to everything he said. He told me a lot of important things," he said.
Sooryavanshi also revealed that reviewing videos of his batting helped him recognise the mistakes he had been making. He then tried to implement Yuvraj's suggestions rather than repeat those errors.
"I saw the video of my batting. I felt that I was making a mistake. I tried not to make those mistake today. I tried to do what he told me to do. He helped me a lot," he added.
Backing his strengths after assessing the conditions
The teenager's innings against the UAE was a remarkable display of power-hitting, but he insisted that his approach was not simply about attacking from the outset. Instead, he first assessed the conditions before deciding to play to his strengths.
"I just had the mindset to go and see how the wicket was. I went and saw a couple of balls. The ball was coming well on the bat, so I backed my game," he explained.
Sooryavanshi also reiterated that he does not consider himself a batter restricted to one format, saying he has the ability to adjust his approach according to the demands of the game.
"When I was interviewed after the IPL in Ahmedabad, I said that I can play in all three formats. I can change the game according to the situation. I have that much control over my game," he said.
He admitted, however, that he had been trying to play the same way in recent matches, even attempting to adopt a longer-format approach when the situation did not necessarily demand it.
"But in the last two matches, I was trying to play the same way. I was trying to play in a long format. Even today, I had the same mindset. But when I saw the wicket, I didn't feel much help. If I tried to take shots, the ball was coming to my bat. So I backed my strength," he concluded.
The result was an astonishing 204 off 53 balls, featuring 28 sixes and seven fours, as India registered a seven-wicket victory over the UAE.

title: Caught in transit: Passenger on moving bike takes one-handed catch of ball hit for six in Pakistan; video goes viral
description: A passenger on a moving motorcycle caught a ball hit for six outside the stadium during a Swat Premier League match between Swat Strikers and GKR Dir in
author: Shubhanshu Dwivedi
content:
A passenger on a moving motorcycle caught a ball hit for six outside the stadium during a Swat Premier League match between Swat Strikers and GKR Dir in Pakistan. The incident took place during the tournament's eighth season and has since gone viral on social media.
The catch came in the sixth over of GKR Dir's innings when a batter struck the ball over the extra-cover boundary. The shot cleared the stadium and travelled outside the ground, where a passenger sitting on a passing motorcycle managed to catch it with one hand while the vehicle was still moving.
The video has attracted attention on social media, with users reacting to the catch and comparing it with some of the fielding efforts seen in international cricket. One user described it as the "Catch of the century". Another appeared to refer to New Zealand's Glenn Phillips, who is known for taking difficult catches on the field, and wrote, "Phillips who?"
The Swat Premier League is a local tape-ball tournament in Pakistan, with each team getting 10 overs to bat in an innings. The incident happened during Match 4 of the competition between Swat Strikers and GKR Dir.
While the catch outside the stadium became the talking point, Swat Strikers also secured a 34-run win in the match. They posted 148/6 in their allotted 10 overs before restricting GKR Dir to 114/9, sealing the victory.
The viral moment has added an unusual talking point to a match that otherwise saw Swat Strikers dominate the contest.

title: A Kerala woman who lost a local election by just 13 votes in 2020 moved to Canada with her husband; five years later, Sneha Joy has won a Canadian $5 million lottery jackpot worth more than Rs 30 crore
description: In 2020, Sneha Joy from Kerala's Ernakulam district contested the local body elections as a United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate but lost by 13 votes.
author: TOI Lifestyle Desk
content:
In 2020, Sneha Joy from 
Kerala
's Ernakulam district contested the local body elections as a United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate but lost by 13 votes. Little did she know that a new beginning was waiting for her. She moved to Canada and five years later she won the Canadian $5 million lottery jackpot, which is nearly Rs 30 crore! Sneha, a woman from Kerala's Ernakulam district, won in Canada’s Lotto 6/49 lottery, turning an ordinary lottery ticket into a life-changing windfall.
Let’s find out more about this lucky woman:
Meet Sneha Joy
Sneha is originally from Vengoor near Perumbavoor in Kerala. Her journey from local politics to becoming a millionaire in Canada has made headlines. While her electoral debut did not go as she had hoped, she got lucky thousands of kilometres away.
Before moving to Canada, Joy had built an academic and professional career in Kerala. An engineering graduate with a triple-main degree, she worked at a firm in the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Kakkanad, Ernakulam.
In 2020, she decided to enter electoral politics and contested the Vengoor Grama Panchayat elections as a UDF candidate from the Kaippilly ward. 
But she lost to her rival from the Left Democratic Front (LDF) by just 13 votes.
Four months after the election, Joy married Vijil Varghese, an engineer from Nilambur in Malappuram district. The couple moved to Canada and settled in Edmonton.
A routine lottery check changed everything
According to a report by Onmanorama, Joy had purchased her ticket through the Lotto Spot app and checked it after the October 21 draw. She had matched all six numbers in the Classic jackpot of Canada's Lotto 6/49 lottery.
The six winning numbers were:
1, 10, 18, 22, 33, 37
The numbers that changed her life as Joy had won CAD 5 million. She had become a multi-millionaire overnight.
"I was shocked!" she said while claiming the prize.
She summed up her emotions in three words: "Shock. Happy. Relief."
The jackpot was officially confirmed by the Western Canada Lottery Corporation (WCLC) on November 20. The lottery corporation announced Joy as the winner of the CAD 5 million prize.
Paying off her mortgage is her first priority
"I'm going to pay off my mortgage," she said, explaining that becoming free of her home loan is the main priority.
For many families, owning a home comes with years of loan repayments, monthly installments and financial planning. Joy's decision to use her unexpected fortune to settle her mortgage reflects the importance she places on financial security.
Once that responsibility is taken care of, she hopes to fulfil another dream: travelling around the world.
"After that, I'm going to take a trip around the world!" she said.
She also intends to share a portion of her winnings with her family.
"To be financially stress-free!" was how she described the best part of winning the jackpot in her conversation with lottery officials.
The WCLC release also recorded her intention to help her family, suggesting that the windfall is not just about personal ambitions but also about sharing the benefits with those closest to her.
A new life in Canada
Her father, PP Joy, is a local Congress booth president, while her mother, Joly, is a homemaker. Sneha is their only daughter. Her connection with public life was perhaps not surprising, given her father's involvement in local politics.
Her marriage to Vijil Varghese came four months after the election. The couple subsequently relocated to Edmonton, Canada, where they began building a life together.
Five years later, the woman who once came tantalisingly close to winning a local election in Kerala has found herself celebrating a much bigger and entirely unexpected victory in a different country. For a family from a modest agricultural background, the news of their daughter winning millions in Canada is undoubtedly a moment to cherish.
And while a lottery jackpot can change someone's life overnight, Joy's first thoughts after the win have been about clearing her home loan, travelling the world and sharing her happiness with family, plans that make this unexpected fortune all the more relatable.

title: 'Reel blocked, visa cancelled': Dhruv Rathee hits out at Centre after Saurav Das denied flight to London
description: NEW DELHI: YouTuber and influencer Dhruv Rathee on Tuesday criticised the Narendra Modi led BJP government.
author: Prisha Patnaik
content:
NEW DELHI: YouTuber and influencer Dhruv Rathee on Tuesday criticised the Narendra Modi led BJP government. In a post on X he alleged that those who speak against PM Modi face a range of consequences, including blocked social media content, legal cases and detention.In a post on X Rathee said, “If you criticise Narendra Modi — your reel will be blocked in India, your visa will be cancelled (if you are foreign citizen), you will be stopped from going outside India (if you are Indian citizen), you will get fake court cases on you, you will get illegally detained / arrested / kidnapped by police.”
He also alleged that critics could face “fake charges” from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), ending the post with the sarcastic remark and a clown emoji, “Mother of Democracy!”Rathee’s post came amid two recent developments involving people associated with criticism of the government.On Monday, a Delhi court issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Rathee in a 2018 defamation case filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan, also known as Vikas Pandey. The case relates to a video uploaded by Rathee on his YouTube channel, which the complainant alleges was defamatory.
Earlier this month, the court had issued fresh bailable warrants after a process server reported that Rathee’s residence was locked when he attempted to serve notice.
The court had also issued fresh summons to Rathee at his Gurugram address.In another incident, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Saurav Das alleged that he was stopped from boarding a flight to London at Delhi airport, where he was scheduled to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.Das said he had been invited by Oxford, Cambridge, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh to speak about the CJP movement. He accused the government of preventing him from travelling because it feared his views would reach international academic institutions.Rathee’s post linked the developments to what he described as consequences faced by people who criticise the prime minister.
Prisha Patnaik is a journalist with The Times of India, writing across geopolitics, international affairs, culture, history and internet culture. With over two years of experience in social media and digital content, she is interested in how news, politics and culture are shaped for digital audiences. She holds a master’s degree in Media and Communications from Goldsmiths, University of London.

title: Already gasping for breath, Delhi battles 14 garbage fires daily
description: Delhi battles 14 garbage fires daily, with waste burning contributing up to 17% of PM2.5; toxic fumes from plastics and chemicals worsen health risks.
author: Abhay
content:
NEW DELHI: For a city already grappling with alarming levels of air pollution, frequent garbage fires are only adding to its environmental woes.On average daily, Delhi Fire Service (DFS) receives 14 calls related to garbage fires, with the burning of mixed waste, including plastics and chemical-laden materials, releasing toxic fumes and further deteriorating air quality.
Apart from worsening pollution, these fires also pose serious risks to public health.DFS data shows calls related to 5,465 garbage and rubbish fires were received in 2025. Till Nov 10 this year, 4,344 such calls have been recorded.
According to fire officials, garbage fires can occur due to several factors, such as the accumulation of combustible waste in landfills. Decomposing waste releases methane, a highly flammable gas that can catch fire when it comes into contact with a spark or an ignition source. Materials such as dry leaves, paper, plastic and other combustible substances can catch fire, particularly during periods of intense heat.
In some cases, people accidentally trigger fires by disposing of hot ash or burnt material without ensuring it has been completely extinguished. There are also instances of people deliberately setting garbage heaps on fire, while some individuals collect combustible waste and burn it to keep themselves warm during the winter months.
Preventing such incidents requires greater public awareness about the dangers of burning garbage and the importance of safe waste disposal practices. Fire officials also emphasise the need to provide adequate electrical equipment, along with promoting responsible waste handling and discouraging open burning.
According to real-time source apportionment data of Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, waste burning is currently one of the top contributors to Delhi’s PM2.5. On Monday, the share of waste burning (municipal/plastic-rubber/e-waste) was 12% while between 1am and 9am Tuesday, it rose to 17%. 
Former DFS director Atul Garg said garbage fires, particularly those involving chemicals and plastics, cause significant harm to the environment. “Garbage dumps contain all kinds of waste, including plastics, chemicals and other combustible materials, and the sooner such fires are extinguished, the better it is for the environment,” he added.
Garbage fires can be triggered by several factors, including carelessly discarded bidi and cigarette butts, which can ignite dry waste and other combustible materials. The accumulation of mixed waste, such as plastic, paper, cloth, dry leaves and chemical substances, further increases the risk of fires. When this waste burns, it releases toxic gases, harmful chemicals and fine particulate matter into the atmosphere, contributing to severe air pollution, Garg said.
“Prolonged exposure to the smoke can cause respiratory problems. Therefore, garbage fires must be extinguished as quickly as possible to minimise environmental damage and protect public health,” he said.
Noting that waste “pollutes our air at every step”, Sunil Dahiya, founder of the think tank Envirocatalyst, said, “In residential societies, garbage and dry leaves are burnt where people live. On roads, waste is dumped and set on fire, and leftover waste is ground into dust that traffic lifts back into the air. Diesel garbage trucks, often uncovered, add emissions and spillage across the city.
“Landfills like Ghazipur, Bhalswa and Okhla smoulder and leak methane year-round, while incinerators burning mixed, wet waste release particulates, dioxins and toxic metals. Without segregation at source, local composting, electric collection and an end to burning, we are fighting air pollution with one hand tied.”

title: Why do plastic water bottles have ridges and grooves? The surprising science behind those lines on your everyday bottle
description: Pick up a plastic water bottle, whether it costs Rs 10, Rs 20 or Rs 40, and take a closer look.
author: TOI Lifestyle Desk
content:
Pick up a plastic water bottle, whether it costs Rs 10, Rs 20 or Rs 40, and take a closer look. Most bottles have a series of ridges, grooves or indented lines running around their bodies. Some have a few prominent rings near the bottom, while others feature patterns that extend almost the entire length of the bottle. They may look like a simple design choice, but these lines serve several practical purposes. From making bottles stronger to reducing the amount of plastic required in manufacturing, these seemingly insignificant details are part of a carefully engineered design. They also help bottles withstand the physical demands of transportation, storage and everyday use. So, why do manufacturers put these lines on plastic bottles, and what would happen if the bottles had completely smooth surfaces? Scroll down to read more.
The lines make plastic bottles stronger
One of the biggest reasons behind the ridges is structural strength. Most disposable water bottles are made using polyethylene terephthalate (PET), a lightweight plastic that is widely used in food and beverage packaging.
While PET is durable for its weight, thin plastic walls can easily bend, buckle or deform when pressure is applied. 
A completely smooth bottle may therefore be more vulnerable to dents and changes in shape, particularly when it is squeezed or stacked with other bottles.
The ridges help address this problem. Much like the folds in corrugated cardboard or the curved surfaces used in certain architectural structures, these patterns improve the bottle’s resistance to deformation. They distribute pressure across different sections of the bottle rather than allowing the entire surface to collapse easily. This is particularly useful during transportation, when bottles are packed closely together in cartons, stacked in warehouses and moved across long distances.
They help manufacturers use less plastic
Another important reason is cost and material efficiency. Plastic manufacturers constantly look for ways to make packaging lighter without compromising its ability to hold liquids safely. Using thicker plastic throughout a bottle would make it more rigid, but it would also increase the quantity of raw material required.
Ridges and grooves offer an alternative. By changing the geometry of the bottle, manufacturers can improve its structural performance without necessarily increasing the thickness of its walls. This allows companies to produce lightweight packaging while maintaining the strength needed for handling, distribution and storage.
The difference may appear insignificant when looking at a single bottle. However, beverage companies manufacture millions of bottles, sometimes every day. Even a small reduction in the amount of plastic used per bottle can translate into considerable material savings across large production volumes.
The grooves also make bottles easier to hold
There is another everyday benefit that people often overlook: grip. A smooth plastic bottle can become slippery, particularly when condensation forms on its outer surface after being taken out of a refrigerator. The ridges provide small areas of texture that make it easier to hold the bottle securely.
This is useful when carrying water while travelling, exercising or walking outdoors. It also makes bottles easier to handle when they are partially crushed or nearly empty. The placement and depth of these grooves vary depending on the bottle’s shape, capacity and intended use. Some manufacturers use subtle horizontal rings, while others incorporate deeper indentations or patterned sections.
Do the lines help bottles withstand pressure?
Yes, although their role depends on the type of bottle and the way it is designed. Plastic bottles experience different kinds of pressure during manufacturing, transportation and storage. Changes in temperature and atmospheric pressure can also affect the shape of a sealed container.
The grooves provide flexibility in the bottle’s structure, allowing certain sections to bend slightly rather than transferring all the force to one area. This can help reduce unwanted deformation. However, not all ridges are designed for the same purpose. Some are primarily structural, while others are incorporated to improve grip or accommodate the requirements of a particular manufacturing process.
For example, carbonated drink bottles generally have more specialised designs because they need to withstand the internal pressure created by dissolved carbon dioxide. Their bases and sidewalls are engineered differently from those of ordinary drinking water bottles.
Why don’t all plastic bottles have the same patterns?
If you compare different water bottles, you will notice that their grooves are not identical. Some have narrow rings around the middle, others have deep vertical indentations, and certain bottles have heavily textured bases.
This is because bottle design depends on several factors, including the type of plastic, the quantity of liquid it needs to hold, its shape, manufacturing requirements and the conditions in which it will be transported. A small disposable bottle may need a different structural design from a large water container intended for repeated handling.
Manufacturers also consider how much material they can save while ensuring the packaging remains functional and does not leak or become damaged during normal use.
Why do some expensive water bottles have a completely smooth surface?
Interestingly, not every plastic water bottle has visible ridges or grooves. Some premium bottled water brands use smooth, minimalist bottle designs, even though their containers are made from lightweight plastic. This does not necessarily mean these bottles are weaker or that they use more plastic. Their strength depends on several factors, including the quality and thickness of the material, the bottle’s overall shape and the way its walls are engineered.
 Manufacturers can also use different moulding techniques and carefully designed curves to achieve the required rigidity without prominent external grooves. In the premium segment, packaging is also an important part of brand positioning. A sleek, transparent bottle with a smooth finish can create a more refined appearance and make the product stand out on shelves. The higher price, therefore, is not necessarily a reflection of the absence of ridges. It can also account for branding, packaging choices, sourcing, distribution and the product’s overall market positioning.
Are the lines only for decoration?
Not entirely. Although bottle manufacturers may use ridges and patterns to create a distinctive appearance for their products, these features generally have practical engineering purposes. The next time you pick up a Rs 10, Rs 20 or Rs 40 plastic water bottle, those seemingly ordinary lines are worth a second look. They are not simply decorative marks. They are part of the design that helps keep the bottle lightweight, manageable and strong enough to perform its everyday job. From reducing material use to improving grip and structural stability, a small detail on an everyday object reveals how much thought goes into modern packaging.

title: Seven farmers in Tamil Nadu started reviving traditional millet crops on just 5.5 acres; years later, K Saravanan's initiative has reached around 250 farmers across 20 villages, restoring cultivation on 426 acres
description: In Perambalur district of Tamil Nadu, traditional millets were gradually disappearing from farmlands as farmers shifted towards commercial crops such as
author: TOI Lifestyle Desk
content:
In Perambalur district of Tamil Nadu, traditional millets were gradually disappearing from farmlands as farmers shifted towards commercial crops such as maize and cotton. The change was largely driven by the hope of earning better returns, but rising cultivation costs, pest attacks and unpredictable market prices created new challenges.
Amid this changing agricultural landscape, seven farmers decided to give traditional millets another chance. They started cultivating kodo millet and black sorghum organically on just 5.5 acres. What followed was a farming initiative that gradually grew into a movement involving hundreds of farmers.
At the centre of this effort is K Saravanan, a 45-year-old from Veppur, who helped establish a system where farmers could grow traditional crops without constantly worrying about finding buyers or receiving fair prices. Today, the initiative has reached around 250 farmers across 20 villages, bringing approximately 426 acres under millet cultivation. Together, they have produced nearly 206 metric tonnes of millets, demonstrating how a small farming experiment can create wider change when farmers receive the right support.
Seven farmers took the first step towards revival
Perambalur was once known for cultivating traditional varieties such as kodo millet, pearl millet, barnyard millet, foxtail millet, ragi and sorghum. 
However, over time, many farmers moved towards maize and cotton in search of better financial returns. Saravanan's involvement in rural development began in 2013 when he joined the Barefoot Academy of Governance, an organisation working towards community empowerment and stronger local governance.
During a four-month study in Veppur block, he interacted with farmers, women and other stakeholders to understand the challenges affecting the region. The declining cultivation of traditional millets emerged as an issue he wanted to address. In 2015, the organisation organised a seminar to encourage organic millet cultivation. Around 200 farmers attended, and 20 expressed interest in trying it. Saravanan assured them that their harvest would be purchased at prices higher than the prevailing market rates.
The initiative began with seven farmers growing kodo millet and black sorghum on 5.5 acres. They harvested approximately 1,350 kg of produce, which Saravanan procured at Rs 30 per kg, compared with the prevailing market price of Rs 25. This assurance of a buyer and a better price gave farmers a reason to reconsider crops that had gradually disappeared from their fields.
A fair price became the biggest reason to return to millets
One of the biggest challenges in agriculture is not always growing a crop, but finding a reliable market for it. Saravanan understood that farmers would be reluctant to abandon commercial crops unless traditional millet cultivation offered a dependable income. Instead of simply encouraging farmers to grow millets, his initiative focused on building a procurement system that considered their actual expenses.
The group began documenting cultivation costs from sowing to harvesting, including the expenses incurred by farmers. These calculations became the basis for deciding procurement prices through discussions with the cultivators themselves.
In 2020, Saravanan took the initiative forward independently by establishing the Nammalvar Iyarkkai Siruthaniya Uzhavar Urpathiyaalar Kuzhu, a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) in Veppur. He currently serves as its coordinator, while the organisation has 19 members. The FPO now purchases organically cultivated millets at around Rs 7 to Rs 9 more per kg than prevailing market prices. During 2025-26, when the market price was Rs 22 per kg, the organisation procured the produce at Rs 31 per kg.
It also purchases directly from farmers, bears transportation expenses and makes payments immediately, reducing the dependence on middlemen. As Saravanan explained, the objective is not to maximise profits but to ensure that farmers receive fair returns and traditional cultivation becomes financially sustainable.
From farm produce to millet-based products
As cultivation expanded, the group realised that purchasing the harvest was only one part of building a sustainable farming model. Processing and marketing the produce were equally important. In 2021, the FPO established a millet processing unit at Nannai village at a cost of Rs 18 lakh, with financial support from the Tamil Nadu State Planning Commission's State Balanced Growth Fund.
The facility processes the procured grains into millet rice and other products, creating additional opportunities to sell traditional crops beyond the local agricultural market. The organisation sells millet rice to organic stores at Rs 100 per kg, traditional millet seeds to farmers at Rs 50 per kg and whole grains to mills at Rs 36 per kg.
It has also distributed around eight tonnes of traditional millet seeds across Perambalur, Ariyalur, Cuddalore, Tiruchy and Villupuram districts through seed festivals and awareness programmes. This approach has helped connect cultivation, processing and marketing, giving farmers more confidence that their harvest will find buyers.
A farming model that puts farmers first
For the farmers who have joined the initiative, the biggest change is the assurance that their hard work will receive a fair price. V Chitra, a farmer from Anganur village, explained how the arrangement has changed their approach to cultivation. “Earlier, farmers were hesitant to cultivate millets as there was no assurance of a market or a fair price for their produce. The FPO’s initiative has given us the confidence to take up traditional millet cultivation again. We can sell our produce directly without worrying about middlemen or transportation expenses,” she said.
P Banumathi, secretary of the FPO, also pointed out that farmers growing maize and cotton had increasingly become dependent on chemical fertilisers and pesticides, adding to their cultivation expenses and exposing them to risks associated with unsafe pesticide use. 
Although Tamil Nadu introduced a millet mission in 2022 to encourage cultivation, Banumathi believes stronger price support and reliable procurement facilities are essential to bring more farmers back to traditional crops.
From seven farmers cultivating 5.5 acres to around 250 farmers across 20 villages, the initiative demonstrates how creating a dependable market can encourage agricultural change. For Saravanan, the bigger achievement is not simply the 426 acres brought back under millet cultivation or the nearly 206 metric tonnes produced. It is restoring farmers' confidence in crops that once formed an important part of the region's agricultural identity. What began with a small group willing to take a chance has now become an example of how fair pricing, collective decision-making and local participation can help revive traditional farming.

title: Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife MacKenzie Scott who sold half of her Amazon shares donated $62 million, what has been called landmark gift to meet 2030 goals by group of coastal communities and …
description: MacKenzie Scott, the ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who has sold around half of her Amazon shares, donated $62 million to marine conservation
author: TOI Tech Desk
content:
MacKenzie Scott, the ex-wife of 
Amazon
 founder 
Jeff Bezos
, who has sold around half of her Amazon shares, donated $62 million to marine conservation organisation Blue Ventures. The contribution, described by the organisation as a “landmark gift”, will support small-scale fishing communities across tropical regions and help them protect marine ecosystems and livelihoods. The funding will also support Blue Ventures' ambitious 2030 goals, which include enabling 10,000 fishing communities to lead marine conservation efforts, improving food security and economic resilience for 5 million people, and bringing 200,000 square kilometres of carbon-rich seas under local stewardship.
Why MacKenzie Scott donated $62 million to Blue Ventures
The donation, announced in December 2025, comes at a time when coastal communities are facing growing challenges from warming seas, declining fish catches and climate change. According to Blue Ventures, more than 100 million people depend on small-scale fishing for their daily food and livelihood. The organisation said the gift recognises the leadership of coastal communities and the solutions they are already developing using local knowledge and experience.
Blue Ventures CEO Ebrima Saidy said: “This gift strengthens trust in community-led conservation at a moment when coastal communities are carrying the greatest burden of the climate and ocean crisis. 
It enables us to continue standing firmly beside communities, complementing their efforts and respecting their autonomy to lead effectively. By backing approaches that have been shaped and proven locally, this funding helps fishing communities continue to safeguard marine life, sustain their way of life, and better respond to the challenges of a changing climate”.
What are Blue Ventures' 2030 goals
As stated above, Mackenzie Scott’s $62 million contribution will support the organisation's 2030 strategy, which places community leadership at the centre of marine conservation. Its targets include:
- Enabling 10,000 fishing communities to lead fisheries management and marine conservation.
- Improving food security and economic resilience for 5 million people.
- Bringing 200,000 square kilometres of carbon-rich seas under effective local stewardship.
- Equipping hundreds of grassroots organisations and communities with funding, skills, data and advocacy support.
A significant proportion of the funding will go directly to local partners through the Frontline Community Fund, providing flexible, long-term resources for communities to set their own priorities.
Chelsea Wieber, Blue Ventures' Director of Development, said: “This generous award couldn’t come at a more important moment for climate action and community-led solutions. We’re grateful for the trust and flexibility this funding brings, supporting not just our work but many others striving for a healthier, more resilient planet. I hope fellow philanthropists will join in, amplifying the impact across this remarkable group of organisations working to deliver lasting climate solutions for people and the planet”.

title: Para-sports selection trials held in Visakhapatnam
description: District-level para-sports trials in Visakhapatnam selected 56 athletes across six disciplines for state-level competition.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The District Sports Authority, Visakhapatnam, conducted district-level selection trials in six para-sports disciplines for boys and girls with disabilities aged above 13 years as on November 23 and 24, with 56 athletes participating.
The trials were organised under the aegis of the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP), in association with the Department for Welfare of differently-abled, transgender persons and senior citizens and the Para Sports Association, Visakhapatnam. The initiative was organised in connection with the International Day of Persons with Disabilities, observed every year on December 3.
The disciplines included para athletics, para badminton, para table tennis, para taekwondo, wheelchair fencing and blind goalball. The events were held at the DSA Indoor Stadium, Gopalapatnam, on November 23 and at the SAAP Integrated Sports Complex, Kommadi, on November 24.
Athletes selected at the district level will take part in the State-level competitions scheduled to be held in Vizianagaram district on December 1 and 2.

Kavitha, Assistant Director, Department for Welfare of Differently Abled, Sheetal Madan, honorary president of the Para Sports Association, Visakhapatnam and technical official P. Siva Kumar and the Samagra Shiksha coordinator were present.

title: Football seasons of a bygone Madras
description: A concise history of Madras football, tracing its roots, key clubs, venues, and evolving culture from colonial era to today.
author: Sriram V.
content:
Chennai’s football season is ongoing. The city’s association with the sport may not be celebrated the way Kolkata’s is but there is, nevertheless, a significant history that deserves better documentation than what we have. S. Muthiah has written about it in the columns of The Hindu and I, too, have written about its origins in Madras on June 20, 2014. This article takes off from what was written there.
That the divide between flannelled fools and muddied oafs existed for long in colonial circles is well known. The former were the cricketers and the latter the football players. Of course, in the off-season for cricket, the flannelled variety turned out to play two rougher games – hockey and football. It was a way of keeping fit in an era when other methods of exercise were not easily available. The Madras Gymkhana Club takes credit for introducing the game to our city and its E.K. Chetty Cup, instituted in 1895, was the first trophy for the game in Madras. That said, I can find no information on who this donor was. Madras had to wait 40 years before it got its next trophy – the Jatprole Cup.
Published - November 25, 2026 07:00 am IST

title: India-Nepal joint military exercise begins in Rupandehi
description: Nepal-India joint military drill Abhyas Suryakiran 20th edition begins in Rupandehi, focusing on disaster management, forestry, and humanitarian aid.
author: PTI
content:
A joint military training exercise between Nepal and India, focusing on disaster management, forest welfare and humanitarian assistance, commenced on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
The 20th edition of the training exercise, “Abhyas Suryakiran”, began at Nepal Army Battle School in Saljhandi, Rupandehi district, according to a press release issued by the Nepal Army.
The exercise, involving battalion-level soldiers from the two countries, will run till December 8.
During the exercise, the military personnel of the two countries will exchange theoretical and practical aspects as well as special experiences relating to disaster management, forest warfare and humanitarian assistance, according to the Nepal Army.
The 19th edition of the joint military exercise was held in Uttarakhand’s Pithoragarh last year.
The Nepal Army believes such types of military exercises will further deepen friendly military relations between the two countries and also enhance professional skills and understanding between the soldiers of the two countries, the press release said.

title: Hyderabad airport commissions facility to raise storage capacity by 140%
description: Hyderabad’s airport to boosts cargo capacity 140% as it commissioned a new storage system
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The Rajiv Gandhi International Airport at Shamshabad has commissioned an upgraded Elevated Transfer Vehicle (ETV)-based storage system at its cargo terminal to increase storage capacity and improve cargo handling. The upgrade will also strengthen facilities for temperature-controlled and specialised cargo, airport authorities said in a press release.
The new system has increased the terminal’s Unit Load Device storage capacity from 33 to 80, a rise of over 140%. By adding vertical storage space, the airport can handle larger cargo volumes without expanding the existing terminal area. The additional capacity will also help it manage multiple freighter operations simultaneously and accommodate future growth, airport officials said.
The upgrade will enable airlines, freight forwarders and logistics partners to handle cargo faster and with greater flexibility, said Kadhir Kadhiravan, CEO, GHIAL. It would also strengthen Hyderabad’s position as a hub for high-value, time-sensitive and pharmaceutical cargo, he added.
“This enhancement enables airlines, freight forwarders and logistics partners to move cargo with greater speed, reliability and flexibility, while supporting the growing demands of global trade. We are not only preparing for future growth but also reinforcing Hyderabad’s position as a trusted hub for high value, time-critical and pharma cargo,” said Kadhir Kadhiravan, CEO of GMR Hyderabad International Airport Ltd (GHIAL), about the development.

title: Kallakurichi police serve summons on TVK MLA
description: Kallakurichi AWPS serves summons on TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh amid POSH case, with investigation under four sections and heightened police presence.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh in connection with a case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer.
Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Mr. Arul Vignesh at the house.
The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages.
The police have booked a case against the MLA under four sections including the POSH Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case registered at the Kallakurichi All Women Police station, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday (November 25).
The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry.
Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the Kallakurichi All Women Police station and the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

title: T.N. government accused of defying Supreme Court on ‘Karthigai Deepam’ lighting in Madurai
description: Supreme Court hears Deepathoon dispute as Hindu parties accuse the State of defying orders on lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The petitioners have accused the Tamil Nadu government of defying the Supreme Court order on lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp in Madurai’s Thirupparankundram.
Appearing before a Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan for the Collector said “unfortunately the lamp was not lit” at the ‘deepathoon’. A status report has been filed.
Also read: Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row updates
Earlier, the Supreme Court had permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the “Karthigai Deepam” lamp at the disputed hilltop Deepathoon (stone) pillar located near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah on November 24, strictly by an authorised team.
However, the ruling TVK government on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) defied the Supreme Court order, and the festival lamp was lit only at its customary place at Thirupparankundram.
Senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for the Hindu parties, countered during the oral mentioning that the State was resorting to “anticipatory mentioning against a blatant breach of the law”. He accused the State of employing “strategies and devices” to circumvent the Supreme Court order to light the Karthigai Deepam on the deepathoon on November 24, 2026, as a “one-time, limited arrangement”.
Mr. Krishnakumar submitted that the State and devasthanam colluded to justify non-compliance of the Supreme Court on the ground that Customs did not permit and that the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam (considered as a traditional place for lamp lighting), on the advice of the Sthanikars. However, Mr. Krishnakumar said the Sthanikars have denied giving such advice.
Mr. Krishnakumar urged the court that the lamp was still burning at the Deepa Mandapam and should be shifted to the hilltop Deepathoon immediately. He asked the court to hear the case in the afternoon, saying, “What is done is a complete infraction of the law.”
“You file the necessary plea. You take the steps… We will consider,” Justice Aravind Kumar said.
Advocate Jaya Sukin, for the Hindu Dharma Parishad, urged the court to take suo motu contempt against the State.
(With PTI inputs)

title: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, says Delhi police
description: Delhi Police says no permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march; organizers say they intimated police for a peaceful Constitution Day protest.
author: Lavpreet Kaur
content:
No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, scheduled for November 26, a senior New Delhi police told The Hindu. However, the organisers have maintained that they have intimated the police about the proposed demonstration.
The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform, a collective of multiple organisations opposing the voter roll revision exercise, has called for a peaceful march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg to Jantar Mantar, demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, among other demands.
Maimoona Mollah, a representative of People Against SIR, told The Hindu that an intimation letter had been sent to the Delhi Police regarding the march earlier this week. “We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” she said.
People Against SIR was formed in October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise.
According to information shared by the platform, participants will assemble at Valmiki Sadan at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 before marching to Jantar Mantar. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration.
The platform has claimed that more than 50% of the voters who were on Delhi’s electoral rolls in January 2025 and voted in the February 2025 Assembly election have either been deleted or categorised as doubtful following the revision exercise. It has also alleged that 13.3 crore voters have been removed from electoral rolls across the country since the SIR exercise began in Bihar last year.
The organisers have described SIR as an attack on the Constitution and the right to vote, alleging that the exercise disproportionately affects marginalised communities, including minorities, Dalits, transgender persons, women, migrant workers and the homeless.
The march will also demand the restoration of pre-SIR electoral rolls, no elections being conducted on the basis of revised rolls, impeachment and legal action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and the repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of election commissioners.
November 26 marks the adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949.

title: Missing BSF jawan’s body found in Kushiyara River in Assam after two days | India News
description: Constable (GD) K Venu, a resident of Telangana and posted at Harinagar Border Outpost (BOP) in Assam's Katigorah, went missing on Monday. | India News
author: Biswa Kalyan Purkayastha
content:
Missing BSF jawan’s body found in Kushiyara River in Assam after two days
Constable (GD) K Venu, a resident of Telangana and posted at Harinagar Border Outpost (BOP) in Assam's Katigorah, went missing on Monday.
The body of a 32-year-old Border Security Force (BSF) jawan who went missing while chasing suspected cattle smugglers near the India-Bangladesh border in Assam’s Cachar district has been recovered from the Kushiyara River on Wednesday morning, two days after the incident, a senior BSF official said.
Constable (GD) K Venu, a resident of Telangana and posted at Harinagar Border Outpost (BOP) in Assam's Katigorah, went missing on Monday. BSF Mizoram and Cachar Frontier deputy inspector general (DIG) Ahsan Shahedi confirmed that Venu’s body was recovered at around 8.20 am on Wednesday near Steamerghat in Sribhumi district, downstream along the river.
“Sad news. His dead body has been retrieved from River Kushiyara near Steamerghat, Sribhumi, after it was found floating downstream,” Sahedi said in a message to HT.
The DIG said the initial investigation suggests that there were no external injuries on the body. However, he added that the body will be sent to Silchar Medical College and Hospital (SMCH) for a postmortem examination.
The body will subsequently be taken to his home state by air, accompanied by BSF officers, where he will be accorded state honours.
The jawan’s disappearance had triggered speculation that he might have been taken into Bangladesh. However, the BSF denied receiving any such information from the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB).
“No, it is not true. He has not been traced yet. Comdt-level meetings with BGB also held but no positive outcome as yet. Search is still ongoing,” the DIG had told HT on Tuesday, responding to claims that the jawan was in Bangladesh.
The incident occurred early Monday near Harinagar BOP, when BSF personnel received specific intelligence inputs about the movement of four to five persons suspected of attempting to smuggle cattle through the border area.
Teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), river police, and BSF personnel subsequently launched a search operation in the river to trace the missing jawan. The search continued until his body was recovered on Wednesday morning.

title: Wedding turns into shootout in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh; one dead, another critical | India News
description: A marriage ceremony was underway at a hotel in Hazaribagh when a dispute broke out between the groom's side and the bride's side over an issue. | India News
author: Raj Kumar
content:
Wedding turns into shootout in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh; one dead, another critical
A marriage ceremony was underway at a hotel in Hazaribagh when a dispute broke out between the groom's side and the bride's side over an issue.
A wedding celebration turned into a scene of panic and bloodshed late on Tuesday night when indiscriminate firing broke out inside a hotel located at DVC Chowk in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh, people aware of the development said on Wednesday.
One person was killed instantly in the firing while another sustained critical bullet injuries. The injured person received first aid at the local hospital and was later referred to RIMS, Ranchi, where their condition remains serious.
According to preliminary information, a marriage ceremony was underway at the hotel when a dispute broke out between the groom's side and the bride's side over an issue. The argument escalated within minutes and turned violent, with gunfire starting soon after.
Chaos spread across the venue as soon as the sound of gunshots echoed, with guests, including women and children, running to save their lives. Tables were overturned, food was scattered, and the wedding atmosphere turned into fear and confusion.
Upon receiving information about the incident, local police arrived at the scene and took control of the situation. The hotel was cordoned off, and the crime scene was secured for forensic examination.
Police have started scanning the CCTV footage installed in and around the hotel to identify the shooter and reconstruct the exact sequence of events. Statements of the hotel staff, the wedding hosts, and the eyewitnesses are also being recorded.
Confirming the incident, Hazaribagh SP Aman Kumar said that a licensed firearm was used in the crime, adding that the accused has been absconding since the incident and that police teams are conducting raids at possible hideouts to arrest him.
The SP said the probe is ongoing and that all angles, including the reason for the dispute and the role of others present at the scene, are being investigated.
Police said the identity of the deceased and the injured will be shared after informing their families and completing legal formalities. The post-mortem of the deceased will be conducted to ascertain the exact cause of death.
The cops have appealed to the people not to pay attention to rumours and have assured that the accused will be arrested soon.
