title: India "Strongly Condemns" Riyadh Tower Attack That Injured 2 Indians
description: The MEA said such attacks endangered civilian lives, violated Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and undermined regional security and stability.
author: Asian News International
content:
India has strongly condemned the Houthi attack on a tower in Saudi Arabia's Financial District in Riyadh, which left 11 people injured, including two Indian nationals, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday.
The Ministry called for an immediate cessation of attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, while reaffirming India's solidarity with the Kingdom amid escalating regional tensions.
In an official statement, the MEA said, "We strongly condemn the attack on one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh on November 24 as well as the continued attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia."
Confirming that two Indian nationals were among those injured, the Ministry said the Indian Embassy in Riyadh was extending all possible assistance to the victims and their families.
"Two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh financial district. The Embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families," the statement added.
Our statement on the Houthi attack on Riyadh Financial District Tower ⬇️ 🔗 https://t.co/JczR8ZAEta https://t.co/orX07MfiHO
— Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) November 25, 2026
The MEA further said such attacks endangered civilian lives, violated Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and undermined regional security and stability.
"These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks," it said.
Reaffirming India's support for Riyadh, the Ministry said, "We also reiterate our firm solidarity with the people and Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and reaffirm our unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the security and safety of its citizens and residents. We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest."
The condemnation comes after Saudi Arabia's General Directorate of Civil Defence confirmed that 11 people were injured when one of the towers of the Financial Centre in Riyadh was targeted in what it described as a terrorist attack carried out by Yemen's Houthi militia.
According to the Saudi Civil Defence, those injured included two Saudi nationals, two Indians, three Nepalese nationals and four Egyptian nationals.
In a statement on X, the authority said emergency response teams immediately reached the location and implemented the necessary procedures to protect lives and property.
The official spokesperson of the Saudi-led coalition also confirmed that a Financial Centre tower had been targeted, describing the incident as a "cowardly terrorist attack". The spokesperson said relevant authorities were conducting an on-site investigation.
The incident comes amid escalating tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi authorities following allegations of Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on telecommunications infrastructure in Yemen's Al-Hudaydah Governorate.
In a statement posted on Telegram on Monday, Yemen's Houthi-controlled Ministry of Communications and Information Technology alleged that coalition aircraft targeted telecommunications buildings, workers' accommodation and a mosque in the governorate.
The ministry claimed that 17 workers were killed and 11 others injured in the strikes, according to an initial toll. It further alleged that several telecommunications facilities were destroyed, disrupting internet and communication services across multiple districts.

title: Where Is Sheikh Hasina Now? What We Know About Her Life In India
description: The former Bangladesh prime minister has been living in India since August 2024. Here's what we know about her residence, life in Delhi and return plans.
author: Amit Chaturvedi
content:
Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has announced that she will return to her home country on December 16, the 55th anniversary of Victory Day, which marks the end of a nine-month war that led to the country's liberation from Pakistan. Hasina has been living in India since August 5, 2024, following weeks of unrest that brought an end to her 15-year rule. She is believed to be living in a secure residence in Delhi but her exact residence has not been made public.
READ | Sheikh Hasina To Return To Dhaka On Dec 16, 55th Anniversary Of Liberation War
Hasina arrived at Hindon Air Force Station in Uttar Pradesh on August 5, 2024, aboard a Bangladesh Air Force aircraft.
In October 2024, reports citing people familiar with the arrangements said she was staying in a government-provided bungalow in the Lutyens' Bungalow Zone, a high-security area of the capital that houses senior officials and other prominent residents.
She has also been given tight security, though the details of the arrangements have remained largely private. Some reports have claimed that Hasina has round-the-clock security, with personnel keeping watch in plain clothes.
During her stay in India, Hasina has maintained contact with the outside world through interviews, statements and remote appearances.
NDTV was among the first news outlets in India to get an exclusive interview with Sheikh Hasina in June in which she had confirmed that she will return to Bangladesh this year. She had also asserted that her party Awami League is not just an organization but a "force".
"I do not fear death. In 1975, I lost my parents, my brothers, and almost my entire family. On 21 August, there was an attempt to kill me with grenades. Many conspiracies have been hatched against me. But breaking through every web of conspiracy, I stood beside the people of Bangladesh," Hasina said.
"I was elected Prime Minister five times by the people's vote and worked for the country's unprecedented development," she added.
A few months later, in September 2026, she told NDTV in another interview - this time on phone - that a death sentence order passed against her in Bangladesh is "politically motivated" and expressed a wish to play a central role in rebuilding the Awami League.
In August 2026, she addressed a press conference organised by the Foreign Correspondents' Club of South Asia in New Delhi through an audio link. Her son, Sajeeb Wazed Joy, also joined the interaction remotely.

title: Alice Huang-Linked Firms Listed $270 Million In AI Servers In China: Report
description: The central-bank documents identify up to 764 AI servers and modules valued at $270 million, along with $31 million in equipment used to connect them into large computing networks.
author: Reuters
content:
Companies linked to Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman whose affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang triggered his short-lived exit, raised financing against powerful computing equipment for major AI data centres in China, previously unreported records reviewed by Reuters show.
The central-bank documents identify up to 764 AI servers and modules valued at $270 million, along with $31 million in equipment used to connect them into large computing networks. Much of the hardware was listed as located at a sprawling Shanghai data centre originally developed under a partnership with Chinese technology giant Tencent.
The records show businesses connected to Alice Huang's family and associates helped finance and equip China's AI industry, even as US authorities investigated whether her Singapore-based company Megaspeed helped Chinese customers obtain restricted Nvidia technology.
The arrangements also illustrate how companies can finance access to the costly computing infrastructure underpinning China's AI ambitions, at a time when US restrictions on advanced processors have made securing the hardware a growing challenge for Chinese technology businesses.
On Monday, the US Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025.
Reuters examined dozens of filings in a Chinese central-bank credit registry that tracks equipment used to secure loans and other financing.
Alice Huang formerly controlled Megaspeed, a major overseas buyer of Nvidia processors. Her relationship with Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's CEO earlier this month before being reinstated to his post 11 days later, has intensified scrutiny of Nvidia's business links to China.
The records do not establish that the servers contained chips prohibited from export to China or show how and when the equipment entered the country.
Financing Hundreds Of Servers
A central business that raised financing was Century Litong, an Nvidia preferred cloud partner that rents powerful servers to customers needing large amounts of computing capacity.
Financial records show five leasing arrangements covering up to 512 servers with a declared value of 1.42 billion yuan ($200 million) between May and December 2024.
Four listed equipment at the Yangtze River Delta AI supercomputing centre in Shanghai, a $6.3 billion complex developed by gaming company Century Huatong, which counts Tencent as a roughly 10% shareholder.
Tencent and Shanghai's Songjiang district government announced a strategic partnership to develop the AI centre in 2020. A 2023 disclosure from Century Litong's JV parent company, Jiangsu Lettall Electronic, identified the centre as a location for Century Litong's server-rental business.
A Tencent spokesperson said Tencent never owned or operated the Yangtze River Delta Data Center Cluster Project, and that its name and trademarks had previously been used without authorisation.
The spokesperson added that the tech giant's investment in Century Huatong was for the gaming business and that it uses data centre hosting providers to support its services.
"Tencent has never entered into or otherwise had any commercial relationship with Megaspeed or any of its subsidiaries," the spokesperson said.
The records do not establish that Tencent bought, rented or operated the particular servers identified by Reuters.
One deal described 128 servers located at that data centre containing eight graphics processors each, or 1,024 chips in total, with computing power of "989 PFLOPs", valued at up to $450,000 apiece.
Another transaction involved 128 servers worth $57 million, financed by an arm of AVIC, a Chinese state-backed aviation and defence conglomerate, and leased to Century Litong.
Such arrangements allow businesses to obtain expensive computers without paying the full purchase price upfront.
A separate inventory listed more than 10,000 Nvidia ConnectX-7 networking cards and 730 BlueField-3 units at the Shanghai facility, equipment used to connect large numbers of computers for AI tasks.
Manufacturer Lettall Electronic invested in Century Litong in 2023 and took full ownership by mid-2024. Its disclosures show guarantees it provided for Century Litong's equipment-leasing agreements with financial institutions.
Nvidia, Century Litong, Century Huatong, Lettall and AVIC did not respond to requests for comment.
Family And Business Connections
Corporate records connect Century Litong, Century Longteng and Century Huatong to Alice Huang's sister, Huang Yu, and Kang Wei, an investment executive who is Alice Huang's husband. Alice Huang, Huang Yu, and Kang Wei could not be reached for comment.
Century Litong was initially established in 2023 as a subsidiary of Shanghai Century Longteng. The latter is now wholly controlled by Century Huatong, but a Shanghai state-backed investment fund and an investment company linked to Huang Yu and Kang previously held shares.
Kang was identified as Century Longteng's executive director in a 2022 government announcement.
Century Huatong also owns 70% of a company where Alice Huang previously served as a director, and holds a stake in gaming firm 7Road Holdings, whose former overseas subsidiary was renamed Megaspeed in 2023, corporate records show.
The network also developed a large data centre in Wuhu, about 300 km (186 miles) inland from Shanghai.
Wuhu Century Longteng, majority-owned by Huang Yu through investment vehicles until early 2026, pledged another 252 powerful AI computing "modules" to Ping An Bank as collateral for a $70 million loan in April 2026. The documents did not disclose the servers' location.
The dollar figures reflect the value of assets covered by financing arrangements, not necessarily new spending or distinct purchases.

title: Opinion | Indian Firms Are Making Record Profits. Why Are Foreign Investors Still Leaving?
description: In the July to September quarter of 2026-27, the 50 companies in the Nifty 50 increased profit after tax by 27% over the same quarter of the previous year - the highest growth in 17 quarters.
author: Aditya Sinha
content:
Opinion | Indian Firms Are Making Record Profits. Why Are Foreign Investors Still Leaving?
In the July to September quarter of 2026-27, the 50 companies in the Nifty 50 increased profit after tax by 27% over the same quarter of the previous year - the highest growth in 17 quarters.                        
In the July to September quarter of 2026-27, the 50 companies in the Nifty 50 increased profit after tax (PAT) by 27% over the same quarter of the previous year. Motilal Oswal Financial Services records this as the highest growth in 17 quarters. For its wider universe of 398 companies, PAT grew 32%, against an estimate of 21%. Estimates of Nifty earnings per share (EPS) have been revised up, to Rs 1,243 for 2026-27 and Rs 1,427 for 2027-28. Yet, according to the National Stock Exchange (NSE) India Ownership Tracker, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) held 14.7% of NSE-listed companies in September 2026, the lowest share in 21 years. The two facts have to be explained together.
Start with composition. Five companies (Reliance Industries, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, JSW Steel, and State Bank of India) contributed 46% of the incremental profit. In the wider universe, PAT in metals grew 78% and in oil and gas 55%. Much of this came from prices, not volumes. And prices revert. Nor is 27% exceptional in the world. FactSet's blended figure for the S&P 500 in the same quarter is 31.4%, the third successive quarter above 25%. UBS expects Korean EPS to grow 81.1% in 2026. India has had a good quarter in a year of good quarters.
What does growth imply? First, profits are a larger share of the economy than they have ever been. By Motilal Oswal's count, profits of Nifty 500 companies were 5.2% of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2025-26, a record, against 4.9% a year earlier. Those profits grew 15.6% in a year when nominal GDP grew 8.9%. Second, the multiple has compressed. By Bajaj Asset Management's count, the Nifty traded at 24.8 times 12-month forward earnings in September 2024. At the close of 25,144 on 13 November, it trades at 20.2 times Motilal Oswal's EPS estimate for 2026-27 and 17.6 times its estimate for 2027-28. Third, profits finance investment. Gross fixed capital formation grew 11.9% in real terms in April to June 2026, against 5.8% a year earlier. Retained earnings are the cheapest capital a company has. Fourth, the pace will not hold. Motilal Oswal expects Nifty earnings to grow 18% in the second half of the year, against 22% in the first. Its EPS estimates imply 14.8% in 2027-28. That is respectable. It is not 27.
What makes India enticing to a foreign fund? One, growth. Real GDP grew 7.8% in April to June 2026, and nominal GDP 10.3%. Two, external balance. The Reserve Bank of India reports a current account deficit of 0.5% of GDP for that quarter. Three, India is not the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. UBS computes that the top five stocks are 34% of the MSCI Emerging Markets Index, and that Taiwan and Korea together are about half of it. A fund that fears this concentration has few large places to go. Daily prices since January 2023 bear this out. On the worst tenth of days for semiconductor shares, Korea's sensitivity to the fall is 0.78, and Taiwan's is 0.54. India's is 0.03, statistically no different from zero. Between 6 and 30 October, semiconductor shares fell 19.1%, and the Nifty gained 1.2%. Four, the exit door. Individuals, directly and through mutual funds, own a record 19.5% NSE-listed companies. National Securities Depository Limited data show net FPI sales of about Rs 2.1 lakh crore in 2026, and the market still cleared. A market one can leave is a market one can enter. Five, positioning. At 14.7%, there is little left to sell. FPIs bought Rs 84,290 crore in the first fortnight of November. That buying followed the rout in AI shares abroad. It did not follow the earnings.
Is this shelter a stable proposition? It is not, for four reasons. First, the money came because AI shares fell, not because India changed. Since the chip trough of November 5, semiconductor shares have recovered 12.6% and Nifty 2.5%. Money that arrives on a rout can leave on a recovery. Second, entries move prices more than exits. From October 29 to November 12, about 8.9 billion dollars of foreign buying lifted the Nifty 10.3%, a little over one percentage point for every billion. In the ten months before, close to 30 billion dollars left, and the Nifty fell 12.2%, or 0.4 of a point per billion. Domestic funds absorb foreign exits. Nobody stands on the other side of foreign entries. Prices that rise on thin supply can fall the same way. The rally is also narrow. Banks rose 12% and the Nifty IT index 0.9%. Third, the shelter holds only when the fall is contained. Across the 17 sessions since 2023 when the broad American market also fell by more than 1%, the Nifty fell 0.46% on average. Fourth, the shelter is six months old. Before May 2026, the Nifty moved with the previous night's chip shares. A coefficient that changed sign in one year can change back in another.
That said, a quarter's earnings do not repair an economy's structure. Consider five problems.
First, the cost of capital. Even on 2027-28 earnings, a multiple of 17.6 is an earnings yield of 5.7%. The 10-year government bond yielded 7.31% on November 13. The domestic saver, investing through a monthly systematic investment plan, does not do this subtraction. The foreigner does. He then subtracts expected rupee depreciation, and a capital gains tax.
Second, oil. Dependence on imported crude was a record 88.7% in 2025-26, up from 85.5% in 2021-22. High crude lifts Oil and Natural Gas Corporation's profit. It also widens the merchandise trade deficit, which was 86.1 billion dollars in April to June against 68.9 billion a year earlier. A gain in one company's profit and loss account is a loss in the country's balance of payments.
Third, manufacturing. The government informed the Lok Sabha in August 2026 that manufacturing was 14.8% of gross value added in 2025-26. It was 14.7% in 2022-23. Three years have moved the share by one-tenth of a percentage point.
Fourth, the index itself. India's listed profits come from banks, oil, metals and cars. Few come from technology sold to the world. India spent 0.84% of GDP on research and development in 2023-24. That is one of the reasons why India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index fell from roughly 20% in mid-2024 to nearly 11% by May 2026, while Taiwan and Korea gained.
Fifth, numbers. Profits cannot grow at nearly twice the pace of nominal GDP indefinitely. A ratio at a record has less room above it.
The companies have done their part this quarter, with some help from the price of oil. But a foreign investor does not buy a quarter. He buys an economy. At 14.7%, he is telling us which of the two he has priced. The CEA is right when he said that India is going through the 1991 moment. It is an opportune time to push for more reforms. Most of this would be at the state level.
(The author was with the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister)

title: Stock Market News: This Small-Cap Stock Reported 38% Growth. Should You Buy?
description: Stock Market News: The company, which listed on the BSE and NSE earlier this month, benefited from higher volumes, and stronger demand.
author: Prateek Shukla
content:
Stock Market Today: Shares of Bombay Coated and Special Steels Limited are likely to remain in focus after the recently listed small-cap company reported strong growth in revenue and profit for the first half of the financial year.
The precision steel processing company said revenue from operations climbed 37.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 6,773.19 million in H1 FY27, while profit after tax surged 80.8 per cent to Rs 199.13 million.
The company, which listed on the BSE and NSE earlier this month, benefited from higher volumes, stronger demand from existing customers and lower finance costs.
Also Read | Layoffs Are Rising In Tech, But These Skills Are Helping People Unlock Better Pay
Volumes during the first half rose 15.8 per cent to 68,952 metric tonnes. Gross profit increased 25.9 per cent to Rs 851.22 million, while EBITDA grew 26.4 per cent to Rs 504.64 million.
The performance remained strong in the September quarter as well. For Q2 FY27, revenue jumped 50.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,802.38 million. Profit after tax rose nearly 40 per cent to Rs 48.38 million, while volumes increased 21.8 per cent.
The company derives most of its business from the home and commercial appliances segment, which contributed 86.9 per cent of first-half revenue. The general engineering segment accounted for the remaining 13.1 per cent.
Bombay Coated said it served 215 customers during the first half, with nearly 98 per cent of revenue coming from existing customers. The company caters to OEM and ODM clients across multiple industries.
The company also reported a decline in finance costs, which fell by Rs 20.76 million during the first half. This helped pre-tax profit rise 78.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 275.28 million.
Operationally, the company generated cash flow of Rs 184.62 million during the first half, aided by inventory optimisation.
Management said demand from appliance and engineering customers remained healthy despite a seasonally softer quarter for air-conditioner sales.
Managing Director Nitin Vijaykumar Gupta said revenue growth was driven by higher volumes and deeper engagement with existing customers. He added that new capacity additions could help the company benefit from rising demand from both appliance and automotive manufacturers.
The company is also using Rs 1,250 million from its IPO proceeds to repay debt. Management expects the debt-to-equity ratio to move closer to 1x from 2.48x reported at the end of September.
As part of its expansion plans, Bombay Coated has acquired additional land at its Ghiloth facility and recently took possession of a new industrial plot at Supa in Maharashtra. The site is expected to strengthen its presence in key appliance and automotive manufacturing hubs.

title: A Lamp, A Hill And History Dating Back To London's Privy Council Intervention
description: The dargah side maintains that it is the owner of the whole of the top of the Thiruparankundram hill and opposes the demand by Hindu worshippers for permission to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp.
author: Ashutosh Tripathi
content:
To light or not to light the ceremonial lamp (deepam) at a newly identified ancient stone pillar (deepathoon) on Thirupparankundram hillock, close to a dargah, or at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple in Madurai during the Karthigai Deepam festival is at the heart of a long-running dispute.
On Wednesday, the ceremonial lamp was lit as per the old practice at the traditional, and designated, Deepa Mandapam atop the Uchipillayar temple. Not at deepathoon, located just about 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah, which is now the demand and cause for renewed litigation.
This despite the Supreme Court last week permitting the lighting of the traditional deepam lamp on November 24 as a one-time measure at deepathoon. The top court said the permission granted by it - amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya dargah over ownership of the hilltop and the location of the ritual - cannot be relied on by any party as evidence of any established custom.
"The Karthigai Mahadeepam has been lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thirupparankundram," Tamil Nadu Law Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar posted on X.
திருப்பரங்குன்றத்தில் மூலவரின் சிரசுக்கு நேர் மேல் உள்ள உச்சிப்பிள்ளையார் கோயில் அருகிலுள்ள தீப மண்டபத்தில் கார்த்திகை மகாதீபம் ஏற்றப்பட்டுள்ளது… #ThiruparankundramDeepam https://t.co/qDKF9EXIP6
— CTR.Nirmalkumar (@CTR_Nirmalkumar) November 24, 2026
The dargah side maintains that it is the owner of the whole of the top of the Thiruparankundram hill and opposes the demand by Hindu worshippers for permission to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp.
The dispute was revived last year when the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, in its December 1, 2025 judgment, directed that the deepam be lit at the hilltop pillar, in addition to the customary location near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple. The court held that the hill belonged to the temple, except for the areas occupied by the dargah, the steps leading to it and the Nellithope area. A division bench upheld the direction in January 2026.
The Tamil Nadu government, then under the DMK, did not implement the direction, citing law-and-order concerns. The then government also disputed the very character of the pillar, arguing that it was a survey stone and that there was no historical record of it being used for lighting lamps. It further argued that the court could not dictate where a religious lamp should be lit, as the decision should be guided by religious and Agama practices.
The Madras High Court's judgment records that attempts to light the deepam at the hilltop location had been made as far back as 1862 and again in 1912. Both attempts were stopped by the authorities, who cited the absence of an established custom and the possibility of a breach of peace.
A 1923 Sub-Court decree recognised the temple's ownership of the hill, except for three areas belonging to the Muslim community - the dargah site, Nellithope and the flight of steps leading to the mosque. Though the Madras High Court had reversed the 1923 judgment three years later, the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London had restored the decree on an appeal filed by the temple. The Council ruled that the hill would be vested with the temple, and at the same time, it protected the dargah and the access steps to it.
There was also a similar dispute in 1996. The Madras High Court had then permitted the Devasthanam to consider lighting the lamp at an alternative location on the hill in future years, subject to prior permission from the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) authorities. The 1996 order directed that any alternative location for lighting the lamp must be at least 15 metres away from the dargah, the steps leading to it and the Nellithope area, besides places declared to belong to the dargah under an earlier civil court decree.
Earlier, the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department had strongly opposed the petition seeking the Archaeological Survey of India's (ASI) control over the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and the Thiruparankundram hill, as also changes in the traditional Karthigai Deepam celebrations.
In an affidavit filed before the top court bench, the HR&CE department had opposed the plea that had sought a direction to the ASI to take over the temple and the Thiruparankundram hill, saying the temple's ownership and the existing religious practices have been settled through decades of judicial proceedings.
HR&CE Commissioner TG Vinay had said the hill is owned by the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple, Thiruparankundram, to the extent recognised by a civil court decree of 1923 that was subsequently restored by the Privy Council in 1931.
The affidavit had opposed three reliefs sought by petitioner Hindu Dharma Parishad -- seeking the handing over of the entire temple and hill to the ASI, keeping a lamp burning round the clock at the stone pillar described as the deepathoon and illuminating the entire hill with lamps during Karthigai Deepam.
On the contentious issue of lighting the Karthigai Deepam, the HR&CE commissioner had maintained that the festival lamp has traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple and not at the hilltop or the stone pillar now being described as the deepathoon.
Opposing the demand for an ASI takeover, the commissioner had contended that archaeological protection at Thiruparankundram extends only to specified features, including the rock-cut cave and inscriptions, and not to the entire hill or the functioning temple.

title: "Not Today": Top Court Denies Interim Bail To Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid
description: The top court also directed that the matter be placed before the CJI on the administrative side for constitution of a three-judge bench for consideration.
author: Press Trust Of India
content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused, as of now, interim bail to activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid, who had challenged a Delhi High Court order denying them bail in a Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) case related to the alleged "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Delhi Police and sought its response.
During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Khalid, sought interim bail in the meantime.
Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Imam, also sought similar relief on grounds of long incarceration.
However, the bench said, "Not today".
It said it will hear the police before considering the prayer for interim bail.
The top court also directed that the matter be placed before the CJI on the administrative side for constitution of a three-judge bench for consideration.
In their pleas before the top court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and that the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry.
Violence erupted in northeast Delhi during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).
Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.

title: Kerala Woman Out On Bail In Drug Cases Attacks Excise Offier During Raid
description: A case has been registered against the woman under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act for possession of a commercial quantity of MDMA.
author: Aswin Nandakumar
content:
A woman with a history of involvement in narcotics cases was arrested with 11.465 grams of MDMA during an Excise Department raid at a private apartment in Thamarassery in Kerala's Kozhikode district.
The accused, identified as Zakira AK, a native of Thiruvambady, allegedly turned violent during the inspection and attacked a woman Civil Excise Officer, leaving her injured.
The seizure was made on Tuesday, November 24, during a joint operation conducted by the Thamarassery Excise Range and the Deputy Excise Commissioner's squad at a private apartment in Vendeckumukku, Kedavur, officials said.
A case has been registered against the woman under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act for possession of a commercial quantity of MDMA.
According to Excise officials, Zakira is an accused in multiple narcotics cases. She was previously booked in a case involving the seizure of 265 grams of methamphetamine under the Kalikavu Excise Range and another involving the possession of 3.06 grams of methamphetamine under the Kalpetta Excise Range.
She was out on bail in the earlier cases when she was arrested again with a commercial quantity of synthetic drugs.
The operation was led by Thamarassery Excise Range Inspector Sajin MJ and the Deputy Excise Commissioner's squad.

title: Just 2 Feet Tall, Worth Rs 1 Crore: Meet Pinky, The Tiny Buffalo Turning Heads At Pushkar Fair
description: Pinky, a buffalo just 2 feet tall, has become the surprise star of the Pushkar Fair in Rajasthan, with her owner quoting a price of Rs 1 crore for the rare tiny animal and drawing large crowds of curious visitors.
author: Nikhil Pandey
content:
At this year's Pushkar Fair, most visitors come to see tall horses, decorated camels and giant buffaloes. But one of the biggest attractions is among the smallest animals at the event. Her name is Pinky, a buffalo that stands just 2 feet tall.
Pinky has become the centre of attention at the Pushkar Mela, one of the world's largest cattle fairs. Crowds gather around her daily, with visitors stopping to take photos and videos. Many say they have never seen a buffalo so small.
Her owner claims Pinky is extremely rare. Because of her tiny size, calm nature and unusual appearance, he has valued her at Rs 1 crore. The figure was quoted by the owner and has not been independently verified. No buyer has been publicly identified.
Watch the video here:
According to her owner, Pinky is gentle and friendly. She stands quietly as visitors approach, and many children are drawn to her because she is almost their height. Some visitors have described her as the cutest animal at the fair.
Pinky is not the only unusual animal at Pushkar this year. The fair also features Punganur cows, which are around two-and-a-half feet tall, as well as large Murrah buffaloes weighing several hundred kilograms. Horses with asking prices running into several crores have also attracted attention. Even so, Pinky remains one of the fair's standout attractions.
Her owner says she receives special care, including a simple diet, clean water and adequate rest. He also says she dislikes loud noises, so she is kept away from drums and other sources of noise when she appears tired.
For many visitors, Pinky is a reminder that at Pushkar, it is not always the biggest animals that capture attention. Sometimes, the smallest ones leave the strongest impression.

title: Happy Thanksgiving 2026: Know Date, History, Significance And Celebrations
description: Happy Thanksgiving 2026: This year, Thanksgiving falls on November 26, marking a day of gratitude with meals and historic significance.
author: Abhinav Singh
content:
Thanksgiving 2026: Celebrated on the fourth Thursday of November every year, Thanksgiving is a national holiday in the United States. It is one of the most celebrated holidays across the country as families come together to prepare festive meals, enjoy time together and express gratefulness for the blessings. This year, Thanksgiving is being celebrated on November 26, which also kickstarts the festive season.
Thanksgiving: History
The origin of Thanksgiving dates back to 1621, when a harvest feast was held between the Wampanoag, a Native tribe who occupied the land long before, and the newly settled English colonists in America.
In 1789, following Congress' recommendation, President George Washington issued a proclamation naming Thursday, November 26, 1789, as a day of public Thanksgiving, the first time it was celebrated under the new constitution, as per the White House.
Later in 1863, Abraham Lincoln, the 16th president of the USS, who guided the country through the Civil War, declared Thanksgiving a holiday and a day off for employees. He also implored the citizens to heal its wounds and restore peace and harmony across the country.
Thanksgiving: Celebrations
Families and friends gather for a meal, play games and have fun on Thanksgiving Day. Pumpkin pie, cranberry sauce, mashed potatoes, stuffing, and roast turkey are all staples. Other customs of the day include Thanksgiving Day parades, especially the Macy's Thanksgiving Parade, donating essentials to those in need and the presidential turkey pardons.
On Tuesday (Nov 24), President Donald Trump pardoned two Thanksgiving turkeys, Freedom and Feathers, at a White House ceremony, sparing them from becoming part of the traditional holiday dinner.
In modern times, Thanksgiving is followed by Black Friday sales. As per some experts, the name Black Friday being associated with the holiday actually originated from frustrated factory managers in the 1950s. It is believed that a lot of workers would call out sick the day after Thanksgiving.
Thanksgiving: Wishes
Here is a list of Thanksgiving wishes and quotes to help you share joy on this day:
- Wishing you a Thanksgiving filled with love, laughter, and delicious memories.
- Give thanks not just on Thanksgiving Day, but every day of your life. Appreciate and never take for granted all that you have.
- Grateful for wonderful people like you in my life. Happy Thanksgiving!
- Happy Thanksgiving! May your day be filled with love, laughter, and a grateful heart.
- Happy Thanksgiving! May this day remind us of the blessings we often take for granted.
- Thank you for being part of my journey. Have a blessed Thanksgiving!
- May your heart be as full as your plate this Thanksgiving.
- Here's to the blessings we count today and the memories we cherish forever. Happy Thanksgiving!
- Family, food, and gratitude - may your Thanksgiving be as amazing as you are.
- Grateful for every moment we've shared. Happy Thanksgiving, dear friend!

title: UK Seeks To Change Age Of Consent After Russell Brand, Other High-Profile Cases
description: If the new laws are approved, it will make anyone 18 or older to have sex with individuals aged between 16 and 18, regardless of verbal consent.
author: Amit Chaturvedi
content:
The recent high-profile cases, including the conviction of Russell Brand for rape, have prompted the UK government to consider changing the legal age of sexual consent in the country. As per the BBC, the government of Prime Minister Andy Burnham has asked public to share its views whether or not to stagger the age of consent. Currently, the age of consent in the UK is 16 across England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. It applies equally regardless of gender identity or sexual orientation.
The call for revisiting the age of consent was given by activists who argue that different age limits should apply, depending on the age gap between people involved. In the case of Russel Brand, he was 31, while the woman he is accused of grooming and raping was 16.
The BBC further said that the UK government is also announcing new limits on non-disclosure agreements (NDAs).
Making a storng case for revising the NDA limits, Burnham said in a piece in The Guardian, "NDAs should protect sensitive business information or commercial interests. They should not protect powerful men who have abused, harassed or discriminated against women."
CBS News quoted British Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden as called incidents like Brand's "appalling stories of abuse of power by powerful men". He added that this warrants consideration of a new law.
McFadden said staggered age of consent is practiced by several other countries and the UK too will "discuss the approach".
Apart from Brand, who was convicted for 10-and-a-half years in prison, another British television personality David Walliams faced allegations of grooming young girls and harassing female colleagues. Both have denied all the allegatiosn against them.
If the new laws are approved, it will make anyone 18 or older to have sex with individuals aged between 16 and 18, regardless of verbal consent.
The UK is looking at other countries as it prepares to relax the age of consent. In Canada, for example, the age of consent for sexual activity is 16 but it varies in case of those under this age. In eight US states - Idaho, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, North Dakota and Florida - the age of consent varies.

title: Pak Space Agency Was Founded Before ISRO, But Then Lost Steam
description: Pakistan, despite its early start, has struggled to maintain momentum and remains heavily dependent on international partnerships for its most ambitious space projects.
author: Pallava Bagla
content:
As Pakistan sent its second astronaut, Zeeshan Ali, into space and its first astronaut to China's Tiangong space station, the mission is drawing attention not only because of its significance for Pakistan's future but also because of its remarkable past. Few people know that Pakistan entered the space age before India. Long before India's lunar landings, Mars mission and growing reputation as a major space power, Pakistan appeared poised to become South Asia's early leader in space science and technology. It established its national space agency before India, launched its first rocket before its neighbour and was among the earliest countries in Asia to engage in space research.
Yet history unfolded very differently.
Today, India stands among the world's leading spacefaring nations with achievements that include missions to the Moon, Mars and the Sun, a thriving launch vehicle program, a growing commercial space sector and an ambitious human spaceflight effort. Pakistan, despite its early start, has struggled to maintain momentum and remains heavily dependent on international partnerships for its most ambitious space projects.
That contrast makes Pakistan's upcoming astronaut mission particularly interesting. While it represents a major national achievement, it also highlights how two neighbouring countries that began their space journeys on similar timelines ended up on vastly different trajectories.
Pakistan's space story began in 1961 when it established the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, better known as SUPARCO. At the time, the world was still gripped by the excitement of the early Space Age. Yuri Gagarin had become the first human in space only months earlier, and nations around the world were beginning to explore the scientific and strategic possibilities of space technology.
India would not establish the Indian Space Research Organisation, or ISRO, until 1969, eight years after SUPARCO came into existence.
Pakistan strengthened its early lead on July 7, 1962, when it launched Rehbar-I from its Sonmiani launch site near Karachi. The sounding rocket was based on the American Nike Ajax system and carried out atmospheric research. The mission made Pakistan one of the first countries in Asia to launch a research rocket.
India followed more than a year later. On November 21, 1963, a Nike Apache sounding rocket lifted off from the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station in Kerala.
At that stage, there was little to separate the ambitions of the two nations that were pursuing scientific research, acquiring technical expertise and building their first generation of space scientists and engineers.
But the following decades would reveal a growing divergence.
India treated space as a long-term national investment and steadily expanded its capabilities. The launch of Aryabhata in 1975 marked India's entry into the satellite age. The spacecraft was launched by the Soviet Union, but its development helped establish the technological foundation for future Indian missions.
Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-1 in 1983, came much later. While it represented an important achievement for SUPARCO, it did not trigger the same cycle of technological expansion that Aryabhata did for India.
Today the difference in scale is dramatic.
India has launched about 140 satellites of its own.
These spacecraft support communications, navigation, weather forecasting, disaster management, military applications, scientific research and Earth observation. Satellite services have become deeply woven into India's economy and national infrastructure.
Pakistan has launched 16 satellites. Many have been developed through collaborations with international partners, particularly China.
The difference becomes even clearer when examining launch capabilities.
From its earliest years, ISRO pursued the difficult goal of building indigenous rockets. This effort required decades of research, repeated failures and sustained political support. The result was a succession of increasingly capable launch vehicles that transformed India into a self-reliant space launch power.
The Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3) was followed by the Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle (ASLV), then the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) and later the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) and the LVM3 heavy-lift rocket.
Over time, these launchers became the backbone of India's space program.
ISRO has conducted 107 rocket launches and has placed satellites into orbit not only for India but also for dozens of other countries. The PSLV in particular earned a global reputation for reliability and became one of the most trusted launch vehicles in the world; it even launched 104 satellites in a single mission.
Pakistan never developed a comparable orbital launch capability. As a result, the country remains dependent on foreign launch providers whenever it needs to place satellites into space.
The funding gap between the two agencies helps explain much of the difference.
SUPARCO operates with an annual budget estimated at $19.38 million. ISRO's annual budget is approximately $1.5 billion.
The disparity is enormous.
ISRO's larger budget supports launch vehicle development, satellite manufacturing, deep space missions, human spaceflight initiatives, scientific research programs and an extensive network of facilities across India.
By comparison, SUPARCO has had far fewer resources available to pursue similar ambitions.
Perhaps nowhere is the contrast more visible than in planetary exploration. India reached lunar orbit in 2008 with Chandrayaan-1.
The mission became internationally important after contributing to the discovery of water molecules on the Moon.
The finding changed scientific understanding of the lunar environment and elevated India's status in planetary science.
Fifteen years later, Chandrayaan-3 achieved another historic milestone by successfully landing near the Moon's south polar region. India became the first country to accomplish a soft landing in that area, which scientists consider one of the most promising regions for future exploration because of the possibility of water ice deposits.
Pakistan's first lunar mission came through partnership with China. The ICUBE-Q CubeSat travelled to the Moon aboard China's Chang'e-6 mission in 2024, marking Islamabad's first participation in lunar exploration.
Pakistan's ambitions are expected to grow further. The country plans to fly a 35-kilogram lunar rover aboard the future Chang'e-8 mission, one of China's key efforts to establish a long-term presence on the Moon in 2029.
India's ambitions have extended far beyond lunar exploration.
In 2014, the Mars Orbiter Mission or Mangalyaan, entered orbit around Mars and made India the first nation in history to reach the Red Planet on its maiden attempt. The achievement attracted global attention because it demonstrated that complex interplanetary exploration could be accomplished at relatively low cost.
India later set its sights on the Sun. The Aditya-L1 mission, launched in 2023, is studying solar activity and space weather from the Sun Earth Lagrange Point L1. The mission placed India among a small group of countries operating a solar scientific observatory in deep space.
Human spaceflight presents another striking point of comparison.
India's first astronaut, Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma, flew aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11 spacecraft in 1984. His mission to the Salyut-7 space station remains one of the defining moments in India's space history.
More than four decades later, India celebrated another milestone when Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew into space in 2025. At the same time, ISRO has been advancing preparations for the country's indigenous Gaganyaan human spaceflight program.
Pakistan entered human spaceflight much later.
On October 6, 2023, Namira Salim became the first Pakistani astronaut when she flew aboard a Virgin Galactic suborbital space tourism mission. Her journey also made her the first astronaut from Monaco and the first female astronaut from the UAE to travel to space.
On Wednesday, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the country's second astronaut and the first Pakistani to visit an orbital space station. He travelled aboard a Chinese Shenzhou-24 mission launched by a Long March 2F rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre.
The destination was China's Tiangong space station, one of only two permanently occupied space stations currently in orbit. The Pakistani and two Chinese astronauts safely docked with the Chinese space station, marking the first foreigner to visit the Chinese space station.
The mission reflects a broader reality about Pakistan's space future. Increasingly, that future is linked to China. Whether through lunar exploration, satellite development or human spaceflight, Beijing has become Islamabad's most important space partner.
The Shenzou-24 launch to the Tiangong mission will not erase the enormous gap that separates Pakistan and India in space capability. India remains far ahead in satellite deployment, launch vehicles, budget, planetary exploration and scientific infrastructure. But Pakistan can bank on China to help it, as they remain an "all-weather friend".
