title: JeM commander acknowledges terror network in Rawalakot
description: In a significant admission exposing the nexus between terror outfits and Pakistani establishment, Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) commander Masood Ilyas Kashmiri
author: Raj Shekhar Jha
content:
In a significant admission exposing the nexus between terror outfits and Pakistani establishment, 
Jaish-e-Mohammed
 (JeM) commander Masood Ilyas Kashmiri has publicly acknowledged the presence of his group’s armed terrorist network in Rawalakot in POK while alleging state authorities plan to target leaders of an ongoing regional protest movement.
Addressing a gathering in Islamabad, Ilyas also criticised Pakistan’s security and intelligence agencies, questioning their failure to identify individuals allegedly involved in anti-state activities as well as those accused of killing paramilitary Pakistan Rangers personnel during recent clashes.
The JeM commander went on to say that some of his group’s armed cadres belong to the same local communities that are participating in demonstrations being organised by Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), a civil society coalition that has led prolonged protests over economic grievances and governance in the region.
He said he had also met with Pakistani govt and security officials in Islamabad to clarify JeM’s position on the unrest. During his address, he alleged officials in Pakistan’s leadership had decided to eliminate both the leaders of the action committee and chief demonstrators in Rawalakot.
Ilyas previously drew attention in Sept 2025 when he was seen in a video addressing a gathering in Balakot and acknowledging significant losses suffered by JeM during Indian military strikes on May 7 that year under Operation Sindoor.
More than 150 people have died in the protests against Pakistani govt in Rawalakot in the last few months. Ilyas’s statement has brought govt’s role in the open.
Amid turmoil and rising casualties of peaceful protesters in Rawalkot and neighbouring regions of POK, JAAC had recently written to Field Marshal Asim Munir, demanding an immediate end to military operations.
The committee had emphasised that continued state violence will only widen the rift between the Pakistani military establishment and the local population, risking the transformation of a peaceful and democratic movement into a violent uprising.

title: Huang in there! Trump's bra-zen tribute to tech bro he rescued
description: TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump has never been one to let conventional presidential decorum get in the way of a provocative
author: Chidanand Rajghatta
content:
TOI correspondent from Washington:
 MAGA boss 
Donald Trump
 has never been one to let conventional presidential decorum get in the way of a provocative social-media stunt. So when Nvidia chief Jensen Huang returned to his corporate throne after an extra-marital affairs scandal, the US President, himself a seasoned veteran in this sphere, celebrated it by posting a meme of Huang waving a red bra in place of a clenched fist he (Trump) had raised after surviving an assassination attempt.
Trump was apparently having a laugh, but not everyone was amused. On CNN, Scott Jennings, the conservative commentator and Trump defender, was challenged by guest host Elie Honig to explain the image. Told to lighten up and that it was just a joke, Honig reminded him of Cory Comperatore, the man who lost his life during the assassination attempt and asked, "Do you think his family is laughing?"
For critics, the issue is not so much about Trump's bizarre sense of humour, but that the office of the presidency has become a social-media trolling operation. One angry reaction captured the sentiment with copulatory nouns and verbs, accusing Trump of having "degraded and debased the institution of the presidency" and lamenting a political culture in which billionaire interests seemed to matter more than public standards.
Others questioned what message the President was sending about fidelity and accountability. Here was a man with his own long and well-documented history of marital infidelity and sex scandals, making light of another powerful man's extramarital relationships. 
The objection was not necessarily that Huang should be denied a second chance. It was the apparent double standard: personal conduct that might have serious consequences for ordinary employees or executives was being transformed into a badge of masculine resilience when the person involved was sufficiently powerful, wealthy or strategically useful.
There was, meanwhile, another curious dimension to Trump's defence of Huang. Having pronounced him a patriot and a national asset, the president introduced an ethnic qualification that was distinctly less reassuring. Huang was born in Taiwan, and Trump suggested that, had Washington failed to bring him back, China might have recruited him to lead Huawei's AI operations. "He's got a little Chinese blood in him," Trump said, suggesting that if Huang had been treated badly, he might have been tempted by an offer from Beijing. It was an extraordinary observation, not least because it appeared to conflate ethnicity with national allegiance.
The controversy also exposed a more consequential contradiction within Trump's own camp. Several Republican lawmakers have questioned both Huang's reinstatement and the administration's intervention. Senators including Tom Cotton and Pete Ricketts have insisted that the company's national-security questions remain unresolved and that Huang must still answer congressional inquiries. The concerns relate not simply to his personal relationships but to possible exposure of sensitive American semiconductor technology to China.
Trump, however, has shown little inclination to follow the Republican establishment's preferred script. On China, as with Russia, he has resisted the hawkish instincts of his own party. On immigration, tariffs, foreign policy and even the conduct of the federal government, he has repeatedly departed from conventional Republican positions, often demanding that his party fall in line behind him.
The question increasingly being asked is not simply what Trump will do next, but what, if anything, constitutes a red line for him and for the Republican Party that has largely accommodated his instincts. If a president can personally lobby for the reinstatement of a billionaire executive facing national-security questions, dismiss the surrounding scandal as potentially good publicity and then celebrate the outcome with a lingerie meme built around an assassination attempt, what exactly is beyond the pale?
For Trump, perhaps nothing is. Every controversy is an opportunity, every outrage an audience, and every institutional convention another obstacle to be trampled, preferably with a camera rolling. The Huang affair is particularly revealing because Trump has managed to combine several presidential roles in a single episode: corporate dealmaker, national-security arbiter, moral relativist, ethnic commentator, and internet comedian. He has intervened in and influenced a private company's boardroom decision, vouched for an executive facing serious questions, and then turned the executive's sexual scandal into a piece of presidential entertainment. Even his most trenchant critics admit this: No one, absolutely no one, could have done this.

title: 'Wo paida hua hai samundar ke liye, abhi wo bas ek chote se talab mein hai' - The unprecedented rise of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
description: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is explosive, yet his movements are remarkably minimal.
author: Pratyush Raj
content:
NEW DELHI:
 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is explosive, yet his movements are remarkably minimal. Few batters have dismantled back-of-a-length and length deliveries down the ground with the kind of authority he has displayed over the last 18 months. He doesn't need a big stride or elaborate trigger movements to generate extraordinary power. Sometimes, all it takes is a shift in weight and those long levers.
On Tuesday, the last ball of the 10th over between India A and UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, when he brought up his 150 off just 40 balls, was perhaps the shot of the match. UAE pacer Zahid Ali bowled wide of the off stump, almost on the eighth-stump line. Sooryavanshi, with his long levers, transferred his weight onto the front foot and launched it over deep extra cover for six. A ball that was meant to keep him quiet was sent soaring into the stands.
In recent months, Sooryavanshi has left everyone scrambling for superlatives. But Bihar coach Ashok Kumar, who has worked closely with the teenager alongside Manish Ojha, believes the bigger picture is still waiting to unfold.
"
Badi machli hai aur talab chota hai uske liye (He is a big fish in a small pond)," Ashok told TimesofIndia.com.
"
Wo paida hua hai samundar ke liye, abhi wo bas ek chote se talab mein hai (He belongs to the ocean; currently, he is in a small pond)."
The evolution
Following Virat Kohli’s unbeaten 82 off 51 balls against Australia during the 2016 World T20, Australian cricket writer Gideon Haigh summed up the masterclass with a memorable line in *The Australian*: “Much as the marketers would like to take the cricket out of T20, Kohli keeps putting it back.”
Even in T20 cricket, the Kohli-esque style of batting was needed. It survived and thrived despite the 360-degree batting of exemplary players such as AB de Villiers and Suryakumar Yadav.
Vaibhav Sooryvanshi scored a a 53-ball 204 against UAE. (BCCI | X)
But on Tuesday, the way 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi batted, it looked to be a case of putting the T20 into an ODI, almost video game-esque. At his age, kids do spend a lot of time in front of screens. Vaibhav, however, was tearing helpless UAE bowlers apart in Doha.
"People complain that there are too many sixes and boundaries and that the grounds are too small. But the reality is that batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker," power-hitting coach Julian Wood told this website.
Look at Vaibhav in the IPL. He hit Jasprit Bumrah for six off the first ball and also hit Pat Cummins for six. It's almost as if there's a lack of respect, but he knows that if the bowler misses, he can hit him for six.
Julian Wood | Power-hitting coach
"If you look at Vaibhav's boundary-hitting patterns, he hits all around the ground, from mid-off all the way around to fine leg. If you're going to bowl wide to him, you'd probably have to bowl wide and full. But you have to execute that delivery perfectly. The problem for bowlers is that when they miss, the ball doesn't just go for four; it goes for six. That puts them under tremendous pressure.
"Look at Vaibhav in the 
IPL
. He hit Jasprit Bumrah for six off the first ball and also hit Pat Cummins for six. It's almost as if there's a lack of respect, but he knows that if the bowler misses, he can hit him for six. The mindsets of both batters and bowlers have changed. Batters now think, 'If he misses, I'm going to hit him for six,'" explained Wood.
Sooryavanshi now owns the record for the fastest 50, 100, 150 and 200 in List A cricket. 
Minimal yet so explosive
Zubin Bharucha, one of Sooryavanshi’s mentors, has explained how the teenager manages to hit length deliveries with extraordinary power. He attributes it to Sooryavanshi’s coiled upper body, deep torso bend and weight-loaded back leg, which allow him to get his head outside the line of the ball and bring deliveries outside off stump directly into his eyeline.
"What enables him to achieve this is a superbly coiled upper half, combined with a considerable bend in his torso at the top of his swing. This allows his head to get outside the line of most deliveries," Bharucha explained.
It is all driven by the hip not sliding forward, and this enables him to remain in such a strong coiled position on one leg, from which he can create that hip-and-shoulder separation and attack every ball.
Zubin Bharucha | Sooryavanshi mentor
With almost all his weight loaded onto the back leg, Sooryavanshi limits forward movement of his hips and avoids the conventional transfer of weight onto the front foot. His front foot often moves only marginally, remaining relatively unloaded, which allows him to finish shots with his foot flared open and ankle turned over.
"He is effectively operating on one leg, which in itself suggests the weight has to remain back," Bharucha said, explaining why Sooryavanshi can generate power without committing his weight forward.
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in action (BCCI | X)
The technique also allows Sooryavanshi to keep his body inside the line of the ball while his hands and bat operate in front of the stumps, a trait Bharucha compares with former greats Don Bradman and Graeme Pollock.
"This is driven by the deep bend in his back, which allows his hands to operate in front of the stumps, much like some of the greats of the past. They would stand well outside leg stump to ensure the bat operated in front of the stumps while the body remained well inside the line. This resulted in Bradman being dismissed LBW fewer than 10 times in his entire career, while players like Graeme Pollock never got out LBW at all. The deep bend in Sooryavanshi’s back accentuates this trait. Even though he doesn't take an outside-leg-stump guard, he is still able to achieve positions on the crease similar to those of these former greats," he said.
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 28-ball century surpassed Jake Fraser-McGurk’s 29-ball effort for South Australia against Tasmania in Adelaide in 2023
"It is all driven by the hip not sliding forward, and this enables him to remain in such a strong coiled position on one leg, from which he can create that hip-and-shoulder separation and attack every ball," he added.
Bharucha believes this allows Sooryavanshi to avoid committing early to a particular length and instead turn almost every delivery into a scoring opportunity.
Blessed with remarkable biomechanics
Earlier this year, after the second IPL playoff between Rajasthan Royals and Gujarat Titans in Chandigarh, Shubman Gill had called Sooryavanshi the "best T20 batter" in the world and explained how blessed the teenager was with his biomechanics.
Rajasthan Royals' Vaibhav Sooryavanshi during the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2026 Qualifier 2 T20 cricket match between Gujarat Titans and Rajasthan Royals, in New Chandigarh. (PTI Photo)
"I've not seen anyone bat like the way he bats, and I think in this format, he's right now one of the best batters in the world. It is just not his hitting, but his biomechanics and his hand speed, and, you know, no matter what opposition he plays against. I think, in the years to come, the opposition that he plays against is going to have a tough time against him," he had said.
Meanwhile, Julian Wood compares his bat swing with that of a baseball player.
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest to score a double century in all List A cricket,
"If you look at Vaibhav, the way his hands come up is very much like a baseball batter. His bat goes past the perpendicular, which is something you wouldn't necessarily coach. But he can generate serious bat speed. Because his bat goes further past the perpendicular, he has more room to whip his hands through the ball and generate speed," he said.
With his 53-ball 204 against the UAE, Sooryavanshi has rewritten the record books in spectacular fashion. Currently, he is not even a regular in T20Is, but he certainly is a big fish in a small pond. He should be thrown into the deep sea. And with age on his side, just imagine how many remarkable things he can do with his bat.

title: ‘Lamp could not be lit at designated spot’: Tamil Nadu govt apologises in Supreme Court, contempt plea to be heard in Karthigai Deepam row
description: NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday apologised before the Supreme Court over the failure to light the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at
author: Ayush Pandey
content:
‘Lamp could not be lit’: Madurai Collector tells SC, court agrees to hear contempt plea over Deepam row
NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday apologised before the Supreme Court over the failure to light the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai district, even as the court said it would hear a contempt plea alleging non-compliance with its directions.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said it would consider the contempt plea and peruse the status report filed by the state government on the developments surrounding the issue.The state government's counsel informed the bench that the traditional lamp had, unfortunately, not been lit at Deepathoon and that a status report detailing the developments had been filed.A senior advocate appearing for the petitioner seeking permission to light the lamp termed the developments "most unfortunate". He alleged deliberate non-compliance with the Supreme Court's directions and urged the bench to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the authorities concerned.
The petitioner's counsel argued that the flame should have been carried to Deepathoon and the lamp lit there. He also submitted that the state government had repeatedly assured the Madras High Court, until the last moment, that it would comply with the court's directions.
When the senior advocate indicated that the petitioners would move a contempt petition, the bench said, "File it, and then we will see."The Supreme Court asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications, assuring them that the matter would be heard.What happened at Thiruparankundram?The controversy centres on the traditional practice of lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon, a stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill. The Supreme Court had permitted the ceremonial lighting at the location on November 24 as a one-time measure.However, the lamp was not lit at Deepathoon on Tuesday evening. Instead, the Maha Deepam was lit at the Ucchi Pillayar temple.The Madurai district collector's status report informed the Supreme Court that the ceremonial lamp could not be lit at the designated pillar despite its directions. The state government has cited law-and-order restrictions and customary practices in opposing the lighting at the disputed location. It also told the court that the temple's Board of Trustees had not authorised the team tasked with carrying out the exercise.The dispute has triggered protests by Hindu organisations across Tamil Nadu, with demonstrators accusing the state government of disregarding the Supreme Court's directions. Several protesters were detained after road blockades in parts of the state.BJP targets INDIA blocBJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi on Wednesday accused the Tamil Nadu government and the INDIA bloc of failing to comply with the Supreme Court's order, calling the episode the "biggest constitutional contempt"."Today, I want to draw your attention to what we consider the biggest constitutional contempt committed by the INDI alliance Tamil Nadu government. On the occasion of Kartik Purnima yesterday, the Tamil Nadu government did not comply with the Supreme Court's order allowing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam for just one day, subject to certain conditions. They have neither followed nor implemented the Supreme Court's judgment," he said at a press conference.Trivedi also questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his repeated references to the Constitution, alleging that the party and its allies were not upholding the Supreme Court's directions."Eradication of Sanatan Dharma is motivated by the evil intention of the INDIA alliance," he said.
He further compared the controversy to the Shah Bano case, saying, "It will be another Shah Bano event of Congress alliance."Earlier on Wednesday, organisations including the Hindu Front and Hindu Munnani staged protests in several parts of Tamil Nadu over the non-lighting of the lamp at Deepathoon. In Ramanathapuram, police detained protesters who blocked a road, while members of Hindu Munnani staged a road blockade in Pollachi.
Ayush Pandey is a journalist at The Times of India, covering breaking news, politics, defence, and major legal and policy developments across India and the world. His reporting focuses on elections, national security, and institutional affairs, tracking the decisions and conflicts that shape public life. He specialises in sharp explainers and in-depth feature stories that go beyond headlines to decode political shifts, defence strategy, geopolitical flashpoints, and changing public sentiment. His work combines speed, clarity, and depth for a fast-moving digital audience.

title: Days after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for disruption in Outlook services globally, company declares 'Code Red' for its engineers; internal memo says ...
description: Days after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologised for a major outage that disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 265 services across the world,
author: TOI Tech Desk
content:
Days after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologised for a major outage that disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 265 services across the world, the company has declared ‘Code Red’ initiative which is aimed at overhauling its engineering, incident response and service recovery processes, as per the internal memos reviewed by Reuters. This move from Microsoft comes after the November 12-13 outage which impacted governments, businesses and consumers across multiple countries, including Australia, Japan and the United States. The service disruption affected Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services, raising fresh concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft also said that the incident was not caused by cyberattack or AI-related activity. Instead, the company attributed the outrage to an undetected Windows scalability defect which was introduced un July.
‘Most customer-impacting incident’ in Exchange Online history
According to an internal memo cited by Reuters, M365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online. "Never before had so many customers been without email for so long," Henderson reportedly told employees, emphasising that the Code Red designation represents the highest-priority work across the team.
The outage lasted nearly 24 hours and affected several core Microsoft cloud services, disrupting communications for enterprises, government agencies and other organisations that rely on Microsoft 365.
Engineers battled ‘fog of war’ during outage
In a separate memo on Monday, Amanda Silver, a corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, said engineers worked through a “fog of war.” Despite deploying top engineers, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and struggled to keep a clear picture of hypotheses and decisions, because diagnostic data was scattered across fragmented internal tracking systems.
Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures, according to Silver’s memo.
Microsoft targets one-hour global recovery
As part of the Code Red effort, Microsoft has launched several high-priority workstreams focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms.
The company has reportedly set an ambitious goal of resolving future global incidents within one hour. Microsoft also plans to use AI agents to help engineers analyse system health data and diagnose issues more quickly during outages.
Henderson is expected to conduct daily reviews with the leadership team overseeing Substrate, the engineering platform that underpins many Microsoft 365 services, alongside weekly progress assessments.
Internal review exposes broader operational weaknesses
Reuters reported that Henderson's review of the outage identified wider organisational and structural issues beyond the specific software defect that triggered the failure. In a separate memo reviewed by the news agency, Henderson said urgent patches for Microsoft 365 Core services were being deployed too slowly across global infrastructure.
He reportedly cited a separate recent incident in which a critical production fix required five to six days to achieve worldwide deployment. According to the memo, Microsoft aims to reduce the time between detecting urgent security issues and safely deploying fixes globally to just one hour. "Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday," Henderson wrote, according to Reuters.
Satya Nadella on Microsoft outage
Microsoft should have caught the software bug that took Outlook offline last week and had safeguards to contain the disruption, chief executive Satya Nadella has said. In an interview with CNBC’s Jim Cramer, Nadella said that the flaw surfaced only under a particular pattern of traffic. “Of course, we should have done the testing before,” he said. The outage disrupted email at businesses that rely on Outlook for day-to-day communication. Nadella said Microsoft should have designed its systems so that a failure in one part of the service could be isolated before it spread globally.
He also raised a broader problem for companies running older infrastructure. AI tools can help engineers identify software flaws and develop fixes faster, but each fix still has to be tested and installed. More frequent updates, he said, can make existing systems less stable. His comments pointed to a trade-off for software providers as they accelerate the release of patches while keeping widely used services online.
 "Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable," Nadella said. "I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet."

title: 'Always wanted Pat to remain captain': Usman Khawaja says he never intended to see Cummins punished amid sandpapergate fallout
description: Usman Khawaja has backed Cricket Australia's decision to retain Pat Cummins as Test captain amid the renewed controversy over the 2018 ball-tampering
author: Shubhanshu Dwivedi
content:
Usman Khawaja
 has backed Cricket Australia's decision to retain 
Pat Cummins
 as Test captain amid the renewed controversy over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying he never intended for anyone to face further punishment over Sandpapergate.
The controversy resurfaced after Khawaja alleged in his autobiography that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to tamper with the ball during the Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. Cummins denied the claims, and 
Cameron Bancroft
 subsequently backed Khawaja's version of events, saying "it was the whole team".
Khawaja, speaking on The Grade Cricketer podcast, said he was not seeking sanctions against anyone and was pleased that Cricket Australia had decided to stand by Cummins.
“That was never my intention to ever put ... we’ve had enough things in terms of punishments, that have already happened,” Khawaja told The Grade Cricketer podcast.
“The really good thing is Todd Greenberg (Cricket Australia CEO) said everyone pretty much has immunity. No one is going to get sanctioned or punished, Pat remains captain."
"This was never about me versus Pat, and I know that's what the media wanted, but that was never my goal or intention there," he said.
“I always wanted Pat to remain captain. It was never about Pat or Pat losing his captaincy.
“I reckon we’re in a really good spot now where it’s a bit freer and I can actually talk about this and I’m not worried about ‘oh I’m going to cook him’ or ‘I’m going to cook this person’. We can actually just talk about what happened.”
However, Khawaja said he was surprised by the extent of Cummins' fiery response.
"I've always loved him as a person and a leader - I was never expecting him to attack me personally like he did," he said.
"Attack what I said, yeah. Personally, the way he did it and kept going and kept going, I've never seen that side of Pat before.
"That disappointed me."
Khawaja also revealed he had reached out to Cummins before he spoke to the media for 70 minutes at Cricket Central in Sydney on November 13, in an attempt to find "middle ground". "I think people would have respected him for that."
He also criticised Cricket Australia for putting Cummins in that position in the first place.
"This is my issue - Pat was 24 at the time. This wasn't a Patrick Cummins issue," Khawaja said of Sandpapergate.
"This wasn't about Pat. I think someone at CA should have taken the lead, not Pat."
Cricket Australia last week expressed its "unanimous support" for Cummins to continue as Test captain, rejecting suggestions that his integrity had been compromised by the allegations surrounding the 2018 scandal.
Cummins had come under scrutiny after Khawaja claimed the entire team was aware of the plan to alter the ball. The Australian captain denied knowing about it during a press conference last week, but Bancroft's subsequent comments added to the controversy.
A Cricket Australia investigation into the incident had held only then-captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Bancroft, who used the sandpaper, responsible.
Khawaja reignited the debate through his autobiography, with Warner, his close friend, backing his claims. Bancroft later said "it was the whole team" and also expressed feeling "angry and betrayed" by Cummins.
Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation into the incident but has set up a forum for players to share their experiences of the 2018 episode.

title: A man named two relatives as beneficiaries of a $746,000 life insurance policy during Idaho divorce proceedings, then died in a mining accident; on November 23, judges revived his wife's claim to a share
description: A life insurance policy became the centre of a legal dispute after a man changed its beneficiaries while his divorce was pending and subsequently died in
author: TOI World Desk
content:
A life insurance policy became the centre of a legal dispute after a man changed its beneficiaries while his divorce was pending and subsequently died in a mining accident. Although his estranged wife was not named on the policy, she argued that she was entitled to half of its proceeds because the insurance benefits were part of their marital property.
In a November 23, 2026, 
decision
 in Ashlock v. Ashlock, the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit vacated a federal court judgment favouring the deceased man's relatives and reopened the wife's legal challenge. The ruling, available on Justia, held that a federal law exception allowing certain divorce-related orders to override Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) preemption can apply to employer-sponsored life insurance plans as well as pension plans. The court sent the case back for further proceedings to determine whether the wife's court orders qualify for that protection.
Husband named relatives as beneficiaries during divorce
Tina Ashlock and Jerry Ashlock married in 2009. Jerry filed for divorce in an Idaho state court in December 2020. During the proceedings, the court issued an injunction prohibiting either spouse from transferring property acquired during their marriage while the divorce case remained pending.
In March 2021, Jerry started working for Stillwater Mining Company in Montana and enrolled in an employer-sponsored life insurance policy issued by Life Insurance Company of North America (LINA). Despite the injunction, he named his relatives, Mary Ashlock and Brad Wilt, as the policy's only beneficiaries.
Jerry died in a mining accident in Montana in June 2021, before the divorce was finalised. Tina subsequently contacted LINA, claiming an interest in the insurance proceeds. The insurer rejected her claim because she was not named as a beneficiary and argued that ERISA prevented her from claiming the money under state community-property laws. In December 2021, LINA confirmed that it had distributed the entire $746,000 policy payout to Mary and Brad.
State courts recognised wife's 50% interest
Tina continued pursuing her claim through state courts. In September 2022, an Idaho court issued an order recognising her 50% community-property interest in the insurance proceeds. It also found that Jerry had violated the divorce-related injunction by naming his relatives as beneficiaries. The Idaho court deferred enforcement of Tina's interest to the Montana probate court, which subsequently adopted the findings and conclusions of the Idaho order and recognised her community-property interest.
Tina then filed a federal lawsuit against Mary, Brad, LINA and Principal Life Insurance Company. She sought a declaration recognising her entitlement to the proceeds and alleged unjust enrichment against the two relatives. She also brought an ERISA claim against the insurer, alleging that it had improperly denied her benefits. However, in July 2024, the US District Court for the District of Arizona dismissed her claim against LINA. It later entered judgment in favour of Mary and Brad, agreeing with the argument that ERISA's exception for qualified domestic relations orders applied only to pension plans, not life insurance policies.
Appeals court explains how QDRO protection applies
Tina challenged the federal court's decision before the Ninth Circuit. The central question was whether ERISA's qualified domestic relations order (QDRO) exception could cover welfare benefit plans, including employer-sponsored life insurance. A QDRO is a domestic relations order that recognises another person's right to receive some or all of the benefits under an employee benefit plan. Such orders can protect a spouse's or former spouse's interests in benefits during divorce proceedings.
The appeals court explained that ERISA recognises both pension plans and welfare benefit plans. The latter include employer-sponsored benefits providing accident, disability and death coverage. The judges held that the statutory language does not restrict the QDRO exception to pension plans. They also noted that several other federal appeals courts had previously reached the same interpretation.
Ninth Circuit sends case back for further proceedings
The Ninth Circuit vacated the federal district court's judgment and remanded the case for further proceedings. It instructed the lower court to determine whether Tina possesses a qualifying QDRO that entitles her to a share of the insurance proceeds.
The November 23 ruling does not itself award Tina half of the $746,000 or order Mary and Brad to return the money. Instead, it establishes that the QDRO exception can apply to the type of life insurance plan involved, allowing her claim to be considered under the correct interpretation of federal law.

title: Navy, Coast Guard helicopter acquisition puts Leonardo, Airbus and HAL in focus
description: The Indian navy and coast guard are preparing to acquire 76 Naval Utility Helicopters (NUHs) in a procurement programme estimated at around Rs 15,000
author: Dhruv Yadav
content:
The 
Indian navy
 and coast guard are preparing to acquire 76 Naval Utility Helicopters (NUHs) in a procurement programme estimated at around Rs 15,000 crore, with European manufacturers expected to emerge as the front-runners. The requirement comprises 51 helicopters for the navy and 25 for the coast guard, and is aimed at replacing the ageing Chetak fleet.
The purchase is likely to be made under the Buy and Make (Indian) category, which would require foreign original equipment manufacturers to team up with Indian companies for domestic production. The helicopters will be expected to handle maritime surveillance, reconnaissance, search and rescue, casualty evacuation and the transport of personnel and cargo. Operating from warships adds further demands, including limited deck space, folding rotor blades and the ability to withstand harsh sea conditions.
Among the possible contenders is Leonardo's AW169M. Italian firm Leonardo has announced a partnership with Adani Defence and Aerospace in February 2026 to build a helicopter manufacturing and maintenance ecosystem in India. The AW169M has been identified as one of the platforms for local production. 
The twin-engine machine has wheeled landing gear, folding main rotor blades and a compact layout suited to shipboard use, for easier stowage in the tight spaces on a ship.
Airbus Helicopters' H160M could also be in the running, though its weight may prove a hurdle. The military version is designed for troop transport, reconnaissance, special operations and armed missions, while its civilian predecessor has experience in offshore transport and search and rescue. Airbus could draw on its industrial tie-up with Tata Advanced Systems for local manufacturing. However, the helicopter's published maximum take-off weight of around 6,050 kg is above the 5,500 kg ceiling set in the August 2025 request for information, which could complicate its eligibility.
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited's Utility Helicopter-Maritime, developed specifically for naval operations, is another option. It is expected to have folding rotor blades, strengthened landing gear, corrosion protection and emergency flotation equipment. Its reported design weight of about 5.7 tonnes, however, also exceeds the RFI limit. The Navy is separately pursuing 60 UH-M helicopters, which is a distinct requirement from the 76 NUHs.
Leonardo's AW109 TrekkerM and Bell Textron's Bell 429 are other possible alternatives, though both would need closer scrutiny of their naval configurations. The AW109 TrekkerM uses skid landing gear in its standard form, while the Bell 429 is available with wheels. Shipboard compatibility, folding rotor arrangements and maritime operational qualifications would remain key questions for both.
The two forces will have differing priorities as the navy needs helicopters that can operate from frigates, destroyers and other warships, while the coast guard is likely to focus on maritime surveillance, search and rescue, medical evacuation and law enforcement support. The programme also comes amid a wider helicopter modernisation drive, with the Army and the IAF pursuing 400 light utility helicopters.

title: Bengaluru landlord refuses to rent flat to Shark Tank contestant despite IIT degrees, wife's Amex job and offer of 3 months' advance rent; know why
description: BENGALURU: An IIT Kanpur graduate and startup founder has sparked a discussion on the challenges entrepreneurs face while renting homes in Bengaluru after
author: TOI City Desk
content:
BENGALURU: An IIT Kanpur graduate and startup founder has sparked a discussion on the challenges entrepreneurs face while renting homes in Bengaluru after claiming that a landlord refused to rent his flat to him because he did not have a regular salaried income.
Aaditya Aanand, founder of Multibagg AI, shared his experience in a post on X, saying he and his wife had liked a flat during their house hunt but were turned down after the landlord learnt about his professional background.
Aanand said the landlord, a 50-year-old Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer, asked about his and his wife's professions. When he explained that he ran a startup, the landlord allegedly declined to rent out the property, saying he wanted tenants with a regular income.
The couple were particularly disappointed as they liked the flat and even tried to convince the landlord to reconsider, Aanand said. His wife suggested that the landlord could collect rent quarterly in advance if his concern was the possibility of delayed or missed payments. However, the proposal did not change his decision.
Highlighting their professional credentials, Aanand said he was an alumnus of IIT Kanpur, while his wife had graduated from IIT Kharagpur and worked with American Express (Amex).
Despite their educational and professional backgrounds, the couple struggled to find a suitable home because he had chosen entrepreneurship over a conventional salaried career, he claimed.
"Still we can't get a good place to live because 'husband' has chosen a risky career path," he wrote.
Questioning the gap between the public encouragement of entrepreneurship and the treatment entrepreneurs receive in everyday life, Aanand said people support startups in theory but are reluctant to accept the financial uncertainty associated with them when it comes to renting out their properties.
"People encourage entrepreneurship only in theory. In practice, nobody gives any f. Everyone wants safety," he added.
According to his X bio, Aanand is building Multibagg AI, a platform focused on equity research for Indian investors. He describes himself as an IIT Kanpur alumnus and a former Goldman Sachs professional, and has also listed his participation in Shark Tank India Season 5.

title: An Arizona woman lived with her partner in the same Phoenix house for 24 years, but he never divorced his estranged wife; after his death, an appeals court upheld the legal wife's ownership of the home
description: An Arizona woman who spent 24 years living in a Phoenix house with her partner has failed to secure ownership of the property after his death.
author: TOI World Desk
content:
An Arizona woman who spent 24 years living in a Phoenix house with her partner has failed to secure ownership of the property after his death. An appeals court has ruled in favour of his estranged wife, who had left the house nearly 25 years earlier but was still legally married to him.
According to the 
judgement
, the dispute centred on a house bought by Troy Torrence and Rita Mack in 1998. The couple purchased the Phoenix property together, with an arrangement that allowed the surviving owner to inherit the other's share.
Their relationship broke down the following year, and Mack moved out. However, the couple never legally ended their marriage or changed the ownership arrangement for the house.
In 2000, Dimica Hicks moved into the property with Torrence. She continued to live there until his death in September 2024. After his death, Hicks was appointed to handle his estate and approached the court seeking rights over the house.
Hicks argued that her long stay at the property and financial contributions towards it gave her a claim to ownership. She also sought repayment for expenses related to the house. However, a lower court rejected her ownership claim and later refused her demand for compensation.
The Arizona Court of Appeals has now upheld that decision. In a ruling filed on Monday, the court said Mack became the sole owner after Torrence's death because their joint ownership agreement remained in place.
Why the 24-year stay did not give her ownership
Hicks argued that she had lived in the house long enough to claim it through adverse possession, a legal route through which someone may acquire rights over property occupied for a specified period under certain conditions.
But the court found that the circumstances of her stay did not support such a claim. Hicks had acknowledged that Torrence had allowed her to move into the house and live there.
The court said this was important because her stay had begun with Torrence's permission. Her presence in the property did not establish that she had occupied it against Mack's ownership rights.
It also found no evidence that the original joint ownership arrangement between Mack and Torrence had ever been ended. Nor could Hicks show that she had taken exclusive control of the house in a manner that would support her ownership claim.
The fact that Mack had moved out did not automatically take away her rights over the property. Since she and Torrence had continued to own the house jointly, his death meant that his share passed to her.
This left Mack as the sole owner, despite having moved out decades before Hicks began living there.
Court rejects demand for money spent on house
Apart from seeking ownership, Hicks wanted Mack to repay money she said she had spent on the property. Her claims included contributions towards the mortgage, repairs and improvements, as well as other household expenses.
The lower court, however, found that Hicks had not established that Mack had unfairly benefited from her spending. The appeals court agreed that there was no reason to overturn this finding.
The earlier judgment noted that Torrence had also used his earnings and Social Security disability benefits to make some mortgage payments. Hicks had contributed towards the loan as well, but her payments were not consistent throughout the period.
The court also considered the fact that Hicks had lived in the house for several years. It found that she had received value from the money she spent because she had been able to use the property as her home during that time.
Her demand for compensation for mortgage payments and improvements was therefore rejected.
Appeals court upholds earlier ruling
Hicks challenged the lower court's decision on several grounds, including her claim that she had not been given a proper opportunity to question Mack during the trial.
However, the appeals court found that Hicks had not taken the required steps to bring Mack into the proceedings as a witness. She had neither included her in the list of witnesses nor taken steps to secure her appearance.
The court also noted that Hicks had not raised an objection during the trial. It therefore rejected her argument that she had been denied an opportunity to question Mack.
The appeals court further found that Hicks had not provided enough material to show that the lower court had made an error while deciding the case.
It ultimately upheld the earlier judgment, confirming Mack's ownership of the Phoenix house and rejecting Hicks's claims for ownership and compensation.

title: NDA-SAD reunion: Why the Akali Dal severed ties with BJP 6 years ago
description: SAD-BJP reunite after six years amid farm-law disputes, Punjab politics, and evolving Panthic influence shaping 2027 chances.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Six years after parting ways over differences on the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), have reunited ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections in 2027. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the development as an effort to place Punjab and the welfare of its people above all else.
Why did the SAD walk out of the NDA?
The SAD and the BJP had been allies since the late 1990s. However, amid widespread protests against the Centre’s farm laws, the SAD severed ties with the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in 2020. Subsequently, on November 19, 2021, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the repeal of the three farm laws.
The SAD exited the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal also resigning from the Union Council of Ministers in protest against the legislation, which sought to overhaul agricultural marketing and triggered months-long demonstrations at Delhi’s borders. Responding to questions about the party’s current stand on the farm laws, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) there was little relevance in revisiting the issue since the legislation had already been withdrawn.
The laws under contention were the Farmers’ Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020; the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020; and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020. Together, they sought to remove restrictions on the stocking, contracting and purchase of agricultural commodities.
Amid protests from Opposition parties and farmers, particularly in Punjab, both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha passed the Farm Laws Repeal Bill without discussion on the opening day of the Winter Session in December 2021. Subsequently, the Law Ministry notified the Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021, nullifying the three farm laws enacted by Parliament in 2020. The move came after President Ram Nath Kovind gave his assent to the Bill, completing the process of repealing the contentious legislation.
Opposition attacks renewed alliance
The Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) have criticised the renewed alliance, alleging that the two parties have put political convenience above Punjab’s interests.
Former Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring accused SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and former Union Minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal of presenting a misleading picture by publicly distancing themselves from the BJP while backing it on important issues in Parliament.
Mr. Warring contended that, despite their formal split in 2020 over the farm laws, the two parties had remained politically aligned and had now come together again after losing electoral ground in Punjab.
Describing the alliance as a “thaggjod” (an alliance of deceivers), Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann urged voters not to place their trust in the two parties again. He alleged that the previous SAD-BJP government, which was in office from 2007 to 2017, failed to curb the drug menace and did not act decisively on incidents of sacrilege reported in 2015.
A chance for SAD revival?
In Punjab, where Panthic politics, rooted in the collective identity of the Sikh community, continues to play a pivotal role, the revival of the alliance could benefit the SAD, which has struggled to regain its political footing in recent years.
Political observers believe that if the party’s core support base sees a realistic path to power in 2027 through its renewed partnership with the BJP, that perception itself could help draw voters back to the Sukhbir Singh Badal-led SAD.
Over the past decade, the SAD has witnessed a marked decline in Punjab politics, where issues linked to Sikh identity remain central to public discourse. At the same time, various Akali factions have competed to occupy the Panthic space.
In 2025, the SAD effectively split after a rebel faction launched a separate outfit, Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit). Separately, Waris Punjab De, led by independent Lok Sabha MP Amritpal Singh, who is currently lodged in Dibrugarh jail in Assam under the National Security Act, has steadily expanded its support base within the Panthic constituency. Observers attribute part of this rise to the weakening influence of the SAD.

title: SC issues notice to Delhi Police on pleas by Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case
description: SC notices bail pleas of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in UAPA Delhi riots case; hearing on interim bail after protected-witness issue.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) issued notice on the bail pleas of activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots. A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said it would consider their pleas for interim bail after hearing the Delhi Police.
Also read | The continued custody in Delhi Riots cases is an injustice
In their pleas before the top court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry.
The petition by Mr. Imam contended that the chargesheet was filed on September 25, 2020, in which 18 accused face trial and the prosecution has cited more than 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses.
Mr. Khalid, in his plea, also cited the failure to examine protected witnesses and said the expiry of the one-year embargo would mean that his continued incarceration would violate Article 21 of the Constitution.
Mr. Imam submitted that despite spending six years and nine months as undertrial, the prosecution has failed to examine even a single witness.
The Delhi High Court on September 30 refused to grant bail to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam in a case under UAPA on the “larger conspiracy” behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.
Observing that it was bound by “judicial discipline”, the high court said it could not modify the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which had asked the two accused to seek bail either after the examination of protected witnesses or the expiry of one year, whichever was earlier.
Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam challenged the trial court’s July 4 decision rejecting their bail pleas for the third time since their arrest.
The trial court had rejected the bail applications, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and, therefore, could neither entertain the plea nor grant any relief.
Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam have been booked under UAPA on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.
The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).
Activist Khalid Saifi and former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain, among others, were also booked for their alleged involvement in the larger conspiracy case, being investigated by Delhi Police’s Special Cell.
Mr. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Mr. Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.
(With inputs from PTI)

title: Seven Andhra fishermen safe; search for six missing off Odisha reaches Bangladesh, Myanmar waters
description: Six fishermen from Uppada in Kakinada district have been missing off Odisha since November 4; the search now reaches Bangladesh. Seven others stranded are safe.
author: G.V.R. Subba Rao
content:
Seven fishermen from Yetimoga in Kakinada district, whose boat broke down at sea after an engine failure, are safe, and efforts are under way to bring them ashore, Andhra Pradesh Minister for Fisheries Kinjarapu Atchannaidu said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
The boat is adrift about 3 km off the coast near Krishnapuram, on the Uppada-Tuni stretch. Since the water there is shallow, officials are arranging another boat to bring the fishermen ashore.
Mr. Atchannaidu praised the officials for promptly alerting the Coast Guard and the Navy after receiving information about the stranded boat. He said rescue efforts were being coordinated to ensure that all seven fishermen reached the shore safely, and urged their families not to panic.
Missing since November 4
Meanwhile, a search and rescue operation is under way for six other fishermen from Subbampeta in Uppada, Kakinada district, who have been missing at sea. The fishermen include Sorada Kondal Rao, Gumpala Prakash, Tirri Narayana, Sorada Chinna, Merugu Narayana and Kandala Ramu. They had sailed on November 4 on a boat owned by Garikani Simhadri along with another fishing boat, for the fishing grounds off Paradip in Odisha. The boats had gone about 200 km out from Paradip, according to their families.
The second boat returned on November 18. The families alerted the Coast Guard on November 19 and the search is being coordinated by the Coast Guard units at Kakinada and Paradip and the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Chennai. No trace of the boat has been found in the areas the families pointed out. The boat was carrying 1,500 litres of diesel and food for 30 days, but the fishermen’s mobile phones and the boat’s transponder have been switched off, so its position cannot be tracked.
The State government has written to the Centre seeking its help in the search, Mr. Atchannaidu said. Since the boat may have drifted off course, the search has been extended to the waters of Bangladesh and Myanmar. The authorities are in touch with representatives of the two countries, he said.
Mr. Atchannaidu said the safety of fishermen was the government’s foremost priority, and that every effort was being made to find the missing men. The government would stand by their families, he said.
Parivartan Rajaniti Party founder V. Vijayasai Reddy asked why successive governments in the State had failed to put in place a reliable tracking and emergency response system for fishing boats, and called for a long-term policy on the safety and livelihoods of fishermen.

title: HUMTA promises space in Hyderabad for pedestrians, other road users by 2050; identifies 120 locations for skywalks, FoBs and other infra
description: Hyderabad aims to be pedestrian-friendly by 2050 with 120 skywalks, FoBs, and integrated multimodal corridors, improving safety and access.
author: Serish Nanisetti
content:
Hyderabad is set to become a pedestrian friendly city by 2050. This was the plan laid out by B. Jeevan Babu, Managing Director of the Hyderabad Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority during the four-day Indian Roads Congress. For that date on the horizon, 120 locations have been identified for skywalks, Foot over Bridges (FoB) and other pedestrian infrastructure facilities.
Gaps in pedestrians infrastructure being examined
“The Comprehensive Mobility Plan for 2050 is nearing completion. Its scope includes assessing pedestrian infrastructure gaps and demand, walking access to [Hyderabad] Metro, MMTS, bus stops and terminals, road safety and pedestrian crashes, links to land use and activity centres, and investment priorities. The final report is expected in one or two months,” said Mr. Jeevan Babu, showing a presentation that showed the gaps and fixes proposed.
A few corridors for initial changes
“We have road space, but that is not properly used. The usability is divided. Pedestrian issues with roads are not properly addressed and vehicular movement is dominating the road. So, we are planning to have space for all. This will create development of roads hierarchy and usage. We have identified a few corridors for the initial changes,” he said.
A few locations which are nightmare for Hyderabad pedestrians
He shared two locations that are a logistical nightmare for pedestrians in Hyderabad: the Secunderabad Station and Rathifile Bus Station area, and another at JNTU and Lulu Mall area. Two other locations where skywalks are planned include the coaching centres zone in Dilsukhnagar and the IT workplaces in Hitec City.
1-km skywalk to connect Metro, railway and bus stations in Secunderabad
The intervention in Secunderabad — a 1-kilometre skywalk — will bring about an integration of the Secunderabad East and West Metro Station, the railway station and the three bus stations of Secunderabad, Rathifile and the Uppal bus station in the area. It will provide a continuous elevated pedestrian corridor reducing the number of people crossing the road and risking their lives.
“So, this is a concept of multimodal integration. This is to actually encourage people to use pedestrian infrastructure to reach from the railway station to their destination. And we are restricting people from spilling over onto the roads through design intervention,” he said giving an outline.
2.63 km intervention in Kukatpally
Similarly, the intervention in Kukatpally, albeit a longer one at 2.63 km, will connect the JNTU Metro station, JNTU campus and the neighbourhood commercial zones of Rythu bazaar and Lulu Mall.
“Rapid urbanisation and increasing vehicle ownership have created significant pedestrian safety and congestion challenges at major commercial and office zones like L.B. Nagar, Dilsukhnagar, Hitec City and Ikea Hyderabad. Existing pedestrian infrastructure is inadequate, resulting in unsafe at-grade crossings, traffic conflicts, and poor first-and-last mile connectivity,” said Mr. Babu.
Along with these interventions, new parking police, street design guidelines, multi-modal integration guidelines are also on the anvil.
“Ultimately, the vision and goal is to transform Hyderabad into an economically competitive, world-class, quality city with public transport-first approach and appropriate non-motorised transport facility for everyone,” said Mr. Jeevan Babu.

title: Workers in high-risk jobs to receive shots against rabies in Tamil Nadu
description: Tamil Nadu approves ₹2.22 crore PrEP rabies vaccination for over 1 lakh high-risk workers including sanitation staff, dog catchers, and animal handlers.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Over a lakh persons belonging to high-risk occupational groups, including animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies, in all 38 districts will receive Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) against rabies under the Tamil Nadu State Action Plan for Dog-Mediated Rabies Elimination (SAPRE) - Vision 2030.
The State government has given the administrative sanction for implementation of the initiative at a cost of ₹2.22 crore, which will be met from the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu, an order issued recently said.
The Directorate of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine noted that certain occupational groups are routinely exposed to dogs and other animals in the course of their duties. Provision of PrEP to such identified high-risk personnel will provide an additional layer of protection and strengthen the State’s rabies elimination strategy.
The programme aims to provide PrEP to identified personnel of occupational groups having sustained risk of exposure to dogs and other potentially rabid animals.
The main categories include sanitation workers, animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies and eligible personnel of the Animal Husbandry Department involved in animal handling, dog catching, veterinary and para-veterinary activities.
Eligibility criteria
As per the National Guidelines on Rabies Prophylaxis, eligibility will be determined based on occupational exposure risk and the nature of duties performed. Based on the presently available department data, the preliminary beneficiary estimation was 1,29,009 - 1,21,844 local body sanitation workers, 3,324 local body animal handlers/dog catchers and 3,841 personnel attached to the Animal Husbandry department, the directorate said.
The initiative will be implemented through designated government health facilities, including Primary Health Centres (PHC), Urban PHCs, government hospitals, and medical college hospitals. Identification of beneficiaries and mobilisation will be carried out by the respective local bodies and Animal Husbandry Department.
Published - November 25, 2026 05:45 am IST

title: Supreme Court 'inclined' to stay Calcutta HC order deferring Kolkata civic polls till decision on ward delimitation
description: SC inclined to stay Calcutta HC order, allowing KMC polls to proceed pending ward delimitation decision; delimitation may raise wards from 144 to 209.
author: PTI
content:
Stating that it shouldn't postpone pending elections "unreasonably", the Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said it is inclined to stay a Calcutta High Court order deferring the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) polls till the issue of ward delimitation is decided.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instructions on the issue by November 30.
The KMC has undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the next civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144.
The High Court had restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing a notification for the KMC election till a single bench disposes of a plea on ward delimitation.
"We are inclined to stay the impugned order for the reason that the factual and legal issues which have been highlighted, the division bench will pass a fresh order, an appropriate order.
"The writ petition before the single judge will be directed to be transferred to the division bench. And till the division bench forms a view the polls can be held off," the Bench observed.
During the hearing, Justice Bagchi said,""We shouldn't postpone pending elections unreasonably."
The division bench of the High Court had directed the State Election Commission (SEC) to not issue a notification for elections to the KMC till the disposal of a petition pending before a single bench.
Challenging the delimitation exercise, the petitioner, a former CPI-M councillor, sought a declaration stating that the entire exercise of determination of the number of KMC wards is void and the quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards is bad in law.
Dipu Das alleged that the delimitation exercise has been undertaken based on electoral rolls instead of the actual population, thereby excluding a substantial number of residents from consideration.
The petitioner claimed that the civic body had no elected council, and the corporation's former chairperson Smita Pandey had been appointed its administrator after the House's dissolution on June 8. He also sought an interim order of stay of operation of the delimitation notification and to restrain the SEC from issuing any notification calling an election to the KMC.
The single bench on October 29 refused an interim stay.
Aggrieved by the refusal, Mr. Das moved the division bench.
The State government, the order had said, could empower its chosen administrator to make a tailor-made recommendation and then be bound by it, effectively allowing the government to recommend amendments to itself and undermining the provision's independence.
"Such puppetry cannot be compatible with the scheme of the KMC Act. The key feature of Section 601 of the KMC Act is the institutional autonomy vested in the Corporation in making a binding recommendation to the state government, which confers authority on the Corporation, an autonomous institution, to decide the delimitation of its own wards, in other words, its electoral constituencies," the order said.
It stated that the manner in which the corporation was dissolved mid-term, and an administrator was appointed, followed by "the hasty chronology of events thereafter" lent substance to the appellant's arguments "that there might have been a method in the madness".
The observations made in the division bench order came with a rider that they were "tentative in nature insofar as the final disposal of the writ petition is concerned."

title: CJP’s Saurav Das moves Delhi High Court over being stopped from flying to U.K.; hearing on November 26
description: Delhi HC case: Saurav Das alleges immigration halt deprived him of a London/Oxford speaking engagement, seeking urgent hearing.
author: PTI
content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) approached the Delhi High Court after he was stopped from flying to the United Kingdom for an Oxford University event, where he was slated to speak on the "cockroach movement."
The plea was mentioned for urgent hearing on Wednesday (November 25).
A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said the matter would be listed on Thursday (Novembre 26).
Mr. Das has alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London.
"I was stopped at immigration. No order was shown to me. No LOC, no prohibition by any authority from letting me travel. I am seeking listing of a fresh petition today. I can still make it to the United Kingdom on November 27, which is where my arrangements are," Mr. Das's counsel submitted.
He said the flight is on Thursday (November 26). "Let it be (heard) tomorrow," the bench responded.
On Monday (November 23), in a series of posts on X, Mr. Das criticised the central government after being prevented from boarding his 1:00 a.m. flight to London.
"I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford. This cowardly government did not allow me to board my flight to London, where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE and Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement," Mr. Das said.
"Indian students put their heart and soul into organising the events, but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!" he added. Mr. Das said he had been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union for a panel discussion.
"And that's why I was going to London. But as soon as I went to the immigration check, I came to know that my passport has been flagged," he said.
"Why is the government so scared of an educated youth going among educated people and having an intellectual discussion? I wish I was Nirav Modi. I wish I was Vijay Mallya. I wish I had looted thousands of crores from the banks..." he said.

title: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Riyadh; New Delhi condemns strike
description: Two Indians injured in Riyadh Houthi attack; India condemns strikes on civilians and infrastructure, supports Saudi sovereignty, and calls for peace.
author: PTI
content:
Two Indians were among those injured in an attack on a financial district in Riyadh that triggered strong condemnation from New Delhi.
India also denounced continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
“Two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh financial district. The embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
The attack was carried out on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). Local authorities said the injured included two Saudi citizens, three Nepalese and four Egyptian nationals.
The MEA said India strongly condemns the attack in Riyadh as well as the continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. “These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks,” it said in a statement.
India also reiterated its firm solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed its unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity.
“We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest,” the MEA said.
There has been a sudden escalation in tensions in West Asia, especially after the Houthis carried out several strikes on Saudi Arabia.
The West Asia conflict began in February following attacks on Iran by the U.S. and Israel. New Delhi has consistently called for finding a solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.
India has been specifically voicing serious concern over the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s civilian infrastructure and economic assets, cautioning that such strikes undermine regional stability and threaten freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
