title: CJP's Saurav Das Approaches Court After He Was Stopped From Flying To UK
description: According to Saurav Das, he was served a show-cause notice a few hours before his scheduled departure and was subsequently prevented from proceeding with his journey.
author: Asian News International
content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das has approached the Delhi High Court challenging the authorities' decision to prevent him from travelling to London, where he was scheduled to deliver lectures at several prominent universities.
Das was scheduled to travel to London on an Air India flight from Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Tuesday at 1 am. However, he alleged that immigration officials stopped him from boarding the flight around 11 pm on Monday.
According to Das, he was served a show-cause notice a few hours before his scheduled departure and was subsequently prevented from proceeding with his journey.
READ | CJP's Saurav Das Stopped From Flying To UK Due To Birthplace Error On Passport: Sources
In posts on social media platform X, Das alleged that the authorities' action was aimed at preventing him from addressing students at foreign universities. He claimed that he was scheduled to speak about the 'Cockroach Movement' at the University of Oxford, Cambridge University, the London School of Economics and the University of Edinburgh, where Indian students had organised events.
Challenging the decision, Das has moved the Delhi High Court against the authorities concerned.
His counsel mentioned the matter for urgent hearing before a bench comprising Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma. The Court, however, said the matter would be taken up on Thursday.
Das has alleged that the decision to stop him from travelling was linked to his proposed engagements at the universities. The allegations are his own, and the authorities' response to the claims was not immediately available.

title: CAT 2026 On November  29: Check Paper Pattern, Marking Scheme, Exam Day Key Guidelines
description: CAT 2026 Exam: Registered candidates who have not yet downloaded their admit cards can download them from the CAT website using their CAT application login ID and password until November 29.
author: Rahul Kumar
content:
CAT 2026 Exam Day Key Guidelines: The Common Admission Test 2026 (CAT 2026) will be held on November 29 in three shifts across approximately 170 cities. To ensure the security of the examination, the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) have taken additional measures, including face matching and the deployment of mobile jammers at select locations.
A mock test with sample questions to familiarise candidates with the exam format and interface has been made available on the CAT website from November 6.
CAT 2026 Admit Card
With only a few days left for the test, registered candidates who have not yet downloaded their admit cards can download them from the CAT website using their CAT application login ID and password until November 29, 2026.
Candidates must download the admit card and print it on an A4-size sheet of paper. To avoid last-minute downloading issues, candidates are advised to download the admit card and print it at least two days before the exam.
The admit card contains key details such as the test date and shift, test centre address, and application number.
CAT 2026 Paper Pattern And Test Duration
The test will be 120 minutes long and will comprise the following three sections:
Section 1: Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension
Section 2: Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning
Section 3: Quantitative Ability
According to the information bulletin, candidates will be allotted exactly 40 minutes to answer questions in each section. They will not be allowed to switch from one section to another while answering questions in a section.
A mock exam to help candidates understand the test format and interface is available on the CAT website.
CAT 2026 Exam Day Guidelines
Candidates are advised to locate their test centre and check its accessibility at least a day before the test. This will help them choose an appropriate mode of transport and reach the test centre on time on the day of the examination.
- Candidates arriving late will not be allowed to enter the test centre and will be barred from appearing for the test.
- Before leaving for the test centre, candidates must verify and carry their original photo ID proof and CAT 2026 admit card.
- PwD candidates using a scribe should carry the scribe affidavit to the test centre. A sample scribe affidavit is available on the CAT 2026 website.
- Candidates must affix their photograph in the space provided on the admit card, as required, before reaching the test centre.
- Candidates must report to the test centre at the time mentioned on their admit card. On arrival, their admit card and photo ID will be scrutinised.
CAT 2026 Frisking And Document Verification
- Candidates should check the location of their test lab on the notice board using the application number printed on their admit card.
- Before entering the exam hall, candidates will undergo frisking. If any prohibited item is found, they will be asked to remove it, and undergo frisking again.
- In case of any argument or non-cooperation with the frisking staff, candidates may be asked to leave the test centre.
- Candidates must deposit personal belongings such as mobile phones, bags, wallets, jackets, jewellery, watches, electronic gadgets, and stationery items at the entry gate.
- Jewellery and other items containing metal are not allowed.
- Only the admit card, original photo identity card, and other necessary documents will be allowed inside the test lab.
- Socks, plain pullovers, sweaters, and cardigans without pockets are allowed.
- Candidates with metal implants, pacemakers or similar medical devices should carry a medical certificate along with the authorisation letter received from the IIM.
- There is no facility for safekeeping candidates' personal belongings outside the test lab. The test-conducting authority will not be responsible for any damage to or loss of such belongings.
- After frisking, candidates will proceed for document verification.
- The candidate's admit card with the affixed photograph, original photo identity proof and other required documents, if any, will be checked at the document verification desk.
- Candidates must carry any one of the original and valid government-issued photo identity documents along with the admit card: PAN card, Driving licence, Voter ID, Passport, Aadhaar card with photograph, E-Aadhaar, Ration card, other valid government-issued identification documents, where applicable.
- The photo identity proof must not be damaged or smudged.
- Candidates using a scribe must carry the scribe affidavit. Candidates with a pacemaker, metal implant or other medical device should carry the required medical certificate and authorisation letter.
- After successful document verification, candidates will be allowed to proceed to their respective test lab.
- Candidates are advised to take a bio break, if required, before entering the test lab.
CAT 2026 Registration And Biometric Verification
- After document verification, candidates will proceed to the registration desk.
- During registration, photograph and iris capture will be mandatory for all candidates. This will be followed by signing the attendance sheet.
- Candidates must ensure that there is no discrepancy in their signature on the attendance sheet, as it will be verified against the admit card and original photo identity proof.
- A scribble pad and pen will be provided for rough work. Candidates must mention their name and application number on the scribble pad provided to them.
CAT 2026 Computer-Based Test Instructions
- After entering the test lab, candidates will not be allowed to leave before the test ends unless a medical emergency arises.
- The exam lab invigilator will read out the instructions before the test begins. Candidates attempting to appear for the test more than once may face action as per the prescribed rules.
- Candidates must use the mouse to mark answers or the on-screen keyboard to answer non-MCQ questions. They must not use the physical keyboard at any point, as doing so will lock the computer system.
- Candidates must not disturb others. They will not be allowed to take a bio break unless there is a medical emergency. If a candidate takes a bio break for any reason, re-frisking will be conducted.
- Any time lost due to a bio break and re-frisking will not be compensated.
- The exam lab invigilator will instruct candidates to log in to the test screen. Candidates must use the mouse on their allocated system to log in and click the keyboard icon on the screen to use the virtual keyboard.
- After logging in, candidates must verify their profile information. If the details are correct, they should click the confirmation icon to proceed.
- The next screen will display the test-related instructions. Candidates should read the instructions carefully and click 'Next' to proceed.
- Candidates must then read and agree to the declaration by selecting the checkbox. The 'I am ready to begin' button will then be enabled. Candidates should click the button to start the test.
CAT 2026 Marking Scheme And Calculator Rules
- The computer mouse must be used to answer questions. Using the physical keyboard will lock the computer system.
- The test will comprise multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and non-MCQ questions.
- Unattempted questions will receive zero marks. For MCQs, an incorrect answer will result in a deduction of one mark. There will be no negative marking for non-MCQ questions.
- A virtual keyboard will be displayed on the screen for answering non-MCQ questions. Candidates must use the mouse to operate it.
- The use of an external or physical calculator is not allowed. However, candidates can use the on-screen calculator available on the test screen.
- Each section will be allotted 40 minutes, making the total test duration 120 minutes.
- PwD candidates will receive an additional 13 minutes and 20 seconds for each section, taking the total test duration to 160 minutes.
- The timer on the screen will display the remaining time for the section being attempted. Once 40 minutes are completed, the timer will reach zero, and the section will be locked.
- The 'Submit' button will be enabled. By clicking it, candidates will move to the next section. Otherwise, the section will be auto-submitted.
- Candidates are not allowed to leave the test lab before completing the test. PwD candidates may submit their answers for a section at any point between 40 minutes and 53 minutes and 20 seconds. Therefore, a PwD candidate may leave the lab between 120 and 160 minutes, depending on the time taken to complete the test.
CAT 2026 Answer Review And On-Screen Options
Candidates will have the following options while answering questions:
- Save and Next: Saves the answer and takes the candidate to the next question.
- Clear Response: Clears the selected answer for the current question.
- Mark for Review and Next: Marks a question for review so that the candidate can return to it later. The question may or may not be answered.
If a question is answered and marked for review, the answer will be recorded, and the question will remain marked for review. At the end of the section, it will be considered answered.
A panel on the right-hand side of the screen will display the status of questions using different colours:
- Green: Answered and not marked for review.
- Red: Visited but neither answered nor marked for review.
- Grey: Not visited or viewed.
- Violet: Marked for review but not answered.
- Violet with a green mark: Answered and marked for review.
Candidates can also view other details, such as the question paper. They can view the entire question paper for a particular section by clicking the 'Question Paper' button at the top right corner of the screen. The Profile option allows candidates to view their profile-related information on the right side of the screen.
The Instructions option allows candidates to view the test-related instructions at any point by clicking the 'Instructions' button at the top right corner of the screen.
The Calculator option allows candidates to use the on-screen calculator.
Candidates must not tear out or retain any page from the scribble pad after the examination, as doing so may affect their candidature.
CAT 2026 Score And Result
CAT 2026 scorecards will be made available on the CAT website. Candidates may also be intimated individually through SMS.
According to the information bulletin, CAT 2026 results are expected to be declared in the first week of January 2027.
The CAT 2026 score will be valid only until December 31, 2027, and will be available on the CAT website until then. After that, no queries related to the release of CAT 2026 scorecards will be entertained.
CAT 2026 Admission Process
Each IIM is independent in setting its own eligibility criteria, including academic cut-offs and relative weightages, and follows its own selection process.
Performance in CAT 2026 is a crucial component of the selection process. IIMs may also consider candidates' previous academic performance, relevant work experience, and other factors while shortlisting candidates at various stages.
For more details, candidates can refer to the admission policies of individual IIMs on their respective websites.

title: Tamil Nadu Blames Temple Board For Defying Supreme Court's Deepam Order
description: In a preliminary status report filed before the Supreme Court, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna gave an unconditional apology for the lamp not being lit at the 'Deepathoon' pillar on November 24
author: Debanish Achom
content:
The Madurai district administration has told the Supreme Court that the Karthigai Deepam ceremonial lamp could not be lit at the hilltop stone pillar in Thirupparankundram because the temple's board of trustees refused to allow a team for the ritual, deciding instead to stick to the traditional spot near the Uchipillaiyar temple.
In a preliminary status report filed before the Supreme Court, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna gave an unconditional apology for the lamp not being lit at the 'Deepathoon' pillar on November 24, while claiming that the revenue department and the police had no legal authority to step in once the temple trustees withheld their nod.
The row over lighting the lamp at the stone pillar next to a dargah on the Thirupparankundram hill has come as a challenging issue to solve for the Tamil Nadu government led by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.
The BJP has accused the state administration and its allies of acting against Hindu traditions after the state sought a review of the court's directions.
The Supreme Court had on November 20 allowed the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon as a one-time event between 6 pm and 6.30 pm on November 24. But the collector said in his affidavit that the court had directed that the lighting "shall be undertaken exclusively by a team of persons authorised by the Devasthanam" and designated him as the nodal officer to coordinate logistics and security with the temple's executive officer, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the police commissioner.
"There has been no wilful deliberate disobedience on my part of any directions of this Hon'ble Court. I hold the orders of the Hon'ble Court in highest respect and remain committed to comply with every direction this Hon'ble Court may issue. I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon," Krishna said in his report.
"The District Administration made every effort to secure the authorisation of the Devasthanam and the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon. However, the Board of Trustees, by its resolution dated 24.11.2026, resolved to light the lamp at the customary place," the collector said.
Explaining the sequence of events between November 20 and 24, the collector said he held three meetings with the police, revenue, Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR and CE) department and ASI officials to finalise every detail of the ceremony.
The temple's executive officer had even submitted a proposal on November 22 to deploy a 27-member preparatory crew at 6 am on the day of the festival, including scaffolding workers and two Deepam experts from Thiruvannamalai, followed by a 10-member lighting team led by two temple priests. To maintain law and order and ensure smooth access control, over 5,000 police personnel, 20 executive magistrates, medical teams and fire and rescue units were deployed on and around the hill.
The collector also defended his decision to impose prohibitory orders banning public assemblies and the climbing of the hill from the night of November 23 to the morning of November 25.
However, the plan ran into difficulties on the morning of November 24 when the preparatory crew did not go up the hill at 6 am. At 10.08 am, the collector emailed the temple's executive officer directing her to send the team immediately and explain the delay in writing.
She replied at 11.30 am that she had written to the temple's board of trustees seeking formal authorisation for the 10-member team and was awaiting their resolution.
That afternoon, the collector was summoned by a division bench of the Madras High Court in Madurai, which was hearing five petitions challenging the prohibitory orders. At 4.30 pm, the high court disposed of the pleas after reminding the collector, the police commissioner, the executive officer and the temple trustees that they were duty-bound to comply with the Supreme Court's order and that a pending review petition was no excuse for delay.
Minutes later, at 5.03 pm, the collector sent an urgent email to the temple administration stating that all observers and security teams were waiting on the hill and directed them to proceed immediately, while asking the state HR and CE secretary and commissioner to intervene.
Yet, no team arrived during the 6 pm to 6.30 pm window. At 8.30 pm, the temple's executive officer gave a report enclosing a unanimous resolution passed by the board of trustees stating that the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple follows ancient Agama rules and that "as per the practice followed from time immemorial, the Karthigai Mahadeepam is lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple on the Hill, directly above the head of the Moolavar, and that such age-old practices, customs, rituals and Agama rules are the unique religious identity of the Temple."
The temple priests had also lit the Mahadeepam at the Uchipillaiyar temple mandapam at 6 pm instead of the hilltop pillar.
"As the order permits the lighting at the Deepathoon only by persons authorised by the Devasthanam, and the District Administration has no power to authorise anyone in their place," the collector said, adding that at no point did the temple management communicate any authorisation to light the lamp at the stone pillar.

title: "Need Rahul Gandhi To Beat BJP": Congress MP Breathes Fire on Samajwadi Party
description: "SP is free to announce candidates for all 403 seats. What's the point of holding talks if you are going to release candidates?" Imran Masood asked in an angry interview with NDTV.
author: Tejshree Purandare, Mohd Asim
content:
First came the humiliation of the 'Special 26'wrapped as an offer, followed by the Samajwadi Party twisting the knife by announcing five candidates for the upcoming polls. The Congress is now fuming, and seat-sharing talks appear to have hit a dead end.
"We are not beggars," declared Congress MP and state working president Imran Masood, accusing the SP of acting unilaterally and showing little seriousness about the alliance.
"SP is free to announce candidates for all 403 seats. What's the point of holding talks if you are going to release candidates?" he asked in an angry interview with NDTV.
Masood, who represents Saharanpur in western Uttar Pradesh in Lok Sabha, has reason to be particularly upset. Among the five names announced by the SP on Tuesday night were candidates for Behat and Saharanpur Assembly seats - both constituencies the Congress was eyeing as part of the seat-sharing arrangement.
"Alliance candidates have to be decided mutually. You (SP) cannot unilaterally announce names while talks are underway. Does this show seriousness?" Masood asked.
#NDTVExclusive | "We are nor beggars": Congress MP Imran Masood amid seat-sharing row with Samajwadi Party @tejshreethought reports https://t.co/mLn8ZRXskD
— NDTV (@ndtv) November 25, 2026
He then accused Akhilesh Yadav of doublespeak, saying the SP chief's actions contradicted his public statements on social media.
"Akhilesh Yadav writes something on X and then behaves in the opposite manner. It appears that the SP is not serious about defeating the BJP," Masood said.
Read | Why Samajwadi Party Announced 5 Candidates Amid UP Seat-Sharing Talks
On Tuesday, Yadav posted what appeared to be an open letter calling for a better understanding between the alliance partners over seat-sharing.
Describing the upcoming elections as a "historic opportunity" to dislodge the BJP, Yadav called for "serious talks", taking public expectations and political realities into account.
"We want you and us to hold serious discussions, taking public expectations and realities into account, to ensure our 'alliance' wins in most constituencies. Among the seats you and we contest, the number we win should exceed the number we lose. Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect," he said in his post on X.
Masood also credited Rahul Gandhi with transforming the political landscape through his Bharat Jodo Yatra, arguing that the impact was reflected in the Congress's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. He also reminded the SP of its failure to defeat the BJP in 2022 despite having a broad alliance.
"What happened in 2022? The SP had the RLD and other allies, but it still could not win. Rahul Gandhi brought about the transformation, which was reflected in the 2024 results," Masood claimed.
Ramping up his attack, Masood said the Congress had shown considerable generosity towards the SP during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections by allowing it to contest more seats.
"Rahul Gandhi gave you more seats in 2024. He showed a big heart. It won't be possible to defeat the BJP without Rahul Gandhi," he declared.
Masood also made it clear that while the Congress was willing to be an alliance partner, it would not play second fiddle to the SP.
"We can be fellow travellers and allies, but we cannot be SP's followers. It's very clear," he said.
Read | Akhilesh Yadav Adds Insult To Injury, Congress Fumes As BJP Takes Potshots
Sources in the Samajwadi Party, meanwhile, blamed some "outspoken" Congress leaders for vitiating the atmosphere around the negotiations and forcing the party to release its list of candidates.
"Instead of reining in its outspoken leaders, the Congress has encouraged them. Some Congress leaders regularly make comments in the media to disrupt the alliance talks," an SP source claimed.
The remark appeared to be an indirect reference to Masood, who has been vocal about the Congress's expectations from the alliance from the outset.
SP sources also questioned the composition of the Congress committee tasked with steering the negotiations.
"When the SP included its most senior members in the committee, the Congress should have included positive individuals in its alliance talks team," a source said.
The SP, sources said, wants the announcement of five candidates to demonstrate both its preparedness for the elections and its position in the negotiations. The party believes that while it has shown its hand by naming candidates, the Congress has so far merely asserted its claims without disclosing the names of its preferred candidates.

title: Man Punches Co-Passenger On IndiGo Flight, Tries To Choke Him With Belt
description: As per the First Information Report, the accused was seated in seat 30D, while Yusuf was in seat 31B when the incident occurred.
author: Press Trust Of India
content:
A man was arrested for allegedly assaulting a co-passenger onboard an IndiGo flight from Abu Dhabi to Kochi, police said on Wednesday.
The incident occurred around 7 pm on Tuesday when the accused, Roshan Martin, a native of Vyttila here, allegedly attacked Yusuf, a Thrissur resident, onboard the flight (6E1404).
According to Nedumbassery police, Martin allegedly punched Yusuf in the face, breaking his spectacles and causing an injury near his right eye.
He also allegedly removed his belt and tightened it around Yusuf's neck during the altercation, police said.
As per the FIR, the accused was seated in seat 30D, while Yusuf was in seat 31B when the incident occurred.
Based on a complaint, police arrested Martin and registered a case against him under Sections 115(2) and 118(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
Section 115(2) deals with voluntarily causing hurt, while Section 118(1) pertains to voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt using dangerous weapons or means, police added.
Police said they would record the complainant's statement soon and take further action based on it.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

title: IIM Mumbai Opens Admissions For Advanced Project Management Programme, Check Details
description: IIM Mumbai Admission: The programme aims to strengthen participants' ability to apply contemporary project management practices across industries.
author: Aakanksha Singh
content:
IIM Mumbai: The Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Mumbai, in collaboration with Jaro Education, has opened admissions for the fourth batch of its Executive Certificate Programme in Advanced Project Management and Analytics, designed to equip professionals with the technical, analytical, and managerial capabilities required to navigate increasingly complex project environments.
In a press release shared with NDTV, the institute said that IIM Mumbai was ranked sixth among management institutions in India by the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) in 2024. "The growing complexity of projects across industries, coupled with the increasing adoption of technology and data-driven decision-making, is creating a greater need for professionals who can manage projects across time, cost, quality and performance parameters," it added.
Programme Details
Interested candidates can check the programme details below.
- Programme: Executive Certificate Programme in Advanced Project Management and Analytics
- Duration: 7 months
- Mode: Blended Mode (Live Online + Campus Immersion)
- Commencement Date: December 20, 2026
- Campus Immersion: 2 days of campus immersion (towards the end of the programme)
- Eligibility: Graduates (10+2+3) or Diploma Holders 50% only for 10+2+3) from a recognised university (UGC/AlCTE/DEC/AlU/State Government/recognised international universities) in any discipline with a minimum of three years of work experience after graduation or diploma holder with at least five years of experience.
- Programme Fee: Rs 2,20,000 + GST
- Application Fee: Rs 1,000 + GST
- Certification: 'Certificate of Completion' for the "Executive Certificate Programme in Advanced Project Management & Analytics"
The institute highlighted that according to a report by the Project Management Institute (PMI), the global economy is expected to require 25 million additional project professionals by 2030, while nearly 87.7 million project management-oriented roles are projected to be required globally by 2027.
At the organisational level, project planning and capability development are also emerging as key priorities, IIM Mumbai noted. A Quixy report found that 46 per cent of organisations identify project planning as a top priority, while 68 per cent place emphasis on developing project management skills to improve performance.
At the same time, project management practices are evolving with the wider adoption of Agile methodologies and analytics-led decision-making, the institute asserted.
IIM Mumbai Director Prof Manoj K Tiwari said, "As AI and generative AI increasingly become part of enterprise workflows, project management is also moving towards greater automation and predictive decision-making."
"This is creating a new requirement for project leaders who can combine domain expertise with data and technology capabilities," Tiwari added.
As per the official document, the programme combines project management frameworks with advanced analytics to help participants develop a structured approach to planning, execution, risk management, and performance improvement. It focuses on the knowledge, behavioural skills, processes, tools and techniques required to manage projects effectively in a dynamic business environment.
With faculty bringing extensive research and consulting experience in project management, the programme aims to strengthen participants' ability to apply contemporary project management practices across industries, the institute said.

title: Humans Could Live For 1,400 Years: Former Oxford Professor Nick Bostrom
description: Philosopher Nick Bostrom believes superintelligent AI could accelerate medical breakthroughs and help humans defeat ageing.
author: Ramarko Sengupta
content:
Swedish philosopher and former Oxford professor Nick Bostrom believes humans could live up to 1,400 years.
"If you think about what our life expectancy would be if we weren't aging, it's something on the order of 1,200, maybe 1,400 years or so," he said in a recent podcast, while discussing the potential benefits of successfully developing superintelligent AI.
That would be more than 11 times the age of the oldest verified human. The oldest verified human in recorded history, Frenchwoman Jeanne Calment, lived to 122 years and 164 days and died in 1997.
Watch our quick take:
So, 1,400 years, how exactly?
Because that totally sounds like Hollywood science fiction - think Adaline (The Age of Adaline) , Captain America, Wolverine. So, Bostrom's 2026 working paper, Optimal Timing for Superintelligence, lays out the assumption behind the calculation.
The idea mathematically revolves around the fact that if scientists could eliminate the biological process of ageing, people might no longer face the sharply rising risk of death associated with growing older. That way, their annual risk of dying could remain closer to that of a healthy young adult.
Bostrom uses the annual mortality rate of healthy people aged 20-25 in developed countries, which he puts at approximately 0.05-0.08 per cent.
He uses 0.07 per cent as an illustrative figure. If that risk remained constant throughout a person's life, the expected remaining lifespan would be approximately 1,400 years.
"If mortality were held constant at this rate throughout life, expected remaining lifespan would be approximately 1/0.0007 = 1,400 years," Bostrom explains in his paper.
To be sure, this is a mathematical projection based on a hypothetical scenario in which ageing is eliminated and the annual risk of death remains very low. It also does not mean people would be immune to accidents, violence or other causes of death.
Bostrom's argument is that superintelligent AI could accelerate scientific discovery, particularly in biology, medicine and anti-ageing research.
His working paper imagines a future in which AI could help scientists:
Develop treatments for diseases that are currently difficult or impossible to cure.
Reverse or repair age-related damage to cells and tissues.
Restore damaged organs and joints.
Develop more precise cancer treatments.
Tackle neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's.
"Superintelligence would be able to enormously accelerate advances in biology and medicine," he says in his working paper.
"Imagine curing Alzheimer's disease by regrowing the lost neurons in the patient's brain," he adds.
The idea is not that AI will magically discover a pill that makes people immortal. It is more about the fact that a sufficiently advanced AI system could help researchers understand complex biological processes, identify potential treatments, run simulations and accelerate experiments that might otherwise take years.
Ageing is not just wrinkles or grey hair - it involves changes at the cellular and molecular level, including accumulated damage, declining tissue function and an increased vulnerability to disease.
Where exactly are we on anti-ageing?
There is serious scientific work underway on ageing where researchers are investigating several possible ways to slow or even reverse aspects of the process.
A July 2026 review in Nature Medicine, titled Biological aging clocks in health and disease, discusses research into:
Cellular reprogramming: Attempts to reset aspects of a cell's biological state.
Senolytics: Experimental approaches aimed at removing senescent cells, which stop dividing but can contribute to inflammation and tissue dysfunction.
Thymus rejuvenation: Research into restoring aspects of the thymus, an organ involved in immune function.
Biological ageing clocks: Tools that attempt to measure how quickly a person's body, organs or tissues are ageing, rather than relying only on their date of birth.
The review explains that these clocks could eventually help researchers assess disease risk and whether interventions are changing the pace of ageing.
To be sure, these are research avenues, not proven routes to human immortality. Measuring biological age is not the same as reversing it, and showing that an intervention changes a biomarker is not proof that it extends human life.
A 2026 perspective in Nature Reviews Drug Discovery assessed the progress of AI in drug discovery and concluded that evidence of clinically relevant impact remains limited.
AI may be extremely useful in research, but translating computational discoveries into safe and effective medicines still remains a difficult process.
Could slowing AI development also cost lives?
Bostrom's comments are part of a broader argument in his working paper about the timing of superintelligence.
It's fairly common knowledge now that there are several researchers including heads of AI labs who have been arguing that the development of increasingly powerful AI systems should be slowed down until safety measures improve. Their concern is that an advanced system could behave in ways that are not aligned with human interests, potentially creating catastrophic risks.
Bostrom acknowledges the safety concern, but argues that there is another side to the calculation: the lives that could be saved if AI accelerated medical progress.
"Every year that we delay it, we have millions and millions of people dying," he says.
Bostrom is essentially raising the issue whether the risks of developing superintelligence should be weighed against the potential benefits of medical breakthroughs that could save lives today.
His paper uses a medical analogy: developing superintelligence is like a patient deciding whether to undergo risky surgery. Waiting could allow doctors to make the operation safer, but the patient remains exposed to the danger of the underlying illness.
"Developing superintelligence is not like playing Russian roulette; it is more like undergoing risky surgery for a condition that will otherwise prove fatal," the former Oxford professor says.
To be sure, his paper is explicitly labelled a working paper. The assumptions and risk calculations are part of his proposed framework, not a scientific consensus that AI should be developed faster.
The World Health Organization (WHO) says global life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023, while healthy life expectancy was 62.8 years. In other words, people are living longer, but they do not necessarily spend all those additional years in good health.
The WHO's October 2026 update also notes that non-communicable diseases accounted for 74 per cent of deaths globally in 2023. Dementia has become an increasingly significant cause of death.
WHO's Dr Alain Labrique says, "The next challenge is to ensure that those additional years are lived in good health."
While Bostrom's vision is extraordinary, the distance between today's medical science and a world where people live for 1,400 years is enormous.
There is no established treatment that can stop human ageing, and no evidence that current AI systems can deliver the kind of biomedical transformation he imagines.
The 1984 hit synth-pop track by the German band Alphaville seems more relevant than ever: "Heaven can wait, we're only watching the skies. Hoping for the best, but expecting the worst...
"Forever young. I want to be forever young. Do you really want to live forever?"

title: Stock Market Today: This Defence Stock Joins MSCI Small Cap Index. Should You Buy Now?
description: Sensex, Nifty News: Apollo Micro Systems will join the MSCI India Domestic Small Cap Index at the close of trading on November 30.
author: NDTV News Desk
content:
Stock Market News: A defence stock with a record order book, sharp revenue growth and a growing presence across India's defence manufacturing sector is set to attract fresh attention from institutional investors.
Apollo Micro Systems, the Hyderabad-based defence electronics company, will join the MSCI India Domestic Small Cap Index at the close of trading on November 30. The inclusion could trigger buying from passive funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that track the benchmark, putting the stock in focus ahead of the month-end rebalancing.
MSCI announced the changes as part of its November index review on November 11. The revised composition will become effective from December 1, 2026.
Also Read | Layoffs Are Rising In Tech, But These Skills Are Helping People Unlock Better Pay
For investors tracking the defence sector, the development comes at a time when Apollo Micro Systems is reporting strong growth in its business. But does the index inclusion, along with its latest financial performance, make the stock worth considering?
Why Apollo Micro Systems Is Entering The MSCI Index
Index inclusion can bring additional demand for a stock.
Funds that track the MSCI India Domestic Small Cap Index generally adjust their portfolios to reflect changes in its constituents. As Apollo Micro Systems enters the index, these funds may need to purchase its shares to align their holdings with the revised benchmark.
Such buying is generally expected around the closing hours of November 30, when the changes are implemented.
The inclusion can also improve the company's visibility among domestic and international institutional investors who follow MSCI indices. However, the actual quantum of buying will depend on the assets tracking the index and their portfolio requirements.
Apollo Micro Systems Reports 72% Revenue Growth
The index entry comes after a strong September quarter for the company.
Apollo Micro Systems reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 388.15 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 225.26 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. This represents a growth of 72.3 per cent.
Net profit increased 53.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 46.15 crore. The company's EBITDA, excluding other income, rose 87.8 per cent to Rs 111.18 crore.
The company also reported sequential growth, with revenue increasing 54.5 per cent over the June quarter and net profit rising 83 per cent.
For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations stood at Rs 639.44 crore, up 78.2 per cent from the corresponding period last year. Net profit increased 49.6 per cent to Rs 71.4 crore.
Rs 1,765 Crore Order Book Adds To Visibility
Apollo Micro Systems had a consolidated order book of Rs 1,765 crore as of September 30, 2026. The order book provides visibility into the company's ongoing business, particularly as defence projects move through different stages of execution.
The company is also looking to expand its presence beyond its traditional defence electronics business. Its subsidiary, Apollo Defence Industries, has signed a binding expression of interest to acquire up to a 26 per cent stake in A-Thon Allterrain, an Indian manufacturer of all-terrain utility vehicles.
The proposed transaction is part of the company's plans to expand its presence in land-based defence systems. Moneycontrol +1
Should You Consider Buying Apollo Micro Systems Stock?

title: UAE vs India Real Estate: Where Can Your Property Investment Earn More?
description: For Indian investors whose wealth is concentrated in rupee-denominated assets, overseas property can offer geographical and currency diversification.
author: Prateek Shukla
content:
For generations, buying property in India has been one of the most popular ways for households to build wealth. From residential apartments to commercial spaces and land, real estate has remained a preferred investment for Indians looking for long-term returns.
But as Indian investors become more globally connected, the investment conversation is changing. Instead of putting all their money into domestic property, many are beginning to explore opportunities overseas. The United Arab Emirates (UAE), particularly Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah, is emerging as one such destination.
The attraction goes beyond luxury homes and high-profile developments. Higher rental yields, exposure to an international property market and a currency linked to the US dollar are adding to the UAE's appeal.
Also Read | Layoffs Are Rising In Tech, But These Skills Are Helping People Unlock Better Pay
So, when it comes to making property investments, where does capital work harder: India or the UAE?
According to CA Ankur Aggarwal, Chairman and Founder of BNW Developments, the UAE offers Indian investors an opportunity to diversify their real estate holdings beyond domestic markets.
India Vs UAE: The Rental Yield Difference
One of the biggest factors influencing a property investment decision is rental income.
According to estimates by Colliers, residential rental yields in India generally range between 1.5 per cent and 4 per cent. Dubai, meanwhile, offers gross rental yields of around 6-10 per cent. For short-term rentals, the yields can rise to 10-15 per cent, depending on the property and location.
Ras Al Khaimah also offers an attractive proposition, with gross residential rental yields estimated at around 5.3 per cent.
The difference is significant. A property generating a higher rental yield can potentially provide investors with a stronger regular income stream.
However, these are gross yields. Actual returns can vary after accounting for maintenance, management charges, vacancy periods, service fees and other ownership costs.
Aggarwal believes that the UAE's rental market and growing international investor base make it an interesting destination for Indians looking to expand their property portfolios.
Why The UAE Is Attracting Indian Investors
The investment case for the UAE is not limited to rental income.
For Indian investors whose wealth is largely concentrated in rupee-denominated assets, overseas property can offer geographical and currency diversification.
The UAE dirham is pegged to the US dollar. This gives investors exposure to a currency framework different from the Indian rupee. However, currency movements between the rupee and the dirham can also affect the final investment returns when money is converted back into Indian currency.
Property ownership rules are another factor.
Foreign investors can purchase freehold properties in designated areas of the UAE. This provides an established ownership framework and access to the country's residential property market.
The growing participation of international buyers is also changing the market. In Abu Dhabi, resident expatriates and non-resident foreign buyers accounted for 70 per cent of residential property sales value, highlighting the role of overseas capital in the emirate's real estate market.
Branded Residences Add A New Dimension
Another trend attracting investors is the growing popularity of branded residences.
International hospitality and lifestyle brands are increasingly entering the residential real estate market. These developments combine private home ownership with hospitality-led services, facilities and management standards.
Dubai has become a major market for such projects. As of June 2026, the emirate had 183 branded residential developments.
Ras Al Khaimah is also preparing for significant growth in this segment, with approximately 10,000 branded residential units scheduled for delivery by 2030.
According to Aggarwal, the growing presence of international brands is adding another dimension to the UAE property market. Such developments can appeal to globally mobile buyers looking for a combination of residential ownership, services and lifestyle amenities.
However, the brand association alone does not guarantee better returns. Investors still need to assess the purchase price, location, rental demand and ongoing costs.
Can Buying Property In UAE Also Offer Residency?
There is another factor that could influence an Indian investor's decision: the UAE Golden Visa.
Under applicable eligibility provisions, property investors purchasing real estate worth at least AED 2 million may qualify for long-term residency in the UAE, subject to ownership conditions and other requirements.
This makes the investment proposition broader than simply buying a property and earning rental income.
For investors considering international business opportunities, lifestyle diversification or a longer-term presence in the UAE, the residency route could add to the appeal.
Aggarwal sees the UAE as a market that offers Indian investors a combination of international exposure, rental income opportunities and potential long-term value creation.
Where Should Indian Investors Put Their Money?
The comparison between India and the UAE is not necessarily about choosing one market over the other.
India continues to offer investors access to a large domestic property market, with opportunities across residential, commercial and emerging real estate segments. The UAE, meanwhile, offers geographical diversification, potentially higher rental yields in select markets and exposure to a dollar-linked currency.
The right choice ultimately depends on an investor's objectives, investment horizon, risk appetite and ability to manage an overseas asset.

title: Now Delhi Schools Can Reserve Parks For Just Re 1, Others Pay Up To Rs 5 Lakh
description: DDA has launched a single-window online park booking policy, allowing schools to reserve designated green spaces for just Rs 1 while opening 17 Delhi parks for cultural, educational and recreational activities.
author: Nikhil Pandey
content:
The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has introduced a single-window park booking policy to make its parks and green spaces more accessible to the public. Under the policy, citizens and institutions can book designated spaces for activities such as corporate events, film shoots and private gatherings. Parks have been divided into three categories based on their capacity, with booking charges ranging from Rs 3,000 to Rs 18,000 per day.
Popular parks, including Mehrauli Archaeological Park, Baansera and Asita, will have higher charges, while schools can book parks for educational and recreational activities for a nominal fee of Rs 1.
"Recognising the importance of outdoor learning and experiential education, DDA has provided for schools to book designated park spaces for Rs 1 for educational and recreational activities. These may include school picnics, painting and photography activities, debates, competitions and similar educational engagements," the statement said.
For an area of up to 4,000 square metres (sqm), the charges are Rs 3,000 plus GST for category A1, Rs 5,000 plus taxes for A2 and Rs 6,000 plus taxes for A3.
"For areas above 4,000 sqm and up to 8,000 sqm, the charges are Rs 6,000 plus taxes for A1, Rs 10,000 plus taxes for A2 and Rs 12,000 plus taxes for A3. For areas above 8,000 sqm and up to 12,000 sqm, the charges are Rs 9,000 for A1, Rs 15,000 for A2 and Rs 18,000 for A3, excluding taxes," the statement added.
The proposed centralised single-window online booking portal will be linked to the DDA website.
The parks can be booked for various activities, including yoga and meditation sessions, nature and heritage walks, poetry readings, book discussions, literary festivals, art and craft exhibitions, workshops, educational programmes and cultural performances.
However, political events and weddings remain on the list of prohibited activities in DDA parks.
Bringing the entire booking process onto a common digital platform, the portal will inform applicants about available locations, capacities, applicable charges and payment details, the DDA said.
According to officials, the initiative, introduced under the directions of Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, seeks to encourage citizens to experience and engage with nature beyond conventional recreation by providing opportunities to organise various activities.
The policy has identified 17 parks, including Swarna Jayanti Park, Rohini; Chitragupta Park, Rohini; G-8 Lake Park, Hari Nagar; District Park, Paschim Vihar; Sandesh Vihar, Pitampura; Lake Park, Pitampura; district parks in Dwarka; Indraprastha Park (Millennium Park); Sanjay Lake; Asita Yamuna Riverfront; Coronation Park; Astha Kunj; Hauz Khas Park; Baansera; and Mehrauli Archaeological Park.
At Baansera in Sarai Kale Khan, the lawn area at the café terrace, measuring 840 sqm, is available for Rs 10,000 per day in the non-commercial category, along with a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000. The Green Area Table Top Plateau, spanning around 12,000 sqm, is available for non-commercial activities at Rs 2.5 lakh per day, with a refundable security deposit of Rs 1.25 lakh. In Mehrauli Archaeological Park, three locations have been notified for booking.
"At the Charbagh Area near Quli Khan Tomb, spanning 14,200 sqm, the charges for non-commercial use are Rs 3 lakh per day, along with Rs 2,500 per day for installation and dismantling for a maximum of two days, and a refundable security deposit of Rs 75,000.
"For commercial use, the charges are Rs 5 lakh per day, along with Rs 5,000 per day for installation and dismantling, and a refundable security deposit of Rs 1 lakh," the statement said.
"In addition, designated amphitheatres at locations such as Indraprastha Park, Astha Kunj, Utsav Ground, Vasant Udyan, Tughlaqabad Recreational Park, Sanjay Lake and Coronation Park are proposed to be made available, subject to notified capacities and operational readiness," it added.
Special safeguards have been incorporated for ecologically sensitive locations, including Asita and Mehrauli Archaeological Park. Activities in notified ridge areas and protected forest areas will be restricted to sunrise-to-sunset timings, the DDA said.
The DDA has fixed location-specific booking charges for Asita at ITO. Its 'Water Body Lawn', measuring about 1,560 sqm, will be available for Rs 30,000 per day, along with a refundable security deposit of Rs 20,000.
GPS-tagged photographs taken before and after events will help ensure accountability and proper monitoring of site conditions, officials said.
Under the policy, the DDA has also allowed liquor consumption at its parks during events.
"Liquor consumption shall be permitted only where specifically declared in the booking application and expressly approved in writing by DDA, subject to applicable laws and regulations," the statement said.
The booking agency will have to obtain all requisite licences and permissions from the competent authorities and submit them to the DDA for verification.

title: Palestinians In Gaza Line Tents With Sandbags To Counter Israeli Bullets
description: Displaced families in southern Gaza are trying to find various ways to protect themselves as Israeli gunfire continues near their camps.
author: Kritika Bobal
content:
Palestinian families living in tents in Gaza are using sandbags to protect themselves from Israeli gunfire. They are filling empty flour sacks with sand and placing them around their tents to stop bullets from hitting their shelters.
This has become common in the Bir 19 camp in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, which is close to the area where Israeli soldiers are stationed. Families are placing sandbags on the sides of their tents that face the soldiers.
Nofal Al-Akhras, who lives in the camp, has also built a wall of sandbags outside his tent.
"Every day, around the clock, we are caught off guard by stray, deadly bullets fired indiscriminately," he told Drop Site News. He said many people have been killed after bullets hit their tents.
"We have lost many loved ones who were martyred by stray bullets striking displacement tents for no reason whatsoever. We had no choice but to collect empty flour sacks, as you can see, and fill them with sand to build protective barriers to shield our children, our families, and our loved ones from the stray bullets," he added.
Many other families in the camp are doing the same.
Tareq Abu Adhra has also built a sandbag wall with his daughter. His family had left Rafah in 2024 after the Israeli army asked residents to leave. They moved to what they thought would be a safe area but still faced gunfire.
He said bullets hit their tents and metal sheets every day. Some of their neighbours have also been injured or killed. People living in the camp have shown bullet holes in their tents and metal sheets. Some families have also built thick walls using iron rods, plastic sheets and sand.
"This is what life is like for us in Bir 19 every day. So we decided to build protective barriers to shield ourselves. When we go to sleep at night, we sleep behind these barriers out of fear of gunfire," Abu Adhra said.
Manar Abu Adhra has also lost her young daughter to gunfire. Her one-year-old daughter, Rafif, was killed by a bullet inside their tent on May 17.
"We go to sleep afraid that we might lose another child or that something might happen to us adults," she added. "At night, we move the children into this area so they can sleep behind the sand barriers we've built," she said.
On November 17, six-year-old Eyas Al-Namnam was shot dead inside a tent in central Gaza. According to his family, Eyas was eating and doing his homework when his mother asked him to go to his aunt's tent.
He was with his older brother and younger sister when Israeli forces opened fire, and a bullet hit him in the chest.
Israel, which accuses Hamas of trying to regroup and rearm, has stepped up its attacks in Gaza in recent months. Hamas denies the Israeli allegations, saying it is committed to the ceasefire agreement and accusing Israel of trying to derail it.
Israeli troops now control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory along Gaza's coast.
Israel's assault has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians since 2023 and has displaced Gaza's entire population.
Israel has said its actions were in self-defence after Hamas killed 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages in an attack on Israeli towns in October 2023.

title: Trump 'Reassures' Nvidia Of Jensen Huang's China Link. But He Has 'Xi' Concerns
description: Trump's explanation about his intervention in Jensen Hunag's reinstatement appeared to conflict with US intelligence's China espionage concerns and his own administration's action on the matter.
author: Sanstuti Nath
content:
Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia after an 11-day period of disorder that included his resignation and reinstatement following the admission of his scandalous affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy.
The 10-person board unanimously voted to rehire Huang as Nvidia's president, CEO and a fellow board member, writing in an announcement that the decision followed discussions with Huang and assurances "from senior levels of the United States government" that the 63-year-old co-founder's involvement posed no security threat.
US President Donald Trump himself has taken credit for pushing for Huang's reinstatement, saying he was vital for the United States' AI dominance. But during his latest interview with CNBC, Trump's own explanation about his intervention appeared to conflict with US intelligence's China espionage concerns and his own administration's action on the matter.
What Trump Said
Talking about his involvement in Huang's return to Nvidia, Trump told CNBC that the chipmaking company's board "did ask for assurance on the national security threat."
"We gave them assurance, at least with everything we know, and we know a lot. So with everything we know, we gave them assurance," he said.
But despite his repeated reassurance that Huang poses no security threat to the United States, Trump also implied he could take Nvidia's most advanced AI chipmaking knowledge to China if the US angered him.
"You know, Jensen could be angry at our country. He'd say, I'm going to go to China. Well, he's got the Blackwell in his brain. It's his baby. That's the thing," Trump said, even though Huang himself has never talked about moving to China.
Highlighting the risks of losing Huang's expertise to China, Trump said, "I know what President Xi is thinking because I would be thinking like, why don't we make a deal with Jensen? We don't have to bother with all the stuff. We don't need spies. Let's hire Jensen."
The Contradictions
Trump also implied that the Justice Department has cleared the Nvidia executive of personal wrongdoing. "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he himself was exonerated," he told CNBC.
However, despite Trump's tall claims, the embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees.
He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California's attorney general has opened an investigation into the company's chip exports and shareholder disclosures.
In parallel, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia's accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders.
The California Department of Justice has also announced that it is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public.
Nvidia itself is continuing its own internal investigation, even after Huang has been reinstated.
Though the ongoing probe into Huang and Nvidia's workings does not necessarily contradict Trump's claim, the scrutiny is far from closed.
Trump also dismissed the concerns regarding Alice Huang's link with the Chinese spy agency and said, "As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that's good-looking or beautiful, they say she's a spy."
The US Department of Justice is still investigating Alice Huang's link to Beijing and Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions.

title: Stock Market Rally: Sensex Skyrockets As Foreign Investors Pour Billions Into Tech Stocks
description: Sensex, Nifty News: The market rally came even as several Asian markets remained under pressure, with technology-heavy indices slipping.
author: Prateek Shukla
content:
Stock Market Today: Global markets often move in tandem, but Indian equities bucked the trend on Wednesday, drawing strength from an overnight sell-off on Wall Street. Investor enthusiasm around AI-focused stocks such as Nvidia and Anthropic cooled sharply, sending both counters lower and triggering a broader rethink of the crowded AI trade.
That shift appeared to benefit Indian technology stocks. As trading began in Mumbai, investors, particularly foreign institutional investors, rotated into companies such as TCS and Infosys, which have relatively limited exposure to the AI-fuelled rally that has dominated US markets in recent months. | FOLLOW LIVE MARKET UPDATES
The buying helped Indian benchmark indices post a strong start despite weakness across several Asian markets. The Nifty 50 opened 308.70 points, or 1.22 per cent, higher at 25,658.35, while the BSE Sensex rose 999.62 points, or 1.21 per cent, to 83,435.61. By 11:35 pm, Sensex had climbed 1,900 points to 84,345 while Nifty was up 559 points at 25,911. As a result, investors earned over Rs 4.2 lakh crore in just a few hours.
Also Read | Layoffs Are Rising In Tech, But These Skills Are Helping People Unlock Better Pay
Stock Market Today: All Sectors Rallied
Gains were broad-based. The Nifty 100 advanced 1.38 per cent, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 climbed 0.89 per cent and 0.48 per cent, respectively.
Market participants attributed the rally to sustained foreign inflows and a shift in investor positioning following the pullback in high-flying AI stocks overseas. With traders booking profits in some of Wall Street's biggest AI winners, part of that capital appeared to move into markets and sectors seen as offering more attractive valuations, providing an additional boost to Indian equities.
Share Market Rally Today: Why India Is Benefiting From The AI Pullback
The contrast between Wall Street and Dalal Street has become increasingly visible in recent weeks.
Overnight, US markets came under pressure as investors extended their sell-off in AI-linked stocks. Nvidia fell nearly 6 per cent, while several semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies across the US and Asia also declined as investors questioned whether the enormous sums being spent on data centres and AI infrastructure will generate returns quickly enough to justify current valuations. The Nasdaq ended lower, and technology-heavy markets such as South Korea, Taiwan and Japan also came under pressure.
India's technology sector occupies a very different position in the AI ecosystem.
Unlike Nvidia, AMD or other AI infrastructure companies that are investing heavily in chips and data centres, Indian IT firms such as Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, HCLTech and Wipro largely operate asset-light services businesses. They help companies deploy and manage technology rather than fund expensive AI infrastructure themselves. As a result, investors increasingly view them as relatively insulated from any slowdown in AI spending while still being positioned to benefit if enterprises continue adopting AI tools.
"Global investors are rotating money out of expensive AI and semiconductor stocks and into traditional software and IT services companies with stronger cash flows, lower capital expenditure requirements and more attractive valuations. This trend has helped Indian IT stocks outperform even as technology shares elsewhere have struggled," stock market expert Nidhi Sharma told NDTV.
She further said, "The shift is also showing up in foreign flows. Overseas investors have poured record amounts of money into Indian equities this month, with inflows exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore and crossing $13 billion, providing a powerful tailwind for domestic markets."

title: California Braces For Flooding Threat From Huge Tides, El Nino
description: The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, which forecasters warned could push seawater into low-lying areas on Wednesday and Thursday.
author: Agence France Presse
content:
Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fueled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding during the busiest US travel week of the year.
The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, which forecasters warned could push seawater into low-lying areas on Wednesday and Thursday.
San Francisco International Airport officials said its runways were no longer at risk of flooding, but authorities still urged residents to reconsider travel plans during the Thanksgiving holiday week.
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie warned the situation was "extremely serious."
Tuesday afternoon, he implored people to avoid driving through flooding that could be triggered by incoming rain that's expected to start Tuesday evening.
"Do not drive through floodwaters," the mayor said. "We are hoping by the mid- to late afternoon the tides will have subsided considerably."
So-called king tides occur every year due to the gravitational pull and alignments of the Earth, Moon and Sun. They will occur again in December and January.
The ocean is also hotter than usual -- and thus increasing in volume -- both due to human-caused climate change and this year's exceptionally strong El Nino weather pattern.
The ocean warming phenomenon in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific has already altered weather around the world, resulting in devastating droughts and wildfires.
Dial Hoang at the National Weather Service (NWS) told AFP that the Bay Area could see up to nearly three feet of flooding when the tides peak Wednesday.
The agency said in a bulletin that dangerously large breaking waves up to 30 feet could hit California's coast on Wednesday, with hazardous beach conditions persisting through Sunday.
Just The Beginning
This year's tides are predicted to be at their highest levels since January 1983, Hoang said.
Those tides also coincided with vicious, El Nino-fueled storms -- and the impact was catastrophic.
"All hell broke loose," said Reinhard Flick, a coastal oceanographer at University of California, San Diego's Scripps Institution. "We had 13-foot waves offshore, the highest tides of the year, and hundreds of millions of dollars in damage."
The state might not see the same level of destruction this week, thanks to storm preparedness and infrastructure improvements.
Dangers still remain. Strong winds could fell trees, Mayor Lurie warned, and "low-lying streets along the waterfront can flood with little to no rain."
After a storm caused major flooding across San Francisco last week, residents and business owners were anxiously preparing for another possible deluge.
"We closed the door thinking that should be sufficient but it wasn't," Eric Im told AFP on Tuesday.
His family's restaurant, Jim Georgie's Donuts, was flooded last week after the heavy rain overwhelmed the city's sewage system. Now they have sand bags ready.
In the city's Marina district, which hugs the coastline near the Golden Gate Bridge, residents were also placing sandbags outside their homes on Tuesday.
"We're hoping for the best, but we're not too worried," one resident, who identified herself only as Heather, told AFP.
In Southern California, forecasters warned that sneaker waves could wash beachgoers out to sea, and surge into parking lots or roadways.
"Always keep an eye on the ocean," the NWS said. "Waves can run up much further than expected, do not assume dry spots are safe."

title: Watch: Man Dressed As Benjamin Franklin Appears In US Court
description: Benjamin Franklin impersonator appears in court facing assault and battery charges.
author: Abhinav Singh
content:
In a comedic turn of events, a Benjamin Franklin impersonator appeared before a Boston court on Tuesday (Nov 23), dressed head to toe in full 'Founding Father' attire. The defendant, 66-year-old Timothy Kingman of Beacon Hill, was arrested on Hanover Street the previous afternoon. Officers took him into custody on two outstanding warrants during a coordinated sweep.
Kingman, who has dressed as Franklin for the last six years and given tours in the city, was committed to his craft when he appeared for the arraignment alongside his lawyer, Nicholas Santiago.
The prosecutors informed the court that Kingman had two active warrants against his name, including an open assault and battery charge for a March 2 fight in the city's Jamaica Plain neighbourhood.
Santiago pleaded his client's case, highlighting that he was dealing with "alcohol issues" at the time of the alleged assault and added that the alleged victim hit a phone out of his hand. Santiago said Kingman had been sober since the alleged altercation, according to a report in CBS News.

He impersonates Mr. Benjamin Franklin...He's passionate about that. It takes guts; he's committed, and he wears the outfit.” Kingman was arraigned while still wearing his colonial garb, pleaded not guilty, and was released on personal recognizance.
