title: Man’s hand chopped off in sickle assault, 2 injured as assailants open fire outside Pune court
description: PUNE: Two people were injured after a group of armed men allegedly opened fire and attacked them with sickles outside the Shivajinagar District Court in
author: Shreedhar Rathi
content:
PUNE: Two people were injured after a group of armed men allegedly opened fire and attacked them with sickles outside the Shivajinagar District Court in Pune on Wednesday afternoon. One of the injured, is in critical condition.
The attack took place around 1pm near Gate No. 4, opposite the Family Court, triggering panic among visitors and litigants gathered in the area.
According to preliminary information, the assailants arrived on two two-wheelers, carrying firearms and sickles. Police said three people were riding one vehicle and four on the other, while eyewitness accounts put the number of attackers at around six.
The group allegedly fired shots before attacking the victims with sickles and fleeing the spot.
One man reportedly suffered a severe injury to his left hand, with his hand allegedly severed at the wrist. He was found unconscious and rushed to hospital. His condition is stated to be critical.
Two firearms and spent cartridges were reportedly recovered from outside the court gate after the attackers fled.
Police and forensic teams launch probe
Police teams rushed to the spot soon after receiving information and cordoned off the area. Senior police officers and forensic experts also reached the scene to collect evidence, including the firearms and cartridges.
The identity of the person who allegedly opened fire and the motive behind the attack are yet to be established. Police are also investigating whether the assault was targeted and what led to the confrontation.

title: Pak astronaut Ali reaches China’s Tiangong station
description: BENGALURU: Pakistan’s first astronaut to travel to space, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, reached China’s Tiangong space station Wednesday, over three hours after
author: Chethan Kumar
content:
BENGALURU: Pakistan’s first astronaut to travel to space, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, reached China’s Tiangong space station Wednesday, over three hours after the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft lifted off at 5.48 am (IST) aboard a Long March-2F rocket.
The docking, confirmed by the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA), marks the first time a foreign astronaut has joined a crewed mission to China’s space station and the first joint crewed flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in its human spaceflight programme.
Shenzhou-24, carrying Ali and Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, separated from the rocket about 10 minutes after launch and entered its designated orbit. CMSA declared the launch a complete success and said the astronauts were in good condition.
The spacecraft subsequently completed its rendezvous and docking with Tiangong, where the incoming joined astronauts who were already aboard the station. The mission is part of China’s regular space-station operations and crew rotation programme.
Ali is serving as a payload specialist and will undertake a short-duration stay. 
Besides participating in routine crew activities, he will work on joint China-Pakistan space science experiments, including the installation of experimental samples and equipment. Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria.
The mission is the outcome of an agreement signed by China and Pakistan in Feb 2025 covering astronaut selection, training and participation in Chinese space-station missions. Following a three-stage selection process, two Pakistani candidates were shortlisted and trained in China. Ali was selected for the flight, with the other candidate retained as backup.
After completing the short-term mission, Ali will return to Earth aboard Shenzhou-23 alongside two members of its crew, Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying.
The Shenzhou-24 mission also has an unusual crew-rotation arrangement. Chinese astronaut Zhu Yangzhu, who is currently aboard Tiangong, will remain in orbit for a year-long stay experiment, becoming China's first astronaut to undertake a year-long orbital mission. The two other Shenzhou-24 astronauts, Tang and Wu, will remain aboard the station for approximately six months.
CMSA said more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests are planned during the mission, covering space life sciences, materials science, microgravity physics, space medicine and new space technologies.
For Pakistan, Ali’s arrival marks its entry into human spaceflight. For China, it is the first operational demonstration of its ambition to open Tiangong to international participation.

title: 'None of us knew about it': Usman Khawaja drops fresh bombshell on Sandpapergate in latest interview
description: Usman Khawaja has doubled down on his account of Sandpapergate, tracing Australia's ball-tampering controversy back to a culture of pushing boundaries
author: Shubhanshu Dwivedi
content:
Usman Khawaja
 has doubled down on his account of Sandpapergate, tracing Australia's ball-tampering controversy back to a culture of pushing boundaries that, according to him, had been building for years before the incident in Cape Town in 2018. While refusing to name individuals, the former Australian batter explained what he meant when he repeatedly said "everyone knew", arguing that the team had collectively benefited from attempts to generate reverse swing.
Speaking on The Grade Cricketer podcast, Khawaja was asked why he was so certain that Australia's bowlers in South Africa were aware of the ball-tampering episode. His latest interview comes amid a divide among those involved in the 2018 infamous incident during Australia's tour of South Africa, with Khawaja, 
Cameron Bancroft
, Chadd Sayers and David Warner maintaining that everybody knew, while 
Pat Cummins
, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have continued to deny prior knowledge.
Khawaja said he could "sleep very easily at night" knowing the allegations in his book were true.
“We can always just talk about the facts in terms of what actually happened at that time. Where I’m at now, I’ve always wanted to take accountability as a team,” he said.
Khawaja says 2021 statement created divide within Australia team
The statement issued by Australia's bowlers in 2021, in which they denied prior knowledge of a foreign substance being taken onto the field during the Cape Town Test, remains a point of disagreement.
Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon had made it clear at the time that they had no involvement in Sandpapergate and have continued to stand by that position.
“The 2021 (statement). They’re pegged to that. It was a very specific statement. I don’t necessarily disagree with the statement,” Khawaja said.
He recalled that when Bancroft had insinuated at the time that everybody knew, he (Khawaja) had spoken to then-coach Justin Langer and wanted the team to take collective responsibility rather than focus on who knew what.
"At the time, Bancroft insinuated that everybody knew. At the time, I was on the phone to JL (Justin Langer) and telling him we should just take it as a team. It was our opportunity to finish it.'
"It wasn't even relevant who knew, who didn't. It was just 'let's take it as a team'.
"And so for me, when I look back at that, the bowlers then went and put the statement out in 2021, and none of us even knew about it. It just happened. They just did it," Khawaja said on The Grade Cricketer podcast.
"It kind of left everyone else with our hands in our pockets. It created this separation. They separated themselves from the rest of the team at that point.
"I talked to Bancroft about this. I was in touch with him all the way from 2018 … He said to me 'that was the loneliest I've ever felt in my life'."
Khawaja said he had recently contacted Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg with a proposal for the entire team from the 2018 South Africa tour to accept collective responsibility for the ball-tampering incident. He also drafted a statement and sent it to Greenberg, sharing it with the podcast.
“We accept as a group we were ball tampering by artificially altering the condition of the ball in South Africa in 2018,” the statement says.
“Furthermore, we would like to acknowledge that Steven (Smith), Cameron (Bancroft) and David (Warner) paid an enormous price for the sake of the team, for which we are sorry and eternally grateful.”
Khawaja said Greenberg's response was that the proposed statement was likely "not going to fly".
'Sandpaper didn't just magically happen': Khawaja traces culture back to 2016
Asked again who knew about ball-tampering in South Africa in 2018, Khawaja took the discussion back to 2016, describing what he believed was a culture driven by a "win at all costs" approach that filtered from Cricket Australia to the coaching staff and then the players.
“From 2016 and that ‘win at all costs’ mentality all the way to 2018. It came from CA up the top. It filtered down to the coaching staff. The coaching staff pushed it onto the players,” Khawaja told The Grade Cricketer.
"And it was a really ugly time in more ways than one because, take away the ball tampering stuff, we were a***holes on the field."
"I see we because we were a team. I don't say anything, I'm a bit of a mute on the field. Fielding sucks most times. I don't really sledge or anything, it's just not part of my personality.
"But when I was a part of this team, we were watching it and it was like 'some of the stuff we're saying is so ugly'.
"It kind of culminated with the Quinton de Kock stuff with Bull (David Warner), the dropping of the ball with Gaz (Nathan Lyon) in front of AB De Villiers' face and the way we were playing, even in the Ashes before, and that was coming from the 'win at all costs, we don't care how you win, just win'.
"When we talk about ball tampering, sandpaper didn't just magically happen. We didn't go from zero to 100.
"It was progressive during that time. We kept pushing the boundaries more and more and more during that two-year period."
Khawaja said the team's approach had continued to push boundaries during that period and that the ball-tampering episode in South Africa was the culmination of a pattern rather than an isolated incident.
"For that two years, 'win at all costs', we just kept pushing and pushing to the point where in Port Elizabeth, obviously Warner was one of the guys who managed the ball, but he had too much heat on him."
"Unfortunately we went down the sandpaper path and people always ask me 'who knew?' and I'm like, we didn't just start (ball tampering) in South Africa. This was going on consistently for a long period of time.
"I don't want to speak on anybody's behalf, but it was going on for a long time. We benefited as a team, we were winning games as a team through our tactics with the ball.
"We win as a team. We lose as a team. We share it as a team. We're doing it to the ball as a team. There's a concerted effort as a team.
“For me, over such a long period of time, we all knew we were trying to reverse swing the ball, and we all know how to reverse swing the ball. That’s the context. You can make up your mind on the rest.”
Khawaja also said Bancroft had sent him a "Thank You" message after learning what was included in his book.
The controversy has put Cummins under pressure since Khawaja alleged that the entire team knew about the plan to alter the ball during the Cape Town Test. Cummins denied being aware of the activity at a press conference last week, but Bancroft subsequently backed Khawaja's account.
A Cricket Australia investigation had held only then-captain Steve Smith, deputy David Warner and Bancroft, who was seend using the sandpaper, responsible. Khawaja reignited the debate through his autobiography, with Warner backing his close friend. Bancroft later claimed "it was the whole team" and said he felt "angry and betrayed" by Cummins.
Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation but has set up a forum for players to share their experiences of the 2018 incident.

title: 'Hum bhi taiyyar hain': Meerut man held for running online ‘jihadi’ groups linked to J&K terror probe
description: Meerut police arrest 22-year-old accused of running encrypted “jihadi” groups to radicalise teens, linked to Jammu terror probe and alleged Army suicide attack plot.
author: TNN
content:
MEERUT: A 22-year-old man was arrested from Meerut’s Kotwali area on Tuesday for allegedly running encrypted social media groups to radicalise teenagers and plotting a suicide attack on an Army camp or convoy.
According to SSP BBGTS Murthy, the accused, Mohd Uzaid, had been absconding for nearly 10 months. Jammu police, assisted by Meerut police, had previously raided his residence on Jan 18 and Feb 21 this year without success.
The arrest stems from an FIR registered on Nov 24, 2025, at Jammu’s Bahu Fort police station under BNS Section 113(3), which deals with terrorist acts. During that investigation, Jammu police arrested Reasi resident 
Mohammad Sajid
, who was allegedly in contact with suspected Pakistan-based handlers and operated groups on Instagram and encrypted messaging platforms.
Police sources said investigators traced four suspicious Instagram accounts, one of which led them to Uzaid in Meerut. During interrogation, Uzaid admitted to regularly watching anti-India content on Instagram and YouTube, including videos of Pakistan-based terrorist 
Masood Azhar
. After he commented “hum bhi taiyyar hain” (We too are ready) under one such video, Sajid allegedly reached out to him.
Police said Uzaid, who had been attending various religious congregations since 2023, forwarded two inflammatory audio clips to teenagers aged over 14 to push them toward “jihad” before deleting the files.
In a press note, police stated that the most serious allegation involves a Nov 2025 plot in which Uzaid and his associates allegedly planned a suicide attack on a major Army camp or convoy. While Sajid was allegedly tasked with conducting reconnaissance, Uzaid was to receive weapons and an explosive jacket, with arms and training allegedly arranged via Gurez Valley.
Investigators said the network later created chat groups named “Tuition-40” and “Brigade” on Instagram and the encrypted Session app—with Uzaid playing a key administrative role—allegedly involving members from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Pakistan’s Punjab province. Police also identified a four-member Instagram group called “Al-Muzzahid” and a WhatsApp group allegedly linked to Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and social media accounts operated by Pakistan-based gangster Shahzad Bhatti.
Police emphasised that the claims and the specific roles of those named are still being verified. “All the allegations are under investigation,” a police note stated. Uzaid remains in custody as further legal proceedings continue, with the Jammu FIR being the only case registered against him so far.

title: In first all-hands meeting after his return to Nvidia as CEO, Jensen Huang again apologised to employees; and said that the meeting he had with his wife was …
description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologised to employees for violating the company’s code of conduct.
author: TOI Tech Desk
content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologised to employees for violating the company’s code of conduct. At his first all-hands meeting since returning as CEO, Huang said personal mistakes had hurt his family and led him to resign. He also told the company’s staff that it was the toughest company meeting he had ever held and the second toughest meeting of his life.
“The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” Huang said, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. He even told employees that he had been going to therapy
“every day for an hour and a half”
 and that it had 
“been helping me a lot.”
 He added, 
“I hurt my family, I hurt my wife.”
What Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees about the code of conduct
Huang said he had written much of Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he said was meant to
“create an environment that’s safe for people.”
 He told employees the company would take violations seriously and weigh the circumstances before deciding how to respond.
“That does not mean the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he said, adding that
“facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would factor into the decision.
Huang also rejected suggestions that his standing in Silicon Valley had earned him special treatment. 
“There are rumours on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,”
 he said.
Jensen Huang says he will seek feedback as often as once a month
Huang acknowledged that his management style had sometimes undermined people who worked with him.
“It disempowers them, and that’s not right,”
 he said.
“I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,”
 Huang said. He told staff he would undergo a 360-degree performance review and could seek feedback from colleagues as often as once a month. He said the review would apply only to him.
Huang also pointed to Nvidia’s flexible work policies as he sought to reassure women at the company. 
“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,”
 he said.
Nvidia’s board is continuing its investigation
Nvidia announced Huang’s return on Monday, after he stepped down following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of having ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia said its board voted unanimously to reinstate him after discussions with Huang and input from senior US government officials.
A committee of independent Nvidia directors is still investigating whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. US lawmakers expect him to testify before Congress next week, the report added.
Huang told employees his brief absence showed Nvidia could keep running without him.
“I promise you, whether I’m here or not, this company is wired up to execute, execute, and execute,”
 he said.

title: ‘A 50-ball 200 is crazy’: Jacob Oram weighs in on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as ODI cricket's 'saviour'
description: NEW DELHI: New Zealand bowling coach Jacob Oram has been left impressed by the extraordinary rise of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but
author: Hijam Raju Singh
content:
NEW DELHI: New Zealand bowling coach 
Jacob Oram
 has been left impressed by the extraordinary rise of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but he has a request for the 15-year-old: save his most destructive innings for someone else.
Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm with his astonishing exploits, most recently smashing a breathtaking 204 off just 53 balls in a List A match on Tuesday. His innings, which accounted for 204 of India A's 254 runs, powered the side to a seven-wicket victory in a chase of 250 in just 14.2 overs, making the contest look more like a video game than a traditional 50-over match.
The knock has also reignited the debate over the relevance of ODI cricket amid the growing popularity of T20s. However, Oram believes it is premature to put the responsibility of saving the format on the shoulders of a teenager.
"It's a bit cool to call a 15-year-old the saviour. Let's see how it pans out. I understand the public love their T20 cricket and the purists love Test cricket, but I still believe there's a place for 50-over cricket," Oram told PTI.
The former New Zealand all-rounder, however, had no reservations about acknowledging the youngster's extraordinary talent.
"He's (Sooryavanshi) exciting, he's entertaining, and the more of those players involved in cricket, the better it is for the product. I just hope he doesn't get a 50-ball double hundred when we have to bowl against him," he said.
'A 50-ball 200 is crazy': Oram marvels at Sooryavanshi
Oram also recalled the teenager's explosive batting against New Zealand in the Wellington T20I, where he scored 45 off just 19 balls.
"He got one score against us, did he not? (45 in 19 balls in the Wellington T20I) and you could see some glimpses of it. I have seen enough of him on TV in the IPL and elsewhere. This guy is amazing, whatever he is, 15 or 16?. Even if he was 25 or 26, like let us say 10 years older, the age is not a factor; it is about how good he is. A 50-ball 200 is crazy, right? You know, and you sort of wonder where you go from there," Oram told ANI.
"I have said, though, I just hope it is not against us, and we have to, every time we play him, we have got to make sure we are on our game or else that sort of stuff could happen because he is a talent," he added.
Sooryavanshi's numbers underline why opposition bowling attacks are already wary of him. In 16 List A appearances, he has accumulated 805 runs at an average of 50.31 and a strike rate of over 193, including two centuries and two half-centuries. He has also smashed 63 sixes in 16 innings.
His exploits in Youth ODIs have been equally remarkable. Representing India Under-19, he has scored 1,412 runs in 25 innings at an average of 56.48 and a strike rate of 165.72, with four centuries and seven fifties. His best score is 175, which came against England in the Under-19 World Cup final earlier this year.
In 10 T20Is for India, the left-hander has already scored 295 runs at a strike rate of over 185, including two half-centuries and a highest score of 81.

title: Egg prices fall as much as 20% in just 8-10 days as bird flu stalls exports from Tamil Nadu, which accounts for over 90% of India’s egg exports; but farmers face 30%-50% higher feed costs
description: Egg prices have plunged in the last few days after a bird flu outbreak in Tamil Nadu has disrupted exports.
author: TOI Business Desk
content:
Egg prices have plunged in the last few days after a 
bird flu
 outbreak in 
Tamil Nadu
 has disrupted exports. Egg prices have crashed anywhere between 10%-20% over the past 8-10 days.
The surplus supplies are being directed into the domestic market at a time when seasonal demand is already losing momentum in southern India.
Farm-gate prices, which had climbed following Chhath Puja, have now begun falling, upsetting poultry farmers who had anticipated better returns during the winter months.
Egg prices crash and demand falls
Consumption demand in southern states has also weakened during the Hindu month of Karthik, adding to the excess supply in the market.
The price drop has come even as production expenses remain high, according to an ET report. Maize and soybean, two key ingredients used in poultry feed, have become 30%-50% more expensive than a year ago, putting further pressure on farmers’ margins.
Poultry feed primarily comprises ingredients such as maize, broken rice, soybean meal and millets. Maize prices have risen by around 50% over the past year, while soybean meal has become approximately 30% more expensive.
Soybean meal is a by-product obtained when soybean seeds are crushed to extract oil. Poultry industry players and farmers had been counting on higher realisations during winter, when egg and chicken consumption typically increases across India.
Egg prices had begun moving upwards across the country after Chhath Puja, reaching a peak of Rs 6.70 per egg in Namakkal, India’s poultry hub, on November 11. However, the upward trend quickly reversed after bird flu was confirmed in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, on November 13. The outbreak prompted containment measures, including the culling of birds and a 90-day prohibition on raising poultry in the affected area.
In Namakkal, egg prices fell to Rs 5.60 apiece, marking a decline of around 19%. The fall has been relatively modest in Delhi, West Bengal, Gujarat and Maharashtra, where prices have dropped by about 6%-10%, while most southern states have recorded declines exceeding 15%.
“Namakkal in Tamil Nadu is India’s egg export hub and accounts for over 90% of the country’s egg exports. The region was exporting about one crore eggs per day last year during the same time, which had reduced to about 15-20 eggs per day just before the outbreak,” Sanjeev Chintawar, chief operating officer, National Egg Coordination Committee told the financial daily.
The seasonal dip in demand has compounded the oversupply in southern India, as consumption of non-vegetarian food is restricted during Karthik, a month in the Indian calendar. “Farmers had reduced production for two months before Diwali to cope with the higher feed costs and planned to increase production in winter hoping to get better realisation,” said Chintawar.
He added, “With feed suppliers refusing to sell feed on credit to the poultry farmers due to supressed prices of eggs and chicken, bird nutrition has been adversely affected either knowingly or unknowingly.”
The price squeeze is also hurting poultry farmers producing chicken. “Farmers are bleeding. The production cost of chicken is over 120/kg, while farmers are getting just about 80/kg,” said KG Anand, general manager, Venkateshwara Hatcheries, the largest fully integrated poultry conglomerate of India.
The wider feed industry is also struggling amid the downturn. “Everyone is making losses. We have no clue how to survive this situation,” said Divya Kumar Gulati, immediate past president, Compound Livestock Feed Manufacturers Association of India, the industry body representing the animal feed industry.

title: Rahul Gandhi assets case: SC quashes Allahabad HC orders seeking CBI, ED inquiry
description: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside Allahabad high court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside Allahabad high court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to examine allegations of disproportionate assets against leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, news agency ANI reported.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant remitted the matter to the Allahabad HC for fresh consideration.The high court had earlier directed the two central agencies to verify the allegations made against Rahul and apprise it of the progress in the matter.
It had also expressed dissatisfaction with the CBI's affidavit and sought a fresh one detailing the status of its inquiry.The petition was filed by Karnataka-based BJP worker S Vignesh Shishir, who alleged that Rahul possessed assets disproportionate to his known sources of income.He had sought a probe against Rahul and other members of his family.According to Bar and Bench, Senior advocate Kapil Sibal appeared for Rahul Gandhi in the matter.Earlier, the Supreme Court had deferred proceedings before the Allahabad HC and restrained the CBI and ED from submitting any report to it.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

title: ‘ICC, boards need to step in’: Harbhajan Singh on India-Pakistan cricket skirmishes
description: MUMBAI: The last couple of India-Pakistan cricket contests, while they've provided plenty of excitement, have also seen ugly scenes of skirmishes between
author: Gaurav Gupta
content:
MUMBAI: The last couple of India-Pakistan cricket contests, while they've provided plenty of excitement, have also seen ugly scenes of skirmishes between the players. On November 14, India's Under-19 players had a go at their Pakistani counterparts, celebrating wildly and overenthusiastically after pipping their arch-rivals by one wicket in a thrilling Under-19 
Asia Cup
 final at Al Amerat in Oman. On November 22 (Sunday) in Doha, players of both India A and Pakistan A (Pakistani Shaheens) exchanged verbal volleys with each other, with India A pacer Harshit Rana involved in heated altercations with the Pakistan players during their Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha, which Pakistan A won by 48 runs.
After the ugly scenes witnessed in the Asia Cup Under-19 final, former India skipper Dilip Vengsarkar had told TOI about the need for the 
BCCI
 to educate young cricketers at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence about behaving well on the field while playing for India at any level. India's off-spin great 
Harbhajan Singh
 has joined the chorus of those voicing their concern at the deteriorating player behaviour during these clashes and has urged the game's authorities — the International Cricket Council and the BCCI — to "step in" to check the trend of players from both countries getting carried away in Indo-Pak cricket matches.
"Somewhere down the line, the ICC needs to step in. I think it is just getting a bit too much with the reactions. First, Pakistan's boys did it (after beating India Under-19s in the league stage). Then the Indians won and did it. And then yesterday too, whatever happened was not right. If you look at sport as a sport, then it will be far better. See, some amount of chit chat happens, and has been happening for a long time. That should happen also.
 The game needs a bit of masala (spice) like that. However, it should not reach a point where you feel it is shameful. So, somewhere down the line, I think that the ICC and the respective boards need to put their foot forward and say, 'this is not done.' 'You try hard on the field to win the match for your team, try your best, but after the match, those reactions, I don't think are the right ones. Both from our side and their side," Harbhajan told reporters at an event at the BPGC Golf Course here on Tuesday.
Asked specifically about Rana's on-field clashes with Pakistan's players, Harbhajan quipped, "I don't think that should happen. I think it is not setting the right example for the generation coming up."
'Have some patience with Team India'
While he wasn't critical of India's bowlers' inability to take New Zealand's eight remaining wickets on the final day of the first Test at Wellington, which ended in a draw on Monday, calling the pitch "really flat," Harbhajan, who took 417 wickets in 103 Tests (1998-2015), wasn't entirely convinced about India's decision to shake hands with their Kiwi counterparts even with 15 overs left to be bowled in the last session of the match, and felt that they could have continued bowling. "I thought the pitch was dry and very flat. It's okay. Pitches in Australia and New Zealand tend to be really flat, at times.
“I think a lot has been talked about in this game. There were 15 overs left and they declared the game (a draw) before. Yes, you could have tried. You never know. Things move very fast in cricket. But somewhere down the line, you have to be honest with yourself, as a captain and management, whether it was the right decision on that pitch or in that scenario. I think that a lot of thought would have gone into that decision. But if I was part of the management, I would have liked to bowl another 15 overs and give it a try. And let's see. You never know,” Harbhajan said.
Recalling how former Australia captain Michael Clarke, with his part-time left-arm spin, had bowled Australia to a win against India in the closing minutes of the controversial Sydney Test in January 2008, taking three for five in 1.5 overs, the former tweaker said, "After everyone else had bowled, Australia introduced Clarke just two overs before (the close of the Test). And nothing was happening. Suddenly he came and he took those two important wickets and they ended up winning that match. So, cricket is a very funny game. Anything can happen."
Citing the fighting attitude of his former India spin-bowling partner and ex-India captain Anil Kumble, Harbhajan said, "I have always been a fan of Anil Bhai. And I still say that his attitude was that you have to fight till the last ball. Whether you are bowling or batting or in the field, you have to fight till the last ball. So 90 balls is a lot. I think we should have tried in those 90 balls (to get the remaining five Kiwi wickets). You never know. Maybe the result will come in your favour."
Harbhajan defended off-spinner Washington Sundar, who took one for 65 in 35 overs as the Kiwis secured a draw in the first Test. "It's very easy for all of us to pinpoint an individual and say he could have done this or he could have done that. I will put myself in his position. He tried his best. He is young. He is learning. And of course, the more he plays, the more he will learn about these situations. Next time, if he is in such a situation, I am sure he will be able to perform better. So, let's not pinpoint an individual. You win with 11, you lose with 11 and you throw with 11. He must have tried. If it was me, I would have tried as well. So, give him some time. I am sure he will learn and he will get better," Harbhajan stressed.
Critics have panned India's inability to close out Test wins in their last two games by taking wickets on the fifth and final day — it happened against Sri Lanka in Colombo in August, and then against New Zealand on the final day of the first Test at Wellington. Harbhajan, though, isn't perturbed and urged fans to "have some patience with the Indian team."
"That will happen (closing out Test wins). This is the same team that won in England (India drew the Test series 2-2 last summer in England). Have some patience with the team. We have a trend here. If you don't get a result that we want from the Indian team, then we go after it. Give them a break. They need to 'breathe out' as well. They are on the road continuously. So, give them some break. I'm sure that they'll get the right results for Team India."
Would it have made a difference if Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammed Siraj had played? "Time will tell. You say, what would have happened if Kapil paaji had played? I can't say much about what would have happened. But if he would have played, we would have talked about it. I can't really predict what would have happened if he would have played. If I would have known, I would have called Gautam and asked him to play," Harbhajan retorted.
Talking about the ongoing 'Sandpaper-gate' controversy rearing its head in Australian cricket again, Harbhajan felt that it "wasn't a new thing" and that it showed that the Australian team sometimes received far more respect than they deserved.
"I don't think this is a new thing. This is a very old thing. Pakistan and India have been talking about this for a long time. That this is a reverse swing.
We are making such a big thing about this. Australia was doing it before. England was doing it. South Africa was doing it. Wherever there is reverse swing, there must be something with the ball. People are doing it. How much they do it naturally, or the way they have done it with sandpaper, that is a little bad. 
Naturally, if you go to make the ball reverse, it takes some time to get the ball going. But if you make the ball reverse in the 10th over, then it is understood that there can be nothing but teasing.

"Australia is not as simple as they used to be. Their players are not as simple as they used to be. I have said this from day one, they should not be given so much respect. They should be given a lot of respect. They have also played the game. They have also done all these things. Now they have been caught or things have come out, they are saying that they did not know. It is not possible that you are living in one house, you are living in another house, you do not know who is living there. Everybody was part of it. I believe. If it is in the team, then it is a collective thing."

title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down after 11 years
description: NEW DELHI: Walmart-owned Flipkart Group on Wednesday announced that CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down from his role and leave the company after more
author: Kanchan Yadav
content:
NEW DELHI: Walmart-owned Flipkart Group on Wednesday announced that CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down from his role and leave the company after more than 11 years, Reuters reported.
Krishnamurthy has led the e-commerce giant through its acquisition by Walmart and years of preparations for a long-awaited initial public offering (IPO).
The company is expected to announce Krishnamurthy's successor in the coming weeks. Balaji Thiagarajan, currently 
Flipkart
's chief product and technology officer, will lead the organisation in the interim, the company said.
Flipkart, one of India's largest e-commerce platforms, has more than 500 million registered users. Walmart said it "remains committed" to Flipkart and its long-term opportunity in India.
Krishnamurthy joined Flipkart in 2016 and was appointed CEO in January 2017. During his tenure, he led several key businesses, including category operations, marketing, customer shopping experience, marketplace, retail advertising and private labels.
Krishnamurthy had also served as the company's interim CFO in 2013 during an earlier association.
Before joining Flipkart, Krishnamurthy served as managing director at Tiger Global Management, where he managed the fund's India portfolio companies.
He was also director of finance for portfolio companies at the investment firm.
He previously worked at eBay Asia Pacific as director of financial planning and analysis and served as country finance director for eBay South Asia in Hong Kong. Earlier in his career, he worked with Procter & Gamble in its supply chain finance business.
Krishnamurthy holds an MBA from the Asian Institute of Management in the Philippines.

title: Telangana HRC takes suo-motu cognizance of three workers’ deaths at Bachupally apartment; seeks detailed report
description: Telangana HRC orders detailed reports after three workers die cleaning a Hyderabad septic tank, directiing inquiry and compensation measures.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The Telangana Human Rights Commission (TGHRC) has taken suo-motu cognizance of the death of three workers who died reportedly after inhaling poisonous gases while cleaning a septic tank at Dinesh Auric Apartments, Bachupally, Hyderabad on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
The Commission, headed by Chairperson Justice Shameem Akthar, took note of the incident based on reports published in several newspapers on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
The news reports cited how the workers lost their lives while carrying out cleaning operations in the septic tank allegedly without adequate safety precautions and protective equipment.
Grave questions about compliance with prescribed safety norms
Expressing concern over the tragic loss of lives, the Commission observed that such incidents raise grave questions about the safety, dignity, and protection of sanitation workers and compliance with prescribed safety norms during hazardous cleaning operations.
The Commission has called for detailed reports from the Secretary to Government, Municipal Administration & Urban Development Department, regarding the circumstances leading to the incident. It has also sought a report from the Medchal–Malkajgiri district administration on the circumstances leading to the deaths, inquiry and coordination by departments, and details of ex-gratia compensation, and other assistance extended or proposed to the bereaved families. The authorities have been directed to submit their reports by December 22, 2026.
Published - November 25, 2026 01:55 pm IST

title: ‘Saam, daam, dand, bhed’: Congress’ swipe at Modi Govt over delimitation issue
description: Congress accuses Modi government of using Kautilya’s methods to push divisive delimitation bills and secure a tainted two-thirds majority.
author: PTI
content:
In a swipe at the Modi government, the Congress on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) alleged that the "self-styled Chanakya" resorted to the last three of the 'saam, daam, dand, bhed' precept of Kautilya to achieve a "super-tainted" two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha but failed.
The four-fold political doctrine was taken from Kautilya's Arthashastra, with 'saam' meaning dialogue, 'daam' referring to financial inducements, 'dand' to punishment or institutional pressure, and 'bhed' to creating division.
"In his desperate search for a super-tainted two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha to get the diabolical delimitation bills passed, the self-styled Chanakya has been resorting to the last three and has failed," Congress general secretary in-charge, communications, Jairam Ramesh, said, and wondered why no chance was given to the first rule of the doctrine.
"The Congress President Mallikarjun Khargeji has written suggesting this precise route to the PM four times in the past seven months — April 11, July 16, Aug 27 and Oct 16 — but there has not even been a routine acknowledgement to these letters," he said.
Mr. Ramesh often takes a dig at Union Home Minister Amit Shah by referring to him as "self-styled Chanakya."
The Congress on Monday (November 23, 2026) claimed that the continued suspense over the Parliament session suggested that either the "PM-HM jodi" is being trapped by its own bluff and bluster or something "truly sinister" is in the works.
The opposition party alleged that either way, the "two GTA (Gyanesh Theft Arrangers)" stars stood brutally exposed and that the institution of Parliament is being diminished greatly by the shenanigans of the "diabolical duo."
The Congress last week said it has been 100 days since the Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die, but Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Minister Shah are still in search of a "supertainted" two-thirds majority in Lok Sabha to get the delimitation bill passed.
Mr. Ramesh then said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and State-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved.
Published - November 25, 2026 02:08 pm IST

title: Keralam CM Satheesan says he too is victim of online attacks, alleges ‘important individual’ behind fake news campaign
description: Kerala CM Satheesan reveals he’s targeted by fake news, pins blame on a central “important individual,” amid calls for quick board appointments.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that he himself was a victim of online attacks, and that an “important individual” was behind the dissemination of such fake news.
At a post-Cabinet press briefing, Mr. Satheesan was responding to questions on the online attacks on Congress party leaders and members of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy’s family.
Mr. Satheesan also displayed copies of social media cards with his photograph which purportedly claim that the government had decided to discontinue the welfare pensions and another attributed to Chandy Oommen that Mr. Satheesan was among the individuals who had caused anguish to his father and Oommen Chandy. “Many such fake news were are being spread in the name of mainstream media organisations,” he said.
“All this comes from one centre, led by an important individual,” he said, but declined to name the person.
On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Mr. Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters.” Such questions should be posed to KPCC president Sunny Joseph, he said.
‘Decision on board, corporation division soon'
Mr. Satheesan said the discussions regarding appointments to the top posts of boards and corporations under the State government were in the final stages.
Mr. Satheesan’s response came amid criticism from within the Congress party and UDF constituents such as the Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) that the appointments were not finalised even after the UDF government had completed six months in power.
Mr. Satheesan said the appointments would be made soon and the talks were in the final stages.
On Monday, after a State secretariat meeting of the RSP, its leader N.K. Premachandran had sharply criticised the delay and also the “absence” of regular meetings of the UDF. The RSP also wanted the appointments to be completed, if possible, this month itself.
On his part, Mr. Satheesan sought to play down the RSP leader’s remarks, saying that it was not criticism as such, and that the party merely wanted the board, corporation division completed quickly.
Published - November 25, 2026 01:58 pm IST

title: Where is the accountability: Kharge slams Modi govt on anaemia report
description: Congress slams Modi govt over anaemia findings, demanding accountability after 12 years amid alarming NFHS-6 and SAMPADA data.
author: PTI
content:
The Congress on Wednesday (November 24, 2026) attacked the Centre over a report on malnutrition and anaemia in the country and asked where is the accountability after 12 years of the Modi government.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge asked how can India realise its demographic dividend when millions of its women and children continue to suffer from malnutrition.
"The Modi Govt's own ICMR-SAMPADA report reveals that 55.9% of women of reproductive age are anaemic. Nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are deficient in Vitamin B12. 42% of children aged 1-4 years are anaemic. In Gujarat, 66% of women of reproductive age and 57% of young children are anaemic," Mr. Kharge said on X.
The Modi government's emphasis on "mild" anaemia cannot obscure the fact that nearly 30% of women of reproductive age suffer from moderate or severe anaemia, the Congress chief said.
The latest NFHS-6 also reveals that nearly one-third of children are underweight and one in five suffers from acute malnutrition, Mr. Kharge said.
"Consider the Government's own financial records. Over Rs 1.13 lakh Cr released under Saksham Anganwadi, POSHAN 2.0 and predecessor schemes in six financial years. Over Rs 2,500 crore gap between funds released and utilised under POSHAN 2.0 in just four years. Nearly 44% of funds released under the original POSHAN Abhiyaan remained unutilised," he pointed out.
Mr. Kharge further said the share of Women and Child Development in the Union Budget has nearly halved — from 0.96% in 2015-16 to 0.50% in 2025-26.
“After 12 years of the Modi government, multiple nutrition schemes, fortified rice and iron supplementation programmes, where is the accountability?" Kharge said.
The Congress on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) cited an official report that showed Gujarat faring poorly in terms of anaemia prevalence in 2023-25, and asked whether Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda would survive the release of this "damning report".
Congress general secretary in-charge of communications, Jairam Ramesh, had pointed out that the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has just put out a report titled "Anaemia and Micronutrient Deficiencies Across the Life Course in India".
In Gujarat, 61.4% of adolescent girls (10-19 years), 63.8% of adult women (20-59 years) and 66.2% of women in reproductive age (15-49 years) were found to be suffering from anaemia during 2023-25, Mr. Ramesh said on X.
"Only Chhattisgarh fared worse. The corresponding figures for the best performing state Kerala were 21.4 per cent, 28 per cent and 29.1 per cent, no doubt high but nowhere near the levels prevailing in Gujarat, which for some years has been propagated as a model state by the prime minister and his cheerleaders," Mr. Ramesh said.
In fact, for children in the age group of 12-59 months, Gujarat had the highest anaemia prevalence (56.5%) while Kerala had the lowest (14.5%), he said.
"Will the genial Union Health Minister survive the release of this damning report?" Mr. Ramesh asked.
Prevalence of anaemia in India is lower than reported in previous national surveys, with severe anaemia accounting for less than 2 per cent of cases across most age groups, according to findings of the Indian Council of Medical Research's SAMPADA survey released on Monday (November 23, 2026).
SAMPADA — or the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry — conducted during 2023-25, covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 states and Union Territories.
More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex and physiological groups.
The findings also showed that most cases of anaemia were mild, indicating an opportunity for early intervention, the Department of Health Research said.
Published - November 25, 2026 01:24 pm IST

title: Calcutta High Court restrains KMC polls until challenge on delimitation decided
description: Calcutta High Court halts KMC elections amid pending delimitation challenge, citing potential gerrymandering and political risk.
author: Shiv Sahay Singh
content:
The Calcutta High Court on Friday (October 6, 2026) restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.
The West Bengal government had passed a legislation in the State Assembly on August 12, redrawing the wards of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) and increasing the number of wards from 144 to 209. Dipu Das, a former councillor of the city’s civic body had challenged the delimitation exercise before the Calcutta High Court.
“Accordingly, MAT No.1917 of 2026 is allowed on contest, thereby modifying the impugned Order dated October 29, 2026 passed in WPA No.31433 of 2026 by restraining the respondent no. 6, that is, the West Bengal State Election Commission, from issuing any notification calling an election to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation on the basis of the amended Schedule II of the KMC Act as notified in the Official Gazette vide Notification No.1728/UDMA-15011(22)/57/2026-LS-MA SEC dated September 11, 2026 till disposal of WPA No.31433 of 2026,” an order by the Division Bench of Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Arjun Ray Mukherjee.
The appeal by the petitioner challenged an October 29 order by Justice Hiranmay Bhattacharyya, who had refused to stay the State government’s delimitation notification proposing amendments to Schedule II of the KMC Act.
The development casts uncertainty over holding of the elections to KMC, something that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government was keen on. In fact, the BJP leadership had started the process of selecting candidates. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has on several occasions, expressed their preference to hold civic body elections in Kolkata and Howrah by the end of November or early December this year.
After the BJP came to power in May 2026, the KMC board, led by former Mayor Firhad Hakim, and the councillors resigned, and the State government appointed administrators to run West Bengal’s largest civic body.
Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya questioned whether the administrator, appointed by the State Government upon dissolution of the corporation, could act as the “Corporation” and issue such a recommendation to reorganise the boards.
Mr. Bhattacharya said that the State Government and its agencies have resorted to gerrymandering in order to secure a partisan advantage for the ruling political party in West Bengal on the premise of previous electoral results, without considering relevant circumstances such as geographical contiguity, compactness and administrative convenience, involving huge expenses from the public exchequer.
Advocate General S.N. Mitra argued that, under Section 601 of the KMC Act, the State Government itself has ample power to add, alter, or modify the Schedules of the KMC Act, irrespective of whether any recommendation is made by the Corporation or not and thus, the appellant’s contentions in that regard were irrelevant.
The Court, however, held the writ petitioner has made out a sufficiently strong prima facie case in the writ petition to be favoured with interim protection in order to save the writ petition from being rendered in-fructuous.
Published - November 07, 2026 08:32 am IST

title: Search intensified for six missing Andhra Pradesh fishermen off Odisha coast
description: Six Andhra Pradesh fishermen remain missing after their boat vanished off Paradip, Odisha; search escalates with Navy, Coast Guard, and state efforts.
author: G.V.R. Subba Rao
content:
Six fishermen from Subbampeta village in Uppada of Kakinada district remain untraced after their fishing boat went missing in the sea off Paradip coast in Odisha. The fishermen ventured into the sea on November 4, 2026.
Even as a search operation has been launched in coordination with the Indian Navy and Coast Guard, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday instructed the official to intensify the efforts.
Also Read: Seven Andhra fishermen safe; search for six missing off Odisha reaches Bangladesh, Myanmar waters
The missing fishermen have been identified as Sorada Kondal Rao, Gumpala Prakash, Tirri Narayana, Sorada Chinna, Merugu Narayana and Kandala Ramu. They set sail into the sea on a boat owned by Garikani Simhadri, along with another fishing boat, towards Paradip in Odisha on November 4. According to information provided by family members, the boats had ventured into waters around 200 km from Paradip, Agriculture and Fisheries Minister K. Atchannaidu said on Tuesday.
He said that the government had been coordinating with the Coast Guard and Indian Navy authorities to trace the missing fishermen. He appealed to the family members not to lose hope.
While one of the two boats returned on November 18, the family members of those on board the missing boat lodged a complaint with the Coast Guard’s toll-free number on November 19. The Fisheries Department wrote to the Coast Guard on the same night, seeking an immediate search operations.
Search operations were subsequently launched in coordination with the Coast Guard units at Kakinada and Paradip and the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Chennai.
The families told the officials that the missing boat had 1,500 litres of diesel and food supplies sufficient for 30 days. At a meeting convened by the Kakinada Coast Guard on Tuesday, officials sought detailed information from the families about the boat’s route and its last known location.
Officials are also examining the possibility of the boat drifting off course due to the impact of the cyclone and being carried towards the maritime waters of other countries. Information has been shared with Bangladesh and Myanmar, the Minister said.
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu also reviewed the steps being taken to trace the missing boat.
Transponder switched off
The fishermen were carrying mobile phones, but they were switched off. The boat's transponder was also switched off, making it difficult to establish its location. Attempts to trace the vessel using GPS have not yielded any results yet, the officials said.
The Indian Coast Guard has deployed ships and a helicopter for the search operation along the coastal stretch near Paradip. Fisheries Department and Coast Guard officials have also met the families of the missing fishermen and apprised them of the situation.
Published - November 25, 2026 12:10 am IST

title: KPCC steps in to quell infighting over ‘A group’ and Oommen Chandy’s political legacy in Keralam
description: KPCC steps in to quell infighting over Oommen Chandy’s legacy amid public sparring and looming Kerala Assembly session.
author: G Anand
content:
The Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) has intervened to quell the infighting over the ‘true heirs’ of late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy’s political legacy.
According to party insiders, KPCC president and Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph has asked All India Congress Committee (AICC) member and Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan not to escalate matters.
Mr Unnithan launched a scathing broadside against Vadakara MP and KPCC working president Shafi Parambil on Tuesday, roiling Congress politics.
Mr Unnithan accused Mr Parambil of seeking to usurp Oommen Chandy’s political mantle. He questioned Mr Parambil’s loyalty to Oommen Chandy during his twilight days, and cast doubt on the MP’s “projected A group credentials”.
Mr Unnithan also sought to link Mr Parambil to expelled Congress leader Rahul Mamkootathil, who is facing multiple charges of rape, and threatened to reveal “salacious details” which, he hinted, could potentially cause reputational damage unless online attacks against him ceased.
A KPCC insider told The Hindu that Mr Unnithan’s public warning presaged further scandal and another season of spiteful ructions, which could provide ammunition for the Opposition and divert political attention from the priorities of voters who gave the United Democratic Front (UDF) government an overwhelming mandate to rule effectively.
“Mr Unnithan had challenged Mr Parambil to an open debate. The KPCC has privately asked both leaders to hold fire and stand down”, he said.
The public sparring has engulfed the Congress at a politically crucial juncture, ahead of the next session of the Kerala Legislative Assembly, which begins on November 30. The row has also inadvertently provided ammunition to the Left Democratic Front (LDF) Opposition to assail the government in the House.
The LDF has signalled that it is primed to put the UDF government on the defensive in the House on various issues, including alleged lack of collective responsibility in the Cabinet, Congress infighting and RSP’s public disagreement with the Congress over what it termed as arbitrary decision-making and lack of consultations in the alliance.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister V D Satheesan refused to comment on the infighting, which made an arguably grim reading for the party and the government on Cabinet day on Wednesday. “The KPCC president has the sole prerogative to comment on organisational matters”, he said.
Mr Satheesan also appeared to wash his hands off the Unnithan-Parambi row. He quoted the late writer and political satirist Manikoth Ramunni Nair, who went by the famous pen name Sanjayan, to signal that he had no role or interest in the acrimonious feud. “I am not from here. I am from Mavilai (a locality in remote Kannur)”.
Nevertheless, the KPCC diktat to the party’s rank and file to avoid public controversy seemed to have little effect on social media, where pro- and anti-Parambil factions continued to spar.
G. Sudhakaran cautions Congress heads
Meanwhile, G Sudhakaran, an Independent legislator from Ambalapuzha in Alappuzha, cautioned Congress leadership from backsliding into infighting reminiscent of the days of fiercely partisan group politics.
“Congress’s infighting matters little to the people, and the UDF could ill afford to lose the public’s trust that the government would deliver on welfare and development promises”, he said in Alappuzha.
Published - November 25, 2026 01:33 pm IST

title: Study finds cost of living way higher than minimum wage in Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru
description: Study finds Bengaluru, Mysuru, and Mangaluru residents earn far less than their cost of living, highlighting a widening income gap.
author: Sharath S. Srivatsa
content:
Amid a pushback on the revision of minimum wages for about 1.8 crore workers employed in over 80 scheduled employments in Karnataka, an effort by an academic forum that has compiled cost of living against the minimum wages shows that earnings of employed residents across Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru are significantly lower than the cost of living.
While the monthly cost of living is calculated to be ₹41,752 in Bengaluru, between 59.9 % and 74.6 % of employed residents are earning less, exposing the stark income gap. The lowest stipulated monthly minimum wage is ₹24,407. Between 5% and 9% employed residents earn less than ₹10,000, says a study by Kolkata-based academic forum ‘Fact or Value’.
Across 37 cities
The study that juxtaposes minimum wages of workers in 37 cities across India, including three from Karnataka, against the cost of living in each city, is set to be discussed on Tuesday during the session on ‘Scientific Calculation of Minimum Wages’ at the 43rd national conference of All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) here by Diven Nagpal, co-founder of ‘Fact or Value’.
In Mangaluru, against the calculated cost of living of ₹32,999, where lowest minimum wage is ₹22,282, 66.7% to 84.8% of employed residents earn less than the cost of living. In Mysuru, where the cost of living is calculated to be ₹31,250, 68.8% to 82.1% of the working population earn less than the cost of living. In Mysuru, the lowest minimum wage is ₹22,282. While 10% to 18.5% of working population in Mangaluru earn less than ₹10,000, the population earning less than ₹10,000 in Mysuru ranges from 14.1% to 24.4%. The large range in data, the researchers say, is becaues of insufficiency of government data.
“Much of the discussion around cost of living and how much is needed to live a basic and dignified life is anecdotal. We arrived at a figure using a methodology historically endorsed by the government, against which people can measure their earnings,” Mr. Nagpal told The Hindu.
The methodology
Figures have been calculated based on the formula developed by 15th Indian Labour Conference in 1957 and provisions laid down by the Supreme Court in the landmark Reptakos Brett and Co. case of 1991.
It has relied on data collected in the 2023-2024 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) to determine which cereals, pulses, vegetables, fruits and other foods are included in each city’s basket, and the Price Monitoring System reported by the Union Department of Consumer Affairs to determine the prices of the food items. The data on labour force has come from the Periodic Labour Force Summary of 2025 and statistics available on the income tax returns has been used too. The income considered of the working individual also includes cash subsidies/financial assistance given by the government, and does not consider subsidies such as foodgrains that are given in kind.
“More worrying than gap between statutory minimum wages and the cost of living is the sheer proportion of workers earning below this benchmark - over 50% in most cities and over 80% in Kolkata, according to our estimates. One can bridge this gap either by raising wages or by better subsidising the basic necessities of food, housing, education, and healthcare,” said Mr. Nagpal, who is also editor at Seagull Books. “Despite decades of economic growth, a large proportion of working population still cannot earn enough to meet the most basic requirements of life. With the rise of automation, there is even less reason to assume that labour will be in demand,” he said.
Karnataka context
In Karnataka, the findings assume significance in the light of revision of minimum wages for the working class hanging fire since 2022-2023. The Labour Department in May 2026 had notified the revision of minimum wages in the range of ₹19,300 to ₹31,100 for unskilled, semi-skilled, and skilled category of workers. The move was bitterly opposed by the trade and industry bodies that fear flight of capital from the State. The government has set up a Cabinet sub-committee under Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara to study and recommend to the future course of action.
AITUC secretary M. Satyanand pointed out that the latest revision in 2026 was done in price data collected in 2023, and prices of essential commodities have increased significantly. “The variable dearness allowance payable once in a year does not compensate even one fourth of inflationary trends.”
Published - November 24, 2026 07:31 pm IST

title: Jharkhand Assembly’s special session starts; Finance Minister moves resolution against SIR
description: Jharkhand Assembly debates halting SIR, with Finance Minister urging immediate stop, SOP reforms, and scrutiny of electoral rolls and mines law.
author: PTI
content:
A two-day special session of the Jharkhand Assembly got underway on Wednesday (Novermber 25, 2026), with state Finance Minister Radha Krishna Kishore moving a resolution against the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, seeking its immediate halt.
During the session, the House will deliberate on the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise and the amended mines law that was passed in Parliament in August.
Jharkhand Assembly to discuss amended mines law, SIR at two-day special session from Nov. 25
Moving the resolution against SIR, Kishore said voters were facing difficulties due to procedural complexities and technical shortcomings in the voter list revision process.
"Of Jharkhand's 2.21 crore voters, 27 per cent were deemed suspicious and sent notices," he said.
Alleging that the Election Commission of India was "working as the Centre's puppet", the minister said that removing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was "necessary to protect the Constitution".
"There is an urgent need to halt the SIR exercise immediately and to issue a fresh standard operating procedure to ensure transparency in the process," Mr. Kishore said.
The Assembly is scheduled to discuss challenges associated with SIR, following which the resolution is expected to be put to vote. Once approved by the House, the resolution will be forwarded to the Centre and other competent authorities, an official said.
Published - November 25, 2026 12:37 pm IST

title: Coimbatore entrepreneur joins Nasdaq Closing Bell ceremony in New York
description: Coimbatore’s iCliniq rings Nasdaq Closing Bell in New York, marking its journey to a global AI-powered health platform.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
iCliniq’s Chief Executive Officer Dhruv Suyamprakasam, who is a member of the Board of Advisors of the Nasdaq Entrepreneurial Center, participated in the Nasdaq Closing Bell ceremony on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) at Times Square in New York. He was joined by other members of the Center in celebration of the National Entrepreneurship Month.
“It was a wonderful experience to be part of this iconic ceremony and a special moment in our journey of building a global healthcare technology company. It was a surreal experience to stand on the same podium where Anthropic co-founders Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei recently rang the bell to mark their IPO,” Mr. Suyamprakasam said in a statement.
iCliniq, which was started in Coimbatore in 2010 and is now headquartered in New York, has evolved into a global health decisions platform with over 80,000 AI-powered healthcare tools.
Mr. Suyamprakasam told The Hindu that the Center is working to bring the benefits of the Startup Intern Match programme to Indian students.

title: 3 killed as car rams trolley on Delhi-Jaipur highway: Police | India News
description: The deceased were identified as Harish Kumar, Devendra Prajapat and Hemant Prajapat, all residents of Mundanwada village. | India News
author: Hansraj
content:
3 killed as car rams trolley on Delhi-Jaipur highway: Police
The deceased were identified as Harish Kumar, Devendra Prajapat and Hemant Prajapat, all residents of Mundanwada village.
Three men were killed and two seriously injured after the vehicle they were travelling in rammed a trolley on the Delhi-Jaipur National Highway (NH-48) late on Tuesday, police said.
The incident took place near Dahmi flyover in Behror area. The deceased were identified as Harish Kumar, Devendra Prajapat and Hemant Prajapat, all residents of Mundanwada village.
According to the police, the five youngsters were returning to their village from Bhagwadi in Behror when their vehicle lost control and crashed into a trolley around 1am. The collision badly mangled the front of the car, trapping all five occupants inside.
“We received information about the accident near the Dahmi flyover around 1am. On reaching the spot, we found a car had collided with a trolley from behind. Three people died on the spot and the other two sustained injuries. The injured were immediately rushed to a hospital, where they are undergoing treatment,” Behror station house officer Ravindra said.
The bodies of the deceased were shifted to the mortuary of Behror hospital for post-mortem.
Police said an investigation was underway to ascertain the exact cause of the accident.

title: Uttar Pradesh government carries out major police reshuffle;10 IPS, 18 PPS officers moved | India News
description: The Lucknow police commissionerate has undergone significant changes, with the state capital getting three new ADCPs. | India News
author: HT Correspondent
content:
Uttar Pradesh government carries out major police reshuffle;10 IPS, 18 PPS officers moved
The Lucknow police commissionerate has undergone significant changes, with the state capital getting three new ADCPs.
The Uttar Pradesh government on Wednesday carried out a major police reshuffle, transferring 28 IPS and Provincial Police Service (PPS) officers, with significant changes in the Lucknow police commissionerate.
Two IPS officers, Punit Dwivedi (2020 batch) and Mavis Tok (2022 batch), have been posted as additional deputy commissioners of police (ADCPs) in Lucknow, while Induprabha Singh, an additional SP-rank Provincial Police Service (PPS) officer, has also been transferred to the state capital as ADCP.
The reshuffle involves 10 IPS officers from the 2020, 2021, and 2022 batches, as well as 18 additional SP-rank officers and PAC commandants.
The reshuffle details
Among the key changes in Lucknow, ADCP Amit Kumawat has been shifted to Ghaziabad. At the same time, Naveen Kumar Singh has been posted as staff officer to the director general of police (DGP) at the police headquarters. ADCP Kiran Yadav has been transferred to the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) as additional SP (operations).
The reshuffle also brought changes in the ADCP-level leadership of other commissionerates. Neetu (2020 batch) has been transferred from Varanasi to Gautam Buddh Nagar, while Shaivya Goyal (2021 batch) has been transferred from Gautam Buddh Nagar to Ghaziabad. Both have been posted as ADCPs. Amit Kumawat will also take up an ADCP assignment in Ghaziabad.
Shiva Singh (2020 batch) has been shifted from Kanpur to Agra as ADCP. Pushkar Verma (2021 batch) moves from Prayagraj commissionerate to Fatehgarh as additional SP, while Aditya (2021 batch) has been transferred from Agra to Budaun as additional SP (rural). In Madurai's Karthigai Deepam row, SC asks parties to file contempt applications, says will pass appropriate orders
The Madurai district collector filed a status report informing the court that the lamp could not be lit at the Deepathoon.
The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused verbal requests to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the Tamil Nadu government over the lighting of a ceremonial lamp atop a temple on the outskirts of Madurai in Tamil Nadu instead of the disputed stone pillar on Tuesday evening. The Madurai district collector filed a status report informing the court that the lamp could not be lit at the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill.
A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi asked the parties to file the necessary applications and said it would pass appropriate orders after examining them. This came after it heard an urgent mention by the original petitioners, Rama Ravikumar and others.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the collector, told the bench: “As the Collector, I have traced out all the steps I was supposed to comply with.”
Deep Dive
Senior Advocate Guru Krishnakumar, appearing for the petitioners who sought the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon, termed the collector’s attempt to place the status report before the court an anticipatory mentioning in response to the breach.
Krishnakumar said the failure to light the ceremonial lamp at the disputed spot was most unfortunate. He alleged a deliberate attempt to circumvent the Supreme Court’s November 20 order. The Supreme Court last week allowed the lighting on the pillar as an interim measure.
Krishnakumar told the bench that a statement was issued in the name of the temple’s Board of Trustees asserting that the lamp should be lit at the Ucchipillaiyar temple, as customary practices did not permit the ceremony at the Deepathoon. He alleged the temple’s sthanikars denied issuing such a statement.
ALSO READ | Madras HC threatens officials of contempt charges over Deepathoon curbs
“Deliberate attempt to non-comply with the order. They have succeeded by stratagems and devices. This is a complete infraction of the rule of law. They kept telling the high court till the last minute that they will comply with the order. They refused to comply,” Krishnakumar said.
He urged the court to direct the authorities to take the flame, which was still burning at the Ucchipillaiyar mandapam, and place it at the Deepathoon as a matter of rule of law.
The district administration maintained it made all arrangements in accordance with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order. It said the temple was asked in writing and reminded to authorise a team to carry out the exercise. The administration said the temple did not authorise any team until the last moment.
Another counsel appearing for the petitioners alleged that the temple’s Board of Trustees was used to circumvent the Supreme Court’s directions and said they would move a contempt petition. The bench expressed its disinclination when the petitioners’ counsel urged it to take suo motu cognisance of the alleged non-compliance.
The Bharatiya Janata Party and Hindu groups protested against the administration and said they would file a contempt petition.
State minister CTR Nirmalkumar said the Karthigai Mahadeepam was lit in the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar temple located directly above the head of the presiding deity at Thiruparankundram.

title: Madhya Pradesh teacher arrested for sending obscene messages to Class 12 student, threatening poor marks | India News
description: Based on the student's complaint, police registered a case against the teacher under relevant provisions of the Pocso Act and took him into custody. | India News
author: Yogendra Lumba
content:
Madhya Pradesh teacher arrested for sending obscene messages to Class 12 student, threatening poor marks
Based on the student's complaint, police registered a case against the teacher under relevant provisions of the Pocso Act and took him into custody.
A government school teacher in Madhya Pradesh's Guna Cantt area has been arrested for allegedly sending obscene and inappropriate messages to a Class 12 student and pressuring her to meet him alone.
According to the complaint, the accused, identified as Narendra Kushwah, had been repeatedly messaging the student for some time, urging her to meet him privately and accompany him outside the school. When she resisted, he allegedly threatened to give her poor marks in examinations and adversely affect her studies.
The student further alleged that the teacher claimed he controlled everything in the school, including examination marks, and insisted that she would have to obey him. She also accused him of pressuring her to sit and talk with him in an area inside the school that had been partitioned with a curtain.
ALSO READ | Rajasthan teacher arrested after refusing to marry 61-year-old Canadian woman he met on dating app
Distressed by the continuous messages and threats, the student informed her mother, following which complaints were submitted to the district education officer (DEO), the school principal and the superintendent of police (SP).
Based on the complaint, police registered a case against the teacher under relevant provisions of the POCSO Act and took him into custody.
ALSO READ | ‘Harassment over fee payment’: Azamgarh Class 8 girl consumes poison, dies, teacher arrested
School principal Sanjay Kumar Jain said the student and her mother approached him with the complaint and submitted copies of the WhatsApp chats. He said the student alleged that the teacher had been communicating with her since after Children’s Day. The matter has been referred to the DEO for investigation.
